Apache-2.0, as is the separate capa-rules repository. v10.0.0 fixes code execution through crafted vivisect .viv workspace files, which affected v9.4.0 and earlier; existing workspaces now load only with CAPA_LOAD_VIV_WORKSPACE=1. A recursive source clone also fetches the test-file submodule, which the installation guide warns contains many malware samples. No samples were analyzed.

name: Ruffle: a Rust reimplementation of Adobe Flash Player
description_en: Reimplements Adobe Flash Player in Rust so that SWF content, from ActionScript 1/2 (AVM1) to ActionScript 3 (AVM2), runs in a native desktop player or in browsers through WebAssembly, as a self-hosted script or a browser extension. Its contributor guide says behavior comes from observing Flash Player's output or from license-compatible sources such as Adobe's open avmplus code, and forbids decompiling Flash Player, Flash Professional or Animate. Regression tests run contributor-made SWFs and compare their trace output, and optionally rendered images, with captures from the official debug Flash Player.
description_zh: 用 Rust 重新实现 Adobe Flash Player，使从 ActionScript 1/2（AVM1）到 ActionScript 3（AVM2）的 SWF 内容能在原生桌面播放器中运行，或通过 WebAssembly 以自托管脚本或浏览器扩展的形式在浏览器中运行。其贡献指南称，行为依据对 Flash Player 输出的观察或 Adobe 开源的 avmplus 等许可兼容来源确定，并禁止反编译 Flash Player、Flash Professional 或 Animate。回归测试运行贡献者自制的 SWF，将其 trace 输出（以及可选的渲染图像）与官方调试版 Flash Player 的记录进行比较。
requirements: The README says Ruffle supports ActionScript 1, 2 and 3 pretty well but is not finished. At review, the website's compatibility page reported 99% of the AVM1 language and 82% of its API, and 90% of the AVM2 language and 82% of its API, and acknowledged graphical inaccuracies in AVM1 content. Release at review: v0.7.1, published 2026-10-07 and described as equivalent to v0.7.0 apart from extension-publishing fixes; nightly builds continue, and the reviewed master commit is 73 commits ahead.

Users supply the SWF files or the pages that embed them. Release assets cover Linux (x86_64, i686 and aarch64), macOS universal and Windows (x86 and x86_64) desktop builds, self-hosted web and browser-extension packages and a reproducible source archive; the README also points to Firefox and Chrome extensions, Flathub, npm and a separate Android project.

Building needs the latest stable Rust (the workspace uses the 2024 edition) and Java on PATH to compile the ActionScript 3 built-in classes; Linux builds need ALSA, udev, fontconfig, FreeType and OpenSSL development packages. Web builds also need the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, Node.js with npm 7+, wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.127 and Binaryen. Bundled scanner and exporter tools bulk-parse SWFs and render PNG screenshots.

Contributors are asked to commit each test SWF with its source, and expected trace output and screenshots come from running the debug Flash Player; known failures can be marked in a test's test.toml. These tests check Ruffle's behavior on authored test files, not equivalence with Flash Player on all content; this review ran none of them.

Dual-licensed MIT or Apache-2.0 (GitHub reports NOASSERTION); LICENSE.md lists third-party dependency licenses, and the repository includes asc.jar from the Flex SDK to compile its ActionScript classes. SWF content keeps its own rights. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: ps3recomp
description_en: Toolkit and runtime for statically recompiling PlayStation 3 games into native executables. Python tools parse PS3 ELF and PRX files, find functions and firmware imports, and lift PPU and SPU code to C/C++; a project template links that code with a C/C++ runtime providing LV2 system calls, high-level emulation of the system libraries and RSX graphics translation to Direct3D 12, Metal or Vulkan.
description_zh: 用于将 PlayStation 3 游戏静态重编译为原生可执行文件的工具包与运行时。Python 工具解析 PS3 ELF 和 PRX 文件，识别函数与固件导入，并将 PPU 和 SPU 代码提升为 C/C++；项目模板再将这些代码与 C/C++ 运行时链接，由运行时提供 LV2 系统调用、系统库的高层仿真，以及转换到 Direct3D 12、Metal 或 Vulkan 的 RSX 图形层。
requirements: The README for v0.15.0 (released 2026-10-16; the reviewed master commit is two commits ahead) reports about 93 complete and 5 partial high-level-emulated system-library modules, with media decoding and SPURS still partial. Only Windows with Direct3D 12 runs a recompiled game from this tree; macOS and Linux build the runtime and pass its tests, but no title has yet booted to gameplay there.

Users supply a decrypted ELF of the game executable (EBOOT.BIN) from their own legally obtained copy; the repository ships no keys, firmware or game files and does not decrypt retail executables. The optional firmware low-level-emulation path also needs decrypted firmware modules that the user provides. Each game is ported in its own project: the README lists The Simpsons Arcade Game and Tornado Outbreak as in game in separate repositories, which this record does not cover.

Building from source needs Python (3.10+ in the README, 3.9+ in the build guides), CMake 3.20+ and a C17/C++20 compiler (MSVC or clang-cl, GCC 12+ or Clang 15+). SDL2 is required off Windows, and FFmpeg is optional and loaded at run time for video and ATRAC3plus decoding. Releases ship prebuilt SDK bundles with the runtime library, headers and Python pipeline for Windows x64, macOS arm64 and Linux x64. Last commit at review: 2026-10-16.

CI builds the runtime and runs the lifter test suites and C unit tests on Windows, macOS arm64 and Linux, plus the Vulkan backend on lavapipe; the README states that a passing check does not mean a game ran. A lifter conformance suite checks the C emitted for single instructions against expectations derived from the PowerISA, and a regression gate compares five ports with recorded milestone logs before shared-runtime changes land.

MIT-licensed; the vendored ATRAC3/ATRAC3plus decoder taken from PPSSPP stays LGPL-2.1-or-later. The README states that the project contains no Sony code, firmware, keys or copyrighted material and that its system-library modules are written from documented behavior, with RPCS3 used as a behavioral reference rather than a code source. This collection did not build or run it, and no game compatibility is implied.

name: Nebula (NebulaFD)
description_en: Work-in-progress decompiler for games made with Clickteam Fusion 2.5, with fixes for older Multimedia Fusion 1.5 files. Its .NET console app reads Windows executables, Android APKs, iOS IPAs, CCN data files and existing MFA projects, then runs plug-in tools: an MFA Parser that writes the game back out as an editable Fusion project, and an Asset Dumper for images, sounds, music, fonts, icons, shaders and packed files.
description_zh: 面向 Clickteam Fusion 2.5 游戏的反编译器，仍在开发中，也针对更早的 Multimedia Fusion 1.5 文件做了修复。其 .NET 控制台程序可读取 Windows 可执行文件、Android APK、iOS IPA、CCN 数据文件以及现有的 MFA 项目，再运行插件式工具：MFA Parser 将游戏重新写成可编辑的 Fusion 项目，Asset Dumper 则导出图像、音效、音乐、字体、图标、着色器和打包文件。
requirements: The README is a placeholder that calls itself a work in progress and documents no usage, build steps or supported formats, so this record relies on the source code and release notes. The latest release, september_2026_update (2026-09-28, the reviewed commit), lists fixes for Multimedia Fusion 1.5 files and Fusion 2.5 build 296 events plus experimental Android support, and notes that console-exporter detection breaks with custom exporters.

Users supply a compiled Fusion game: the console asks for a file path and picks a reader from the extension (EXE, APK, IPA, MFA, ZIP, ANM, TMP or GAM, with other files read as CCN data) or from the user's choice. The MFA Parser and Asset Dumper load as DLLs from the program's Tools folder and write to a Dumps folder.

Release archives require the .NET 6.0 Desktop Runtime, and the projects target net6.0. The only GitHub workflow compiles the solution with MSBuild on Windows and uploads the build as an artifact, and the dumper's post-build step uses the Windows robocopy command; no other platform is documented. The repository contains no test project.

There is no license file and GitHub detects none, so reuse terms are not stated. The README credits Kostya for the image bank. Reviewed sources state no REA use, and this collection did not run the tool or analyze any game.

name: ScooterLink: reconstructing Honda RoadSync’s handlebar-button protocol
description_en: Replaces Honda RoadSync’s Apple Music-only media control with an iOS app that pairs with a Honda PCX 2025 TFT dash over Bluetooth Low Energy and turns handlebar presses into system-wide commands for any player. The author documents the dash’s BLE services, key exchange, button registration and event bytes, reportedly worked out from the official Android app and logged traffic. Results are author-reported on one PCX125, and the protocol notes separate confirmed from unverified parts.
description_zh: 以一个 iOS 应用替代 Honda RoadSync 仅支持 Apple Music 的媒体控制：通过低功耗蓝牙与 Honda PCX 2025 的 TFT 仪表配对，把车把按键转换为对任意播放器生效的系统级命令。作者记录了仪表的 BLE 服务、密钥交换、按键注册与事件字节，据称依据官方 Android 应用及通信日志推断得出。结果为作者在一台 PCX125 上的报告，协议说明区分了已确认与未验证的部分。
requirements: The reviewed commit follows the v1.2 release and changes only one README link. It targets a Honda PCX 2025 with the TFT dash and RoadSync support; README reports testing on a PCX125 2025 and calls other RoadSync models untested. Select and Back map to play/pause and Next/Previous to track changes, and the app reconnects at ignition and switches the dash to phone mode. Now-playing text, speed and volume control are unavailable, and no Android version exists.

No Honda software is needed at runtime, but RoadSync’s phone pairing must first be deleted on the dash, which keeps one phone key. The protocol was reportedly derived from the official RoadSync Android app and logged traffic; source comments cite decompiled Android app version 26.8.10 and a findings file, but the app, decompiled code, captures and that file are not in the repository.

Building needs a Mac with Xcode 16+, XcodeGen and the user’s own signing team and bundle ID; the app targets iOS 17, and the prebuilt v1.2 IPA must be sideloaded with a personal or developer Apple ID. Controlling other apps’ playback relies on Apple’s private MediaRemote framework, which README says rules out App Store distribution.

docs/PROTOCOL.md marks key exchange, per-connection validation, button registration, the phone-screen request and button events as confirmed on a real PCX125 2025, and dash drawing as unverified. A Mac-run Swift self-test checks CRC values, a simulated key exchange, validation parsing and registration and screen byte layouts; this review ran neither the tests nor the app. README reports that experimental colour slots and a drawn screen left the dash refusing phone mode until re-pairing, keeps that code switched off and warns never to write to the firmware-update service.

MIT covers the project code. README says the project is independent of Honda and contains no Honda code or files, only original code and a description of the Bluetooth messages written for interoperability; Honda, PCX and RoadSync remain trademarks of their owners. The author’s post credits Claude with the reverse engineering, but the repository does not document that workflow, and no REA use is established.

name: Frontkick vs Rikugan: a CREBench agent comparison
description_en: Matthieu Breuil’s Synacktiv article explains tool-calling and code-executing agent designs and describes Frontkick, a CodeAct agent that runs generated Python inside Binary Ninja. It compares Frontkick with the open-source Rikugan plugin on two CREBench cryptographic binary tasks, then attributes most of Frontkick’s advantage to a prompt that listed installed Python libraries rather than to its architecture. It is a small evaluation write-up with per-run results, not a released tool or a general benchmark finding.
description_zh: Matthieu Breuil 在 Synacktiv 发表的文章讲解了调用预定义工具与执行生成代码两类智能体设计，并介绍在 Binary Ninja 内运行生成的 Python 代码的 CodeAct 智能体 Frontkick。文章在 CREBench 的两个密码二进制任务上将 Frontkick 与开源插件 Rikugan 对比，随后指出 Frontkick 的优势主要来自提示词中列出已安装 Python 库的做法，而非其架构本身。这是一篇附逐次运行结果的小规模评估文章，不是已发布的工具，也不是普遍性的基准结论。
requirements: The article on Synacktiv’s publications site is dated 13/10/2026. It describes Frontkick as a CodeAct agent that executes generated Python against Binary Ninja’s API, with a recipe-retrieval corpus, a single-level subagent and truncation of older turns; no download, repository or license for Frontkick is linked. Rikugan is an MIT-licensed community agent plugin for IDA Pro and Binary Ninja built on schema-validated tools, while Vector 35’s closed-source Sidekick was excluded because its internals are not accessible.

The comparison used Claude Sonnet 5.5 with CREBench’s AES-128-CBC and ChaCha20 cases in the hardcode_plain/O0 setting, supplied as stripped binaries, with four runs per case for each agent and a 1M-token budget. Each run had to identify the algorithm and key and reimplement decryption to recover the flag. The article does not state the Binary Ninja, Rikugan or Frontkick versions or publish the run transcripts it inspected.

In the published run table Frontkick fully solves six of eight runs and Rikugan none; the means are about 86 versus 31 out of 100 and about 0.60M versus 0.95M tokens, which the article summarizes as roughly half the tokens and nearly three times the score. On AES-128-CBC, Rikugan repeatedly tried a Python crypto package that was not installed and fell back to a manual implementation, whereas Frontkick’s prompt listed the installed libraries. The author therefore calls the outcome a draw driven by prompt design rather than evidence for CodeAct, and proposes a rerun with aligned prompts.

Two tasks, one model and eight runs per agent cannot support general conclusions about either agent, about tool-calling versus code-executing designs, or about other CREBench settings. The separate CREBench paper record covers the benchmark itself; the article reports no REA use and no reconstruction. This collection read the article, Rikugan’s README and the CREBench README without running either agent or the benchmark.

name: OpenDMCUFirm: a reimplemented Wii U DMCU display firmware
description_en: Reimplements in C the firmware of the Wii U’s DMCU, the M68HC11-compatible display microcontroller in its AMD graphics controller, which in Wii mode reads the Video Interface state and configures display output, deinterlacing, scaling and overscan. The README says the work is based on reverse engineering of the original firmware but is not a byte-for-byte matching decompilation, and calls it a work in progress. The built image replaces the stock firmware in Wii mode when loaded through the evWii plugin.
description_zh: 用 C 语言重新实现 Wii U 的 DMCU 固件。DMCU 是其 AMD 图形控制器中兼容 M68HC11 的显示微控制器，在 Wii 模式下读取视频接口（VI）状态，并配置显示输出、去隔行、缩放与过扫描。README 称这项工作基于对原固件的逆向工程，但并非逐字节一致的反编译，并说明项目仍在开发中。构建出的镜像经 evWii 插件载入后，在 Wii 模式下替代原厂固件。
requirements: The reviewed main commit has no releases or tags. The README describes a work-in-progress reimplementation with potential issues expected; recent commits name registers and state fields, and one reports a function fully matched after a missing variable caused problems in 240p titles. link.ld warns that Nintendo’s nn_cmpt writes values into the middle of the DMCU’s ERAM and can overwrite the code.

The build uses only the project’s C sources and needs no original firmware. Running the result needs a Wii U with the Aroma plugin environment and evWii: dmcu.d.hex goes in the SD card’s wiiu folder and is loaded with evWii’s “Load DMCU Firmware from SD Card” option for Wii mode.

The compiler is GCC 3.3.6-m68hc1x-20060122 from the GNU 68HC11/12 packages. The Dockerfile sets it up on Ubuntu 24.04 from the checksum-verified Windows installer run under Wine, and a prebuilt garyodernichts/dmcubuilder image is offered; Python 3 runs hexconv.py to turn the S19 output into the DMCU hex format.

CI only builds dmcu.d.hex in that container and uploads it as an artifact. The reviewed files contain no test suite, hardware test log or comparison with the stock firmware’s behavior, and this review built or ran nothing.

The repository has no license file and GitHub detects none; project source files state only that they are part of OpenDMCUFirm. The bundled 68HC11 and stdint headers keep their FSF GPL and BSD notices, evWii is GPL-2.0, and the original firmware keeps its own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: CoD4 Rewrite: Rust/Bevy reconstruction
description_en: A Rust/Bevy reconstruction of Call of Duty 4 multiplayer systems, using assets from a local game installation. Source covers menus, local bots, movement and combat, and connects custom relay-based netplay to the game.
description_zh: 以 Rust/Bevy 重建《使命召唤4》的多人游戏系统，使用本地游戏安装中的素材。源码包含菜单、本地机器人、移动和战斗，并将自定义中继联机实现接入游戏。
requirements: Requires Windows, a Vulkan-capable GPU and an owned CoD4 patch 1.7 installation. Optional Black Ops, Modern Warfare 2 and World at War content requires their separate installations; game assets are not supplied.

Current source connects the multiplayer dependency and NetplayPlugin despite README statements that networking is pending. Complete online-match behavior and compatibility with original CoD4 servers are not established by this review.
Rendering and gameplay include deliberate extensions, so original-game equivalence is not established. No game, launcher, relay or test was run for this review.
Cargo declares MIT OR Apache-2.0, inherited by the game and multiplayer crates. No standalone license text was found in the reviewed tree.

name: libd2: Diablo II 1.14d engine-core libraries
description_en: Zig libraries reconstructing Diablo II 1.14d seeded maps, item generation, saves, simulation rules and network formats. Selected components expose native and WebAssembly interfaces; verification notes distinguish retail map comparisons from weaker subsystem evidence.
description_zh: 以 Zig 库重建《暗黑破坏神II》1.14d 的种子地图、物品生成、存档、模拟规则和网络格式。部分组件提供原生与 WebAssembly 接口；验证说明区分了原游戏地图对照与其他子系统较弱的证据。
requirements: Builds require Zig 0.16.0. These are modular engine libraries, not a complete playable client; basic generation uses embedded data and fixtures.
MIT covers the Zig source. Included Blizzard-derived binary blobs and map fixtures are expressly excluded from that grant; the repository is not asset-free.

The authors report cell-level comparisons for five Nightmare seeds and two holdouts, plus per-level CRC checks for 200 seeds at three difficulties. This finite corpus does not establish all-seed or whole-engine equivalence.

The game and net packages are checked against recovered rules and packet layouts, not a live server; save, item and pathfinding checks have different depth. No experiments were independently reproduced here.

name: Underworld Exhumed: reconstructing Ultima Underworld I and II
description_en: Pairs reconstructed DOS sources with native ports of Ultima Underworld I and II. The upstream documents Exhume-based byte-matching builds, routine-level comparisons and recorded-session replay against DOS.
description_zh: 将 Ultima Underworld I 与 II 的 DOS 源码重建与原生移植结合。上游记录了基于 Exhume 的字节匹配构建、例程级比较及对照 DOS 的录制会话回放。
requirements: Native ports target macOS, Windows and Linux. Playing and checking against the originals requires your own matching game files (the README targets GOG releases); byte-matching builds additionally require the documented Turbo C++ 1.01 and TASM 2.0 inputs. Native-port compilation itself does not require game data.

The MIT license covers the project’s own tools, documentation and added annotations/structure. NOTICE explicitly excludes rights in the original games and derived game code; optional MT-32 playback requires separately obtained ROMs.

Recorded sessions and routine tests provide bounded upstream evidence, not an independent whole-game equivalence result. Full tests require licensed inputs absent from the public repository. This review did not build, run or compare the games; no REA integration is established.

name: LineWars II: a portable SDL3 reconstruction
description_en: Provides an SDL3 backend for a portable-C reconstruction of the 1994 DOS game. Its build configuration links the reconstructed engine to video, input and audio adapters; the upstream documents differential gates against original machine code.
description_zh: 为 1994 年 DOS 游戏的可移植 C 重建提供 SDL3 后端。构建配置将重建引擎接到视频、输入与音频适配层，上游记录了对照原始机器码的差分测试关卡。
requirements: Builds target Windows and Linux using C99, CMake 3.16+ and SDL3; the reviewed build notes specify SDL 3.4.12 built with the same compiler as the game. This is a port of the separate LineWarsII-DOS reconstruction, not a claim to original source ownership.

The reconstructed/ported source uses PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. NOTICE reports original-author Patrick Aalto’s July 16, 2026 permission for freeware distribution of the original game material; it does not grant commercial-use permission. SDL keeps its separate zlib license.

The upstream reports renderer and menu comparisons and captured PCM levels within about 10% of its DOS reference; higher-resolution rendering changes the presentation. No game binaries or assets were downloaded, and no port, emulator or verification suite was run here; no REA integration is established.

name: BFM-decomp: Brave Fencer Musashi matching decompilation
description_en: Documents an agent-assisted reconstruction of the USA PlayStation game with a pinned compiler and whole-binary SHA-1 gates. The verification recipe covers the main executable, resident engine and disc-loaded code modules, with explicit library and assembly exceptions.
description_zh: 记录美版 PlayStation 游戏的智能体辅助重建，使用固定编译器及完整二进制 SHA-1 检查。验证规约覆盖主程序、常驻引擎及光盘加载代码模块，并明确列出库与汇编例外。
requirements: Requires an owned USA SLUS-00726 disc dump, Linux/WSL2, Python 3.12 and the documented pinned GCC 2.7.2/MIPS toolchain. Optional PsyQ SDK objects must be supplied separately; no disc, SDK or compiler package was downloaded in this review.

AGPL-3.0 applies to the project’s tools and documentation. src/NOTICE.md asserts no license over the reconstructed game code, whose original rights belong to Square/Square Enix; third-party components retain their own licenses.

The 218-binary matching contract is an upstream claim backed by its recipe and a recorded full run dated September 7, 2026. That log is for an earlier tree, not this reviewed HEAD. SDK/assembly exceptions and unfinished readability remain documented; public no-ROM CI audits and compiles but cannot perform the original-byte comparison. Nothing was built or run here; no REA integration is established.

name: Logic-Lens
description_en: Experimental JavaScript source-analysis toolkit that classifies AST-token sequences into configured formula families after local training, and produces heuristic structure, call-graph and intent reports. It supports code-comprehension experiments; its predictions do not establish arbitrary program invariants or semantic equivalence.
description_zh: 实验性 JavaScript 源码分析工具：本地训练后将 AST token 序列归入预设公式类别，并生成启发式结构、调用图和意图报告。它可用于代码理解实验，但预测结果不证明任意程序的不变量或语义等价。
requirements: The README documents Node.js 18 or newer. Package version 1.1.0 declares TensorFlow.js, its native Node binding and Acorn; the setup first tries the native TensorFlow binding and then falls back to the pure JavaScript CPU backend.

Formula prediction requires local synthetic-data generation and training. The predictor expects model weights and metadata that are absent from the reviewed repository tree; no pretrained model or successful local setup was established by this review.

Predictions select from a configured formula catalogue. The README’s accuracy/confidence examples are author-reported and do not establish correctness on arbitrary unseen functions; heuristic intent and quality reports are not behavioral-equivalence proofs.

Standalone semantic-test definitions cover structure, heuristic patterns and report shape. CONTRIBUTING mentions npm test, but package.json has no test script. No tests, training or inference were executed for this source review.
README and package metadata declare MIT, but the reviewed commit has no LICENSE file. Keep that distinction when assessing reuse.

name: Android Security Toolkit
description_en: Local Python APK triage tool that drives apktool and strings, checks manifest settings and source/native-library strings, and produces TXT/JSON findings for manual review. Its rules flag possible issues without proving exploitability or reconstructing application behavior.
description_zh: 本地 Python APK 初步分析工具，调用 apktool 与 strings 检查清单配置、源码及原生库字符串，输出 TXT／JSON 结果供人工核验。规则仅提示潜在问题，不证明可利用性，也不重建应用行为。
requirements: Python 3 standard-library imports, separately installed apktool and strings/binutils, and an authorized local APK are required. Manifest analysis depends on successful apktool decoding.

String and manifest-rule matches require manual verification. A symbol, permission or flag alone does not establish an exploitable execution path. The README distinguishes this initial static pass from manual code review, dynamic/native analysis and library CVE matching.

The reviewed two-file tree contains no automated tests or versioned validation corpus. README sample output is an author-provided illustration, not an independently reproduced result. No APK was scanned for this review.
The README states MIT, but the reviewed tree contains no standalone license file.

name: Littlebird.ai static home-page rebuild
description_en: Rebuilds the Littlebird.ai home page in plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript from captured markup and assets, with source-wired mobile navigation, FAQ toggles, scroll reveals and OS-dependent call-to-action presentation. It illustrates a bounded website reconstruction, with uncaptured routes and product functionality left outside the scope.
description_zh: 依据捕获的标记与资源，用原生 HTML/CSS/JavaScript 重建 Littlebird.ai 首页；源码实现移动导航、FAQ 展开、滚动显现及随操作系统变化的按钮展示。它是范围明确的网页重建案例，不涵盖未捕获路由或产品本身的功能。
requirements: The captured scope is the home page and five embedded demos. Pricing, blog and other uncaptured routes are absent; several download controls are placeholder links. This is not a recreation of the Littlebird desktop/mobile application or its backend.
The shipped site is plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript without a build step. The documented local preview and asset-integrity suite use Node.js 20+ and its standard library.

The original npm test passed all five checks on the pinned inputs. These check local asset references, basic file and embedded-page completeness, and independence from the ignored capture directory; they do not establish visual similarity, accessibility conformance, interaction correctness or equivalence to the original site.

The MIT file covers repository code. The README explicitly excludes captured third-party fonts, imagery, markup and copy from that grant and identifies this as an unofficial study rebuild. For the later integrity check, pinned site files were kept in a private test snapshot without rendering; historical recon data was not fetched.

name: ilspy-cli: targeted .NET decompilation for agents
description_en: Rust CLI that hosts an ILSpy C# bridge in-process for assembly, type and named-method decompilation, source search and structured JSON output. A separate PE-header detector identifies managed assemblies without loading the .NET runtime.
description_zh: 通过进程内托管的 ILSpy C# 桥接层，提供程序集、类型和指定方法的反编译、源码搜索及结构化 JSON 输出的 Rust CLI；独立的 PE 头检测器无需加载 .NET 运行时即可识别托管程序集。
requirements: Building requires a Rust toolchain and .NET 8 SDK; build.rs invokes dotnet publish for the C# bridge, whose project pins ICSharpCode.Decompiler 9.1.0.7988. Decompilation needs the .NET 8 runtime; the detect command follows a separate Rust-only path.

Method selection matches the first method with the requested name within the named type; it does not disambiguate overloads by signature. Source search skips types whose decompilation throws, so an empty result is not proof that the requested pattern is absent from the complete assembly.

The integration suite builds one small SampleLib fixture and checks command output, including a simple Add method. Its source and cross-platform CI definition were inspected, but no build, .NET hosting, fixture execution or decompilation was run during this review; general accuracy and behavioral equivalence are not established.

README and Cargo metadata declare GPL-3.0, but the complete pinned tree has no separate LICENSE/COPYING text. The upstream ILSpy engine and user-provided assemblies retain their own licensing conditions.

name: swe1r-assets-unity: Racer model-block editor sample
description_en: Work-in-progress Unity editor sample for importing and modifying Star Wars Episode I: Racer model blocks, then serializing them back through swe1r-assets. Its editor includes an unmodified import/export byte-comparison command; it is an asset-format workflow rather than a reimplementation of the game.
description_zh: 尚在开发中的 Unity 编辑器样例，可导入和修改《星球大战：极速飞车》的模型块，再通过 swe1r-assets 序列化回原格式。编辑器提供未修改导入／导出结果的字节比较命令；其范围是资产格式工作流，而非完整游戏重实现。
requirements: The README explicitly says this is currently a sample project. The package and sample pin Unity 2022.3.30f1; packages.config references SWE1R.Assets.Blocks 0.0.1-alpha.15 and ByteSerialization 0.0.1-alpha.9. Required game block files are read from a user-selected local game-data directory.

Model import/export is wired in the editor and importer/exporter classes. Texture, spline and sprite sections currently expose filenames without equivalent operation controls; spline importer/exporter subclasses are empty. Do not present the sample as complete support for every asset kind.

Test Re-Export compares the original and serialized model-item byte arrays with SequenceEqual, and Test Re-Export All loops over the loaded model block. The README claims bit-perfect unchanged round trips, but the reviewed tree contains no saved corpus/result report establishing that across game versions or arbitrary edits. No Unity project or game asset was run or loaded in this review.

Repository code has an MIT LICENSE and source SPDX headers. That code license is not evidence of permission to redistribute the original game data; no game blocks, screenshots, textures or other binary assets were downloaded for this review.

name: React-Decode
description_en: Static-analysis CLI for compiled React JavaScript that produces readable bundle output and inferred API-request, route and application-constant reports. It can extract embedded source-map contents when available.
description_zh: 面向已构建 React JavaScript 的静态分析 CLI，可输出更易读的代码，以及推断的 API 请求、路由和应用常量报告；存在 source map 内嵌源码时可将其提取。
requirements: The reviewed package declares Node.js >=20, but its locked Babel 8 dependencies require ^22.18.0 or >=24.11.0. The lock pins Babel parser/traverse 8.0.7, generator/types 8.0.6 and Prettier 3.9.10; runtime compatibility was not tested.
Provide authorized JavaScript bundles, HTML, source maps or a URL. URL mode retrieves scripts, chunks and maps; source extraction requires strings in sourcesContent, not just mapping coordinates.

API and value inference is bounded and heuristic: wrapper discovery uses at most six rounds, dynamic values can remain placeholders, and inferred request/response fields are not a verified API specification. Control-flow flattening and string-array obfuscation are outside the documented scope; complete original-source or application/backend behavior recovery is not established.

The MIT LICENSE and package.json agree, but package.json declares 0.1.0 while the root lock metadata says 1.0.0 and ISC. These are inspected package declarations, not a verified published release; input bundles retain their own rights.

Reports may contain credential-like strings from the input; --json prints them unmasked. The five synthetic node:test definitions were read, not run. No dependency installation, tool execution or target execution was performed.

name: WasmLens: exploratory WebAssembly inspection
description_en: Python CLI with static paths for inspecting WebAssembly sections and function signatures, producing WAT-style instruction listings, and reconstructing limited C-like pseudocode. These are exploratory analysis aids for supported modules, not recovered original source or a complete WebAssembly runtime.
description_zh: 提供 WebAssembly 区段与函数签名检查、WAT 风格指令列表和有限 C 风格伪代码重建的 Python CLI。所收录的是面向受支持模块的探索性静态分析路径，不代表恢复原始源码或实现完整 WebAssembly 运行时。
requirements: The reviewed package declares version 0.1.0 and Python >=3.10, with Typer, Rich, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, NetworkX and python-multipart dependencies; pytest/httpx are development extras. The source includes an MIT LICENSE. Dependency lower bounds are declared, but no lockfile or tested environment was established.

The info, disasm and decompile commands read a supplied .wasm file through the same parser. That parser has no 0xFD SIMD decoding branch and may label unsupported opcodes as unknown; the README’s broad WebAssembly 2.0 coverage claim is not established by this review.

The WAT-style module listing is not a lossless reassembly format: data segments are reduced to previews of up to 32 bytes and active offsets use a placeholder. The C-like reconstructor has no general fallback for unhandled instructions, uses only the first result type, and expresses branch labels in comments; compiler-ready or behavior-equivalent output is not established.

The separate emulator is outside this entry’s supported scope. Its inspected dispatch lacks handlers for operations including floating-point arithmetic and indirect calls, and an unhandled instruction can advance the program counter without implementing its effect. Do not use it as a full-runtime or equivalence reference.

Parser and decompiler test definitions were inspected; sample-based string assertions do not establish general correctness. No package installation, bundled .wasm download, execution, decompilation or test run was performed, and the README’s test-count/coverage badges were not independently reproduced. Supply only modules you are permitted to analyze.

name: Awesome Decomp Games
description_en: A generated, rated index of public game reconstruction projects: decompilations, disassemblies, static recompilations, source ports, engine remakes and browser ports. A daily job merges several upstream lists and registries with GitHub and decomp.dev metadata, drops dead links and rebuilds the README and website from data files. Useful for discovery; its scores are automated heuristics, not reviews.
description_zh: 自动生成并附评分的公开游戏重建项目索引，涵盖反编译、反汇编、静态重编译、源码移植、引擎重制及浏览器移植。每日任务合并多个上游目录与登记站点，结合 GitHub 和 decomp.dev 元数据，剔除失效链接，再由数据文件重建 README 和网站。适合用来发现项目；其评分是自动启发式结果，并非人工审阅。
requirements: The reviewed README, generated 2026-10-16, reports 2,118 projects covering 1,829 games, with sections for 646 decompilations, 520 static recompilations, 230 source ports, 206 engine remakes, 107 disassemblies, 53 browser ports, tools, mods and 347 inactive entries. These are the list's own counts, not verified projects.

Each entry's 1–5 playability, completeness, activity and popularity sub-scores are computed by scripts/build.py from GitHub metadata, decomp.dev progress and description keywords. Projects their source list flags as AI-generated are marked ⚠️ and lose 0.2. A score or section is not a matching, completeness or runtime check; follow each project's own sources.

Entries are seeded from the listed upstream collections and registries plus data/additions.json and data/overrides.json. A scheduled GitHub Actions job runs daily at 03:17 UTC to refresh metadata, check links and browser-play URLs, and commit the regenerated files, so summaries can still lag the linked projects.

The list states that it hosts no ROMs, ISOs, BIOS files or game assets, and its contribution rules refuse links to them and repositories that ship game data; most listed projects need files from the user's own copy. Some browser entries are labeled as playing instantly without the user's files. The list does not document each site's rights basis, and this catalog did not review those sites.

The list and data are released under CC0 1.0 and the scripts and website code under MIT; linked projects and game screenshots keep their own rights. Two REA showcase repositories appear among the entries, but the list establishes no REA affiliation.

name: Snowboard Kids: an agent-assisted N64 matching decompilation
description_en: A matching decompilation of the original Nintendo 64 Snowboard Kids that rebuilds SHA1-identical North American and Japanese ROMs from a user-supplied ROM. The author’s 84-day post-mortem describes coding agents run through his Nigel harness alongside m2c, the permuter and a shared file of compiler learnings, and declines to credit LLMs alone for the speed-up. It is a separate project from the Snowboard Kids 2 decompilation.
description_zh: 原版 Nintendo 64 游戏 Snowboard Kids 的匹配反编译，利用使用者自备的 ROM 重新构建 SHA1 一致的北美版与日版 ROM。作者在 84 天复盘文章中介绍了通过自建的 Nigel 工具调度编程智能体，并结合 m2c、permuter 与共享编译器经验文件的流程，同时表示不应把提速完全归功于大模型。它与 Snowboard Kids 2 反编译是不同的项目。
requirements: The 2026-08-26 post reports the game 100% decompiled: every function has C that compiles to identical machine code, apart from a small amount of handwritten system-library assembly that was original source. It dates the repository from 28 May 2026 to the final matching function on 19 August 2026 and counts 2,145 functions, against 596 days and 2,995 functions for Snowboard Kids 2. The README says the Japanese version currently builds from extracted assembly; reports/jp-exact-functions.md lists 120 JP functions compiled from C.

Building requires the user’s own North American or Japanese ROM, named snowboardkids.z64 or snowboardkids.jp.z64 with the SHA1 listed in the README; the build extracts assembly and assets from it into git-ignored directories. The README says the repository contains no game assets or assembly, although the reviewed tree tracks libultra .s files and a box-art image. CI builds both regions from a baserom checked out of a separate private repository.

The verified host is x86-64 Linux with make, git, Python 3, clang, wget, tar and binutils-mips-linux-gnu; a macOS setup is documented but still needs validation. make -C tools sets up the recompiled IDO 5.3 toolchain (IDO_DIR can point to another), submodules supply asm-processor, asm-differ and decomp-permuter, and optional matching helpers need requirements.txt.

tools/build-and-verify.sh cleans, extracts, builds and checks the output ROM’s SHA1 against the original for the selected region, and reports/region-functions.md aligns 1,293 of 2,110 US functions with the JP ROM by exact or address-normalized matches. The post describes agents writing C function by function, a script running m2c on every unmatched function, permuter runs with deadlines and four parallel worktrees; it calls its comparison of GPT-5.5/5.6, Claude 4.5, Fable and GLM 5.2 unscientific. This catalog did not build or verify any ROM.

The author estimates that roughly 4.8% of matching commits involved expert intervention, says the figure does not measure effort, credits contributors for many difficult IDO matches and calls attributing the whole speed-up to LLMs a gross oversimplification. A 100% match still leaves generated names, unknown structure fields and data to document. No license file is present at the reviewed commit, the README states commercial use is a non-goal, and no REA use is stated.

name: reflecticon-224: running Lexicon 224 reverb firmware on emulated hardware
description_en: Emulates the Lexicon 224, 224X and 224XL digital reverbs so that their own firmware runs in a browser page or a JUCE plugin. The repository layers KiCad schematics, gate-level and board-level Verilog models, an 8080-hosted C++ emulator and analog input/output models, and checks faster layers against slower ones using user-supplied ROMs. It is a work-in-progress hardware-and-firmware emulation whose documentation is still pending, not recovered algorithm source.
description_zh: 模拟 Lexicon 224、224X 与 224XL 数字混响器，使其原厂固件能在浏览器页面或 JUCE 插件中运行。仓库分层包含 KiCad 原理图、门级与板级 Verilog 模型、以 8080 为主机的 C++ 模拟器及模拟输入／输出模型，并用使用者自备的 ROM 以较慢层级校验较快层级。这是仍在开发、文档尚未完成的硬件与固件模拟，并非恢复出的算法源码。
requirements: The reviewed pin is from 2026-10-13; the repository was created on 2026-09-28. README calls it a work in progress whose documentation will follow, so the Makefile is the main map: it links the schematics, gate-, board- and ISA-level models, the C++ emulator, analog models, the WebAssembly page and the plugin. Recognized firmware sets include several 224 versions, 224X v8.1 and 224XL v8.1A and v8.21.

Users supply their own Lexicon ROM chip files, which README says stay on their computer. The page and plugin recognize known sets by SHA-256, and the repository lists those hashes, not ROM bytes. Firmware checks read a LEXICON_FIRMWARE folder with one subfolder per set and skip when it is absent. The web demo does ship program-name and slider-value catalogs keyed to specific firmware sets.

make check runs the firmware-free checks, and any target whose tool is missing, such as Verilator 5 or KiCad’s command-line tool, reports itself as skipped. The page builds with Emscripten 5.0.1 for GitHub Pages. The plugin builds with CMake and JUCE 8.0.14 as macOS AU, VST3 and standalone targets, and CI validates the AU with auval; the tagged v0.1.0-alpha.1 prerelease is an ad-hoc signed macOS 11+ build that contains no firmware.

make check-firmware runs the user’s ROMs through several layers, including service-manual signature tables at gate level. Qualification compares the emulator’s CPU state, control-store writes and DAC captures with board-level runs, and qualified.json stores expected hashes for two scenarios. A byte-exact gate compares the WebAssembly build bit for bit with the native reference. These project checks need the ROMs; this collection ran none of them.

GitHub detects no repository license, so no reuse terms beyond viewing are granted; the included 8080 cores carry zlib and MIT notices. README disclaims affiliation with Lexicon or its owners, and the original firmware remains theirs. In the Hacker News thread for a related report, a commenter who identifies the repository as theirs describes paid schematic tracing and LLM agents turning schematics into Verilog; no REA use is stated.

name: Sonic Advance 3: an AI-assisted match of one enemy module
description_en: Macabeus’s dated study describes prompting Claude Sonnet 3.5 and DeepSeek R1 with assembly, similar decompiled functions and structs to write matching C for Marun, one enemy module of the community Sonic Advance 3 GBA decompilation. The resulting pull request replaced that module’s assembly and was merged; the author calls the setting unusually AI-friendly, and the project now bars LLM-origin contributions.
description_zh: Macabeus 在注明日期的研究文章中，介绍了如何把汇编、相似的已反编译函数和结构体放进提示词，让 Claude Sonnet 3.5 与 DeepSeek R1 为社区 Sonic Advance 3 GBA 反编译项目中的敌人模块 Marun 编写匹配的 C 代码。由此产生的拉取请求替换了该模块的汇编并已合并；作者认为这一场景对 AI 格外友好，而该项目现已不接受源自大模型的贡献。
requirements: The post, dated 20 May 2025 and subtitled an ongoing study, covers a single module: Marun, an enemy in the community Sonic Advance 3 GBA matching decompilation. Work began on 6 January 2025, and pull request #4, which replaced the module’s 1,154-line assembly file with 494 lines of C, was merged on 31 January; the post equates it to 0.3% of the project’s total progress. It is a bounded contribution study, not a whole-game decompilation.

Building the SA3 decompilation requires the user’s own European Sonic Advance 3 ROM, named baserom_sa3.gba and matching the release the README identifies by SHA1, plus a sufficiently recent agbcc compiler fork. The study itself worked in decomp.me scratches, putting assembly, similar decompiled functions and relevant structs into prompts for Claude Sonnet 3.5 and DeepSeek R1.

Match percentages come from decomp.me: the post reports a 96% first Sonnet 3.5 attempt that later prompts could not reproduce, a 74% DeepSeek R1 result raised to 100% by replacing memset with CpuFill16, and R1 output that usually matched at least about 60%. The merged pull request is the project-level outcome; the post reports no separate build or test, and this catalog ran nothing.

The author calls the setting very AI-friendly because similar modules were already decompiled for use as examples and the GBA compiler is simpler and more predictable; generated C lacked project-specific macros and needed readability work. The author’s decomp.me AI-panel pull request was closed unmerged; the post says user benefit was unclear and it required a paid API key.

At the reviewed SA3 commit, the README states a strict no-LLM/no-AI policy for issues and pull requests, so that project no longer accepts this workflow. The SA3 repository has no license file at that commit, the ROM and its assets retain their own rights, and no REA use is stated.

name: iX500 Scan: a macOS client for the reverse-engineered ScanSnap Wi-Fi protocol
description_en: Replaces ScanSnap Home for a Fujitsu/PFU ScanSnap iX500 on macOS with a SwiftUI app and Python service that scan over Wi-Fi through the community-reverse-engineered VENS protocol, or over USB through SANE, and produce searchable PDFs. It vendors bramheerink’s GPL-2.0 driver, extends it for macOS, and documents further handshake and hardware-status fields, including the scan-button bit. Results are author-reported; the repository publishes no tests or captures.
description_zh: 在 macOS 上以 SwiftUI 应用和 Python 后台服务替代 ScanSnap Home，为富士通／PFU ScanSnap iX500 提供扫描：Wi-Fi 经由社区逆向的 VENS 协议，USB 经由 SANE，输出可搜索的 PDF。项目内置 bramheerink 的 GPL-2.0 驱动并为 macOS 做了扩展，还记录了更多握手字段和硬件状态字段，包括扫描键状态位。结果均为作者报告，仓库未公开测试或抓包记录。
requirements: Reviewed commit 24a5f7c (three commits, all dated 2026-10-15) targets the Fujitsu/PFU ScanSnap iX500. README says ScanSnap Home 3.7 is no longer maintained and hangs on macOS 27; the project offers Wi-Fi scanning started by the device’s scan button, a USB path through SANE, and searchable PDFs with rotation, cropping, blank-page removal and OCR. No release build is published, and other ScanSnap models are not claimed.

The Wi-Fi path needs the user’s own iX500 and two values that README says only ScanSnap Home knows: the scanner’s 12-character pairing key and the paired computer’s 8-byte HostID. They are obtained once from ScanSnap Home’s own connection to that scanner; the repository includes no vendor software, firmware or captures.

Building needs macOS 14+, Xcode 15+ (Swift tools 5.10), the system Python 3 with Pillow, and Homebrew sane-backends, ocrmypdf, img2pdf and tesseract-lang. build.sh bundles the Python service and vendored driver into an ad-hoc-signed app that runs the service with /usr/bin/python3.

The protocol work extends bramheerink/scansnap, whose VENS specification says it was reverse-engineered from captures of ScanSnap Home talking to an iX500. README adds handshake fields for the paired HostID, local time and UTC offset, hardware-status bits for an empty feeder and the scan button, and a session timeout of about 40 s, and notes that Wi-Fi images always arrive as 300 dpi colour, rotated 180° with scanner background. No automated tests, captures or comparisons with ScanSnap Home output are published; this review ran neither the app nor a scanner.

GPL-2.0, matching the vendored driver at commit 5706688, whose file header records the author’s changes. This is an unofficial client, not recovered vendor source or firmware. The repository’s draft social posts credit an evening with Claude Code for closing the remaining protocol gaps; no REA use is stated.

name: Roborock Local Server: a self-hosted stand-in for Roborock’s vacuum cloud
description_en: Runs a local HTTPS and MQTT stack in place of Roborock’s cloud, so supported vacuums keep live maps and controls on an isolated network without rooting or hardware changes. The maintainer’s technical write-up recounts earlier app and traffic analysis and a later investigation in which Claude Code and Codex worked against an emulated firmware environment. Compatibility is reported per model by the project and its users.
description_zh: 运行一套本地 HTTPS 与 MQTT 服务来替代 Roborock 云端，使受支持的扫地机在隔离网络中无需 root 或改装硬件即可保留实时地图与控制。维护者的技术说明回顾了早期的应用与流量分析，以及后来借助 Claude Code 和 Codex、在模拟固件环境中开展的调查。兼容性由项目及其用户按型号报告。
requirements: Reviewed version 1.2.1 (commit c3b3284) targets most Roborock vacuums on the v2 protocol; README excludes the entry-level Q series, and the tested-models page lists confirmed models, unresolved failures and certificate-chain notes. Documented limitations include firmware updates and schedules; camera streaming is verified on two models, and China-market devices reject commands outside China.

Setup needs a domain the user controls with local DNS rewriting, a valid TLS certificate, a LAN host for Docker Compose or the Home Assistant add-on, and a second Wi-Fi computer for one-time onboarding. The official Roborock app works only after an interception login step and, on Android, a patched APK; Home Assistant and the open-source LocalRock app are alternatives.

Python 3.11–3.13 with FastAPI, aiohttp, cryptography and python-roborock 4.20.0; a container image is published, and CI runs the pytest suite before building it. Tests cover onboarding, protocol authentication, MQTT proxying, certificates and scenes; this review ran neither the tests nor a vacuum.

The write-up says long-running Claude Code (Opus 4.6) and Codex sessions, given the maintainer’s own rooted S7, its firmware, python-roborock and the decompiled app, helped find the remaining onboarding step after earlier manual attempts stalled. It credits Dennis Giese’s firmware research, Valetudo and other community work; no REA use is stated.
MIT license with an as-is disclaimer; the project is not affiliated with Roborock. It is a compatible server, not recovered Roborock server code, and vendor firmware or app changes may break it.

name: WristBeam: reconstructing Garmin’s watch protocol for a Mac companion
description_en: Implements a Garmin watch companion as a native macOS menu-bar app that pairs over Bluetooth, receives live health notifications and original FIT files, and can upload them to Garmin Connect. Source comments attribute its GFDI framing, handshake, file-transfer and status fields to analysis of a supplied Garmin Android package, cross-checked against community implementations such as Gadgetbridge. Device verification covers one watch model, and the opt-in MCP and HTTP interfaces expose only locally cached data.
description_zh: 以原生 macOS 菜单栏应用实现佳明手表的配套客户端：通过蓝牙配对，接收实时健康通知和原始 FIT 文件，并可上传至 Garmin Connect。源码注释称，GFDI 分帧、握手、文件传输和状态字段依据对一个自备佳明 Android 安装包的分析实现，并与 Gadgetbridge 等社区实现相互核对。设备验证仅涵盖一款手表；可选启用的 MCP 与 HTTP 接口只提供本地缓存的数据。
requirements: Reviewed at VERSION 0.3.7 plus unreleased changes. It needs macOS 13+, a Garmin watch prepared with heart-rate broadcast off, and, for cloud features, a Garmin China or Global account signed in through Garmin’s own page; a local mode pauses all Garmin cloud access. Application-level encryption, native MLR/CoreTransfer and desktop widgets are unsupported, and a sleeping Mac cannot sync.

Protocol source comments describe an independent Swift implementation of GFDI framing (COBS, CRC-16), multilink registration, device information, file directories and transfers, battery status and account-identity fields, each tied to named classes of a supplied Garmin Android package. Gadgetbridge, garmin-bridge and garmin-ble are cited as corroborating wire observations that were consulted, not ported. The reviewed tree contains no APK or decompiled listing; cloud history uses Connect client endpoints that the developer guide says are not a published Garmin API contract.

Building needs macOS 13+, Swift 5.9+ and Command Line Tools; native swift test and CodeQL analysis need full Xcode, which CI supplies. CONTRIBUTING lists lint, localization, secret-scan, release-pipeline and core regression scripts. Release packages are ad hoc signed and not Apple notarized.

The device matrix marks pairing, fresh notifications, original FIT download, China upload and daily charts verified only for an Instinct 2 Solar on 2026-10-13, with firmware unrecorded. Other Instinct, fēnix, epix, Forerunner, Venu and vívoactive models and real Global uploads remain unverified. VERIFICATION.md records regression counts run through Command Line Tools rather than full XCTest; this review read the sources and did not run the app or a watch.

MIT covers the project, which says it is not affiliated with Garmin; Garmin services, the Android package, watch firmware and health data keep their own terms. MCP, the HTTP/HTTPS API and webhooks are off until enabled. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA attribution for building the app.

name: abc-decompiler
description_en: Decompiler for HarmonyOS Ark bytecode (.abc), the format HarmonyOS app packages carry in modules.abc, built by adapting the jadx decompiler and reading files through a patched copy of the abcde library. Because much of Ark bytecode is semantically close to DEX, it reuses jadx's GUI, IR and passes: an .abc file dropped into the jadx-based window is shown as decompiled code. The README reports that all 227 usable instructions of the 282 Ark opcodes are implemented, most special instructions as pseudo-functions.
description_zh: 面向鸿蒙方舟字节码（.abc）的反编译工具；HarmonyOS 应用包中的 modules.abc 即为此格式。它通过改造 jadx 反编译器实现，并借助打过补丁的 abcde 库读取文件。由于方舟字节码有很大一部分与 DEX 字节码语义相近，它沿用了 jadx 的图形界面、中间表示和处理流程：把 .abc 文件拖入基于 jadx 的窗口即可查看反编译代码。README 称 282 条方舟字节码中可用的 227 条指令均已实现，其中大部分特殊指令以伪函数形式实现。
requirements: The README describes the project as still in development: decompilation passes for more readable output, a custom IR and data-flow analysis are listed as unfinished. The only release, h1, published 2024-12-20, ships a single jadx-dev-all.jar built from the reviewed master commit, and the repository has had no pushes since.

Building needs JDK 17+; the patched abcde fork must first be published to the local Maven repository and its version substituted into the Gradle files before ./gradlew dist. Input is the modules.abc file from the user's own HarmonyOS HAP package.

The repository is a modified jadx code base: jadx's DEX input, test samples and inherited CI files remain, and it has no GitHub Actions workflow of its own, so no tests of Ark bytecode output are reported.
Apache-2.0, as inherited from jadx; the abcde fork is also Apache-2.0. No files were decompiled.

name: pypush: a Python client for Apple’s push protocol
description_en: Reimplements the client side of Apple’s private Apple Push Notification service (APNs) protocol in platform-independent Python: it activates as an Apple device, connects to the APNs courier, mints app-scoped tokens and receives push notifications. The project began as the author’s proof of concept for iMessage reverse engineering, but the current rewrite has removed IDS and iMessage support for now. It uses Apple’s services outside Apple’s official clients.
description_zh: 以与平台无关的 Python 重新实现 Apple 私有推送通知服务（APNs）协议的客户端：它以 Apple 设备身份完成激活，连接 APNs courier 服务器，生成限定于应用的令牌并接收推送通知。项目最初是作者 iMessage 逆向研究的概念验证，但当前重写版暂时移除了 IDS 和 iMessage 支持。它在 Apple 官方客户端之外使用 Apple 的服务。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-03-15 main head, identical to release v2.0.2 on PyPI. The README warns that the rewrite is unstable, that many features have been temporarily removed and that stability should not be expected before 3.0.0. The IDS, iMessage, GrandSlam and CloudKit packages are empty placeholders, so the earlier iMessage work is not part of this version.

Activation and connections go to Apple’s live activation and APNs servers through what the project calls Apple’s internal API, outside Apple’s official clients; the README notes that some APIs may need device identifiers. Apple’s terms for these services apply separately. This record names no accounts, identifiers or credentials, and the certificate file in the test assets is deliberately not linked.

Requires Python 3.9+ with anyio, httpx (HTTP/2) and cryptography; the cli extra adds Frida, Rich and Typer. The CLI listens for notifications on a topic, and its proxy mode, meant for observing a Mac’s own APNs traffic, attaches Frida to the local apsd daemon and requires System Integrity Protection disabled and root.

Pull-request CI runs Ruff and pytest on Python 3.9–3.12 across Linux, macOS and Windows. The tests activate against Apple’s servers, open an APNs connection and round-trip a sandbox notification through a scoped token, so they depend on live services rather than offline protocol fixtures. This source review ran no tests, activation or connections.

LICENSE is the Server Side Public License v1, and the package metadata classifies it as Other/Proprietary; the README says Beeper purchased the project and directs licensing questions to Beeper. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: LuaJIT Decompiler v2
description_en: Decompiles LuaJIT bytecode files back into Lua source, written as a replacement for the older Python LuaJIT decompiler. The README reports full support for gotos and for stripped bytecode, including reconstructed locals and upvalues, and its boolean-expression recovery follows a published decompilation algorithm. It processes single files or whole folders and writes .lua output.
description_zh: 将 LuaJIT 字节码文件反编译回 Lua 源码，作为旧版 Python LuaJIT 反编译器的替代品编写。README 称它完整支持 goto 和去除调试信息的字节码，包括还原局部变量和上值；其布尔表达式恢复基于一篇已发表的反编译算法论文。它可处理单个文件或整个文件夹，输出 .lua 文件。
requirements: Users supply LuaJIT bytecode files or a folder containing them, by drag and drop or on the command line; decompiled .lua files go to an output folder beside the executable unless overridden. Options filter by extension, ignore debug info, skip files that fail instead of showing an assertion pop-up, and format output to minimize diffs.

The reader accepts bytecode format versions 1 and 2 and rejects big-endian bytecode, which the README lists as future work along with better decompilation of conditional assignments. The repository has no tests, CI or published accuracy results; the program reports how many files failed to decompile.

Windows only: the README directs users to a release executable (the Mar_24_2024 release, whose notes say it was rebuilt on 2026-05-14), and main.h lists Visual Studio, C++20, the Windows API and an unsigned default char as build requirements, with no project or build files included. A Call-of-Duty branch, four commits ahead of master, has its own release executable. Last commit at review: 2026-05-14.
MIT license text that also carries the LuaJIT and Lua copyright notices; GitHub does not classify it. Reviewed sources state no REA use, and this collection did not run the decompiler.

name: FLARE Learning Hub
description_en: Free English reverse-engineering and malware-analysis modules from Mandiant's FLARE team, published as Google Docs, with lab binaries, IDA databases and scripts kept in this repository. The Malware Analysis Crash Course builds from x86 basics to reading Windows API use through assembly-patching exercises and labs with worked solutions; the other modules introduce WinDbg Time Travel Debugging for malware triage and provide a reference to how Go 1.24 programs look in Windows executables.
description_zh: Mandiant FLARE 团队发布的免费英文逆向工程与恶意软件分析课程模块，正文以 Google Docs 形式发布，实验用二进制文件、IDA 数据库和脚本存放在本仓库中。其中的恶意软件分析速成课从 x86 基础讲到解读 Windows API 调用，穿插汇编修改练习和附详细解答的实验；其余模块介绍如何用 WinDbg 时间旅行调试（Time Travel Debugging）分诊恶意软件，并提供一份说明 Go 1.24 程序在 Windows 可执行文件中呈现方式的参考手册。
requirements: At reviewed commit ebd4e3a (2026-03-31), the repository, first committed on 2026-03-19, holds three modules: Malware Analysis Crash Course (nine chapters, five labs, hacking exercises and flash quizzes), An Introduction to Time Travel Debugging (a demo, one triage lab and a JavaScript automation reference) and The Go Reverse Engineering Reference. Module text lives in web-published Google Docs that change outside the repository. The README promises refinements and new modules, but no commits followed 31 March by the review date.

The crash course is the entry point: it assumes Windows command-line use, Boolean logic, two's complement, basic programming and networking. The TTD module assumes basic x86 Windows reversing and WinDbg. The Go reference assumes x86 reversing and Go, and is restricted to Windows AMD64 executables built with Go 1.24.0.

The README says all modules support only Intel x86-64 environments and strongly recommends an isolated, snapshot-capable FLARE-VM virtual machine. The crash course uses IDA and FakeNet, and its exercises ship with IDA database files; the TTD module uses WinDbg, which includes TTD, and ttd.exe. Lab and demo binaries, databases and scripts are FLARE-made and come as password-protected archives. The README warns that some behave like malware and may be flagged, so they belong only in that VM; one TTD demo trace is a separate Google Drive download.

The repository is Apache-2.0; the Google Docs reviewed carry no separate license statement. The project does not accept contributions and takes errata by email. This collection read the README, module directory notes and the three published documents; it did not run the labs, and nothing in the material mentions AI or REA.

name: pw: a matching decompilation of the Pokéwalker firmware
description_en: Reconstructs as C the firmware of the Pokéwalker, the pedometer accessory for Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, for its Renesas H8/38606 microcontroller. With artwork from the user’s retail firmware image and a supported Renesas compiler suite, the README reports a byte-identical rebuild of the 48 KiB image; without that image, original placeholder art gives a non-matching reference build. The author describes disassembling and decompiling the retail binary, the HeartGold/SoulSilver ROMs and the candidate compilers, alongside published hardware research.
description_zh: 以 C 语言重建 Pokéwalker 的固件。Pokéwalker 是《宝可梦 心金／魂银》配套的计步器配件，采用 Renesas H8/38606 微控制器。README 报告，使用从使用者自备的零售固件镜像中取得的美术素材及受支持的 Renesas 编译器套件，可重新构建出逐字节相同的 48 KiB 镜像；没有该镜像时，项目原创的占位美术只能生成不一致的参考构建。作者称其结合已公开的硬件研究，对零售二进制文件、心金／魂银 ROM 及候选编译器进行了反汇编和反编译。
requirements: The reviewed main branch is a single initial-release commit of 2026-09-14 with no tags or releases. The README calls the matching reconstruction complete for one image, 49,152 bytes with SHA-256 f9e210a3…d15607, and assumes it is the only Pokéwalker firmware. The source keeps 40 C90 modules whose file names encode the observed link order, and changes must preserve matching.

Users supply a lawfully obtained Pokéwalker firmware image, used only for artwork, and the Renesas H8, H8S, H8SX family C compiler package; neither is distributed, and the README withholds acquisition instructions. Only suites 6.02.01 and 6.02.02 are reported to reproduce the image. Missing artwork falls back to the bundled placeholders, which normally changes the output hash.

Builds are reported on macOS Arm64, where the 32-bit Windows compiler runs through Wibo and Rosetta, and natively on Windows x86_64; other hosts are unverified. uv supplies Python 3.11+ (3.12 by default), Ninja and Pillow from uv.lock, configure.py generates build.ninja, and macOS configuration downloads and validates the recorded Wibo release.

ninja verify requires the retail size and SHA-256 and writes verified.json; the build guide asks for that check under both compiler suites and records per-module input and output hashes to catch stale objects. Host unit tests cover the build utilities, a development check adds clang-format, Ruff and Cppcheck, and there is no CI workflow. Matching is author-reported; this review built or ran nothing.

Original project material is dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, and the placeholder artwork carries its own CC0 notice; retail firmware and extracted artwork keep their rights. include/startup/iodefine.h is a retained Renesas HEW device header outside the CC0 dedication with no license grant, and the compiler-archive reader credits MIT-licensed ISx and Unshield. The project states no affiliation with Nintendo, The Pokémon Company, GAME FREAK or Renesas; the reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: slicer
description_en: Browser-based Java reverse-engineering tool that loads class files and JAR/ZIP archives and disassembles or decompiles them with Vineflower (the default), CFR, Procyon or JASM, compiled to run in the browser, next to its own bytecode disassembler. It draws inheritance and interface graphs and per-method control-flow graphs, searches constant-pool entries, instructions and member declarations or usages, applies Tiny, SRG/TSRG/CSRG or ProGuard mappings, and offers generic transformers that strip or normalize bytecode attributes so decompilers cope better with obfuscation. A JavaScript scripting API can add disassemblers and manipulate the workspace; the README itself recommends Recaf for serious reverse engineering.
description_zh: 基于浏览器的 Java 逆向工程工具：可加载 class 文件和 JAR/ZIP 归档，使用编译为可在浏览器中运行的 Vineflower（默认）、CFR、Procyon 或 JASM 进行反汇编或反编译，另有自带的字节码反汇编器。它能绘制继承与接口实现关系图以及单个方法的控制流图，搜索常量池条目、指令以及成员声明或使用位置，可应用 Tiny、SRG/TSRG/CSRG 或 ProGuard 映射，还提供剥离或规范化字节码属性的通用转换器，帮助反编译器更好地应对混淆。JavaScript 脚本 API 可添加反汇编器并操作工作区；README 自己也建议，若要进行严肃的逆向工程，应使用 Recaf。
requirements: Runs as the hosted web app at slicer.run and can be installed as a PWA. The repository has no releases or tags, so this entry pins the reviewed main commit (2026-09-19); local builds are a Vite and Svelte app built with pnpm, and the repository has no CI workflow. The documentation says slicer is in active development and that features may be missing.

The documentation states that no data is sent to any server and that decompilers run locally in the browser; JDK library classes are fetched on demand from data.slicer.run, and URL parameters can load a JAR, mapping file or script from another site. Input is class files or JAR/ZIP archives from software the user may analyze; HPROF heap dumps and Android binary XML can also be viewed.

The documentation warns that decompiled output is a best-effort approximation that may not be valid Java, especially for code from non-javac compilers or obfuscators. slicer has no obfuscator-specific deobfuscation, and its remapper does not propagate names through inheritance.
MIT license for slicer; bundled components such as the Vineflower and Procyon decompilers are Apache-2.0. No classes were decompiled.

name: SteamKit
description_en: .NET library that implements the client side of Valve’s Steam network protocol: connection-manager sessions, authentication, friends, unified service and Game Coordinator messages, Web API calls and CDN depot downloads. Message classes are generated from Steam protobufs tracked in a submodule and from the project’s own SteamLanguage definitions. Its Resources tree adds protocol-research tools: NetHook2, a Windows DLL that hooks a running Steam client to dump the network messages it exchanges, NetHookAnalyzer2 for viewing those dumps, and ProtobufDumper for recovering protobuf definitions from executables.
description_zh: 实现 Valve Steam 网络协议客户端的 .NET 库，涵盖连接管理服务器会话、身份验证、好友、统一服务消息与 Game Coordinator 消息、Web API 调用以及 CDN depot 下载。消息类由子模块跟踪的 Steam protobuf 和项目自有的 SteamLanguage 定义生成。其 Resources 目录还提供协议研究工具：NetHook2 是挂钩正在运行的 Steam 客户端、转储其收发网络消息的 Windows DLL，NetHookAnalyzer2 用于查看这些转储，ProtobufDumper 则从可执行文件中恢复 protobuf 定义。
requirements: The reviewed master head is identical to GitHub release 3.5.0 of 2026-10-19; at review NuGet still listed 3.4.0 as the newest SteamKit2 package. The README requires the .NET 10 runtime to use the library and the .NET 10 SDK to build it, although the library project multi-targets net8.0 and net10.0. Documentation consists of XML API docs, the wiki and numbered samples covering login, QR authentication, web cookies, friends, Web API and a Dota Game Coordinator request.

Authenticated features need the user’s own Steam account; this record names none. The library follows Valve’s undocumented, changing protocol: a weekly workflow regenerates message classes from the SteamTracking protobuf submodule and opens a pull request, and the NetHook2 readme notes that releases can lag behind Steam changes.

NetHook2 is a Windows-only C++ DLL built with Visual Studio 2022 and vcpkg that needs the x86 Visual C++ redistributable. Its readme says it depends on binary signature scans of the Steam client that updates can break, and that Steam may crash while it is attached. NetHookAnalyzer2 is a Windows GUI; CI publishes both as workflow artifacts. They inspect the user’s own client traffic, and this record gives no usage steps.

CI builds the library, SteamLanguage parser, protobuf tools and samples on Windows, macOS and Linux (x64 and ARM) and runs the xUnit v3 test project, whose fixtures include recorded packets and small depot manifest and chunk samples. The tests check parsing, crypto helpers, async jobs and depot handling, not equivalence with Valve’s client; this source review ran none of them.

LGPL-2.1 (LICENSE). The tracked Steam protobuf definitions come from a separate submodule, and Valve’s services and terms apply independently of the library license. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: Nintendo Switch Reverse Engineering
description_en: Notes begun by dekuNukem in 2017 and extended by contributors on how the Joy-Con, Pro Controller and parts of the Switch console and dock work, worked out from teardowns, logic-analyzer captures and packet logs. Markdown files cover the Joy-Con board test points and rail-connector pinout, the wired serial handshake with its CRC-8 checksum, Bluetooth HID input and output reports with 32 documented subcommands, the USB HID commands of the Pro Controller and charging grip, the SPI flash memory map with stick and 6-axis calibration, IMU conversion formulas and rumble encoding tables. The repository also keeps STM32 test firmware that plays the console or a Joy-Con on the rail, a Wireshark dissector for the Bluetooth traffic, and the captures behind the notes.
description_zh: 由 dekuNukem 于 2017 年发起、众多贡献者陆续补充的笔记，记录 Joy-Con、Pro 手柄以及 Switch 主机与底座部分硬件的工作方式，依据来自拆机、逻辑分析仪抓取和数据包记录。各 Markdown 文件涵盖 Joy-Con 电路板测试点与滑轨接口引脚定义、带 CRC-8 校验的有线串口握手、蓝牙 HID 输入与输出报告及其中记录的 32 个子命令、Pro 手柄与充电握把的 USB HID 命令、含摇杆与六轴校准数据的 SPI 闪存布局、IMU 换算公式以及振动编码表。仓库还保存了在滑轨接口上扮演主机或 Joy-Con 的 STM32 测试固件、用于解析蓝牙流量的 Wireshark 解析器，以及笔记所依据的抓取数据。
requirements: Reviewed at commit b354f21 (2026-08-21). Of 277 commits, 228 date from 2017 and most others from 2018–2021; the 2026 changes document the console's sanity checks on stick calibration. The notes describe the original Joy-Con and Pro Controller, listing controller firmware 3.89 as the latest, and several fields remain marked unknown, so newer firmware and controllers need separate checking.

Following the notes needs one's own controller. The wired-protocol work involves opening a Joy-Con and connecting its rail connector, which uses 1.8 V logic, to a logic analyzer or microcontroller; the Bluetooth and USB notes assume a host that can exchange raw HID reports, and their sample C code uses hidapi-style calls. No controller or dock firmware is included: the README says a dock firmware dump was made but is not posted.

The joycon_reader and joycon_spoofer projects target an STM32F072 and were generated with STM32CubeMX for Keil MDK-ARM; their build outputs are committed alongside the sources. The nxbt dissector has to be compiled as a plugin within a Wireshark source build, a Lua script dissects Bluetooth traffic captured over USB, and small Python scripts parse captures and compute the serial checksum. The .logicdata captures need logic-analyzer software that reads that format.

The Bluetooth notes also document SPI flash write and sector-erase and firmware-update commands, with warnings about erasing whole sectors; the field meanings come from the contributors' own captures and tests, which this collection did not repeat.

GitHub detects no license and the repository has no license file, so the notes state no reuse terms; a datasheets folder holds copies of third-party chip datasheets, and the Lua dissector says it is provided with no license. The README credits the many contributors. Nothing in the reviewed files mentions AI or REA.

name: Android App Reverse Engineering 101
description_en: Maddie Stone's free English workshop introducing static reverse engineering of Android apps, published as GitHub Pages. Its chapters cover app components and entry points, Dalvik bytecode and smali, decompiling DEX with jadx, finding and reading JNI native libraries in Ghidra, and string deobfuscation. Seven exercises with written solutions apply this to triaging malware samples and spotting command-execution flaws in pre-installed apps.
description_zh: Maddie Stone 编写的免费英文工作坊，以 GitHub Pages 发布，入门讲解 Android 应用的静态逆向工程。各章涵盖应用组件与入口点、Dalvik 字节码与 smali、用 jadx 反编译 DEX、在 Ghidra 中定位并阅读 JNI 原生库，以及字符串去混淆。七个附书面解答的练习将这些方法用于分诊恶意软件样本，以及找出预装应用中的命令执行缺陷。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 17f9eeb, the last default-branch commit (2020-04-29); most pages date from 2019 and the material is not being extended. The introduction says the workshop covers static analysis only and does not teach app development, malware analysis or vulnerability hunting themselves; the conclusion points to Frida and dynamic analysis as next steps.

Exercises are designed for the author's Ubuntu 18.04 64-bit VM image, offered for VirtualBox and VMware from Google Drive, with jadx and Ghidra installed. The exercise APKs (apps triaged as possible malware and two pre-installed vendor apps, each named with a SHA-256 digest in most exercises) exist only inside that VM; the repository holds Markdown pages and images and no APKs.

The native-library chapter assumes some ARM assembly, pointing to outside tutorials, and says every exercise library also has an x86 build. The pages were last updated in 2020, so their screenshots may not match current jadx and Ghidra releases.

The repository has no license file, so reuse terms for the text are not stated; the pages credit the Android robot logo to Google under CC BY 3.0. This collection read the pages at the reviewed commit and did not download the VM or repeat the exercises; the workshop mentions no AI or REA use.

name: wii-ipl: a decompilation of the Wii Menu (System Menu 4.3)
description_en: A work-in-progress decompilation of the Wii Menu, the console’s System Menu (IPL), targeting version 4.3 in its USA, European, Japanese and Korean builds. It recovers the menu’s own code together with the Revolution SDK, NintendoWare (NW4R), EGG and middleware libraries linked into it, matched unit by unit against the original executable with decomp-toolkit and objdiff. The repository holds no assets or assembly; a build needs the user’s own Wii Menu WAD and yields only main.dol.
description_zh: Wii Menu（即主机的 System Menu，IPL）的反编译重建，仍在进行中，针对 4.3 版的美、欧、日、韩四个版本。项目重建菜单自身的代码，以及链接进其中的 Revolution SDK、NintendoWare（NW4R）、EGG 和中间件库，并借助 decomp-toolkit 与 objdiff 逐个编译单元与原可执行文件比对。仓库不含任何素材或汇编；构建需要使用者自己的 Wii Menu WAD，且只生成 main.dol。
requirements: The reviewed main commit has no releases or tags. decomp.dev’s report for that commit puts 4.3U at 58.5% matched code, 8,837 of 12,563 functions (70.3%) and 45.2% fully linked code, with the menu’s own code at 53.6% matched; library READMEs mark each RVL_SDK, NW4R, EGG, RevoEX and middleware component as matching, equivalent or not yet matching. The build yields main.dol, not a WAD, and the README warns that the code is not fully shiftable because no SEL file is generated.

Users supply their own Wii Menu 4.3 WAD for the selected version (4.3U by default, or 4.3E, 4.3J or 4.3K); the README states that the repository contains no assets or assembly of the executable. Each version’s configuration pins the SHA-1 of the target main.dol.

Builds need Python and Ninja on Windows, macOS or Linux. configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.7.5, objdiff v3.4.5, binutils 2.42-1 and the 20251118 compiler bundle for Metrowerks CodeWarrior (GC/3.0a5.2 as the linker version), and wibo runs the 32-bit Windows tools on macOS and Linux. CONTRIBUTING lists Ghidra with a shared project, IDA/Hex-Rays, m2c and decomp.me as decompiling aids and objdiff for diffing.

CI builds all four versions in a private container that supplies the original files, then uploads map files and progress reports; the percentages above come from those reports and do not establish a complete or shiftable rebuild. This review built or ran nothing.

LICENSE is CC0 1.0. The BTE Bluetooth library notes code taken from Android’s bluedroid under Apache-2.0, and the GameSpy SDK subset is BSD-3-Clause. The decompiled third-party middleware (JustSystems ATOK, Zi eZiText, TMC JPEG, eSOL PrFILE2) and the Opera WWW headers carry no separate grants, and the Wii Menu keeps Nintendo’s rights. CONTRIBUTING forbids using AI to decompile code and asks contributors to avoid AI-only matching forks; the reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: usque: an open reimplementation of Cloudflare WARP’s MASQUE mode
description_en: Reimplements the MASQUE mode of Cloudflare’s WARP client in Go, tunnelling IP traffic over QUIC/HTTP/3 with Connect-IP (RFC 9484) and exposing it as a native TUN device, SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies, TCP-only L4 proxies or port forwarding. RESEARCH.md describes how the author worked out device enrollment, TLS client authentication and Cloudflare’s non-standard cf-connect-ip variant by analyzing the official Android client with Frida, mitmproxy, JADX, IDA Free and Wireshark. It registers with and connects to Cloudflare’s service outside the official client.
description_zh: 用 Go 重新实现 Cloudflare WARP 客户端的 MASQUE 模式：通过基于 QUIC/HTTP/3 的 Connect-IP（RFC 9484）隧道传输 IP 流量，并以原生 TUN 设备、SOCKS5 或 HTTP 代理、仅 TCP 的 L4 代理或端口转发等形式提供。RESEARCH.md 记录了作者如何借助 Frida、mitmproxy、JADX、IDA Free 和 Wireshark 分析官方 Android 客户端，弄清设备注册、TLS 客户端认证以及 Cloudflare 非标准的 cf-connect-ip 变体。它在官方客户端之外向 Cloudflare 服务注册并建立连接。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-07-20 main head, identical to release v4.2.1. The README calls the project early-stage, says its Go API is unstable if used as a library, and states that only the Linux amd64 release binary was tested, although builds are published for Android, Linux, Windows and macOS on several architectures. RESEARCH.md is a narrative research log; the concise protocol document the README plans has not been written.

Requires access to Cloudflare’s WARP service: the register command creates a new WARP account and enrolls a device key, and the generated config holds that registration’s keys and tokens. The tool uses Cloudflare’s service outside the official client; the README says it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or reviewed by Cloudflare, asks users not to abuse the service and notes that the tool is detectable. ZeroTrust login needs SSO the tool cannot perform; this record gives no token, account or configuration details.

Building needs Go 1.26.3+ with CGO disabled. The project depends on the author’s fork of connect-ip-go because, the README says, Cloudflare’s implementation is not fully RFC 9484-compliant; quic-go carries the connection, and gVisor and wireguard-go netstacks let the proxy modes run in user space without root. Native TUN mode is limited to Linux and Windows, while the README’s Known Issues list still says Linux only. A Dockerfile is provided.

CI verifies modules and runs go build, go vet, go test and golangci-lint, but the reviewed tree contains no Go test files, so correctness evidence is the author’s own use. The README reports one SOCKS5 speed test of about 834/773 Mbps on a 1 Gbps link and lists missing features such as happy eyeballs, WireGuard and DNS-over-HTTPS. These results are author-reported, and this source review ran nothing.
