MIT (LICENSE.md). Cloudflare’s service terms and trademarks apply separately, and the README describes usque as an independent research project. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: awesome-unofficial-pc-ports
description_en: A single-README guide to unofficial PC ports of console games built from decompilations or recompilations and chosen for easy installation by players. Its 76 game entries, grouped under Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, SEGA, Indie and J2ME, each recommend a port with short setup notes and often link the underlying decompilation and alternative ports; a Utilities section adds two recompilation launchers.
description_zh: 以单个 README 维护的非官方 PC 移植指南，收录基于反编译或重编译、且便于玩家安装的主机游戏移植。76 个游戏条目按 Nintendo、PlayStation、Xbox、SEGA、独立游戏和 J2ME 分组，每项推荐一个移植版并附简短安装说明，常同时链接所依据的反编译项目和其他移植版；“实用工具”部分另列两个重编译启动器。
requirements: The reviewed README, committed 2026-10-15, has 78 collapsible entries: 43 Nintendo, 12 PlayStation, 14 Xbox, 5 SEGA, 1 indie and 1 J2ME game, plus 2 launcher utilities. Its stated criteria are console games ported to PC through decompilation or recompilation that offer an easy install path, such as a launcher or drag-and-drop; a star marks the most user-friendly option for each game.

Entries are written for players: a recommended port, a line or two of setup notes and, for some games, the underlying decompilation, alternative ports or tutorial videos. They state no matching, completion or license status, and the list also carries projects outside its stated criteria, such as Severed Chains, which it calls a reverse-engineered native recreation, and a port of the PC game Cave Story+, so each project must be checked at its own source.

Most entries tell players to supply their own ROM, disc image, ISO, game dump or XBLA package. The Ratchet & Clank: Clone Home entry also links a third-party archive.org copy of the recovered original J2ME build; this catalog does not link it, and a listing does not establish rights to any game files.

The README promotes Quiver Launcher, a separate catalog website and launcher, and says the list is kept up in spare time with updates that can take months. The repository holds only README.md and an MIT license (copyright 2023 Sebastrion); linked ports, original games and their assets keep their own rights. An independent discovery list; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: Reverse Engineering iOS Applications
description_en: Ivan Rodriguez's free English course (version 1.1) on reverse engineering iOS applications, aimed at beginners in iOS app security. Five Markdown modules cover setting up a jailbroken test device, decrypting App Store apps for analysis, static analysis of an IPA's files, frameworks, Objective-C classes and ARM binary in Hopper or Ghidra, runtime analysis with Cycript and Frida, and binary patching in Hopper. Exercises use CoinZa, a deliberately insecure Objective-C app the author built from vulnerability classes he reports finding in production App Store apps.
description_zh: Ivan Rodriguez 编写的免费英文课程（1.1 版），讲解 iOS 应用逆向工程，面向 iOS 应用安全初学者。五个 Markdown 模块依次介绍越狱测试设备的环境配置、为分析而解密 App Store 应用、对 IPA 中的文件、框架、Objective-C 类和 ARM 二进制进行静态分析（使用 Hopper 或 Ghidra）、用 Cycript 和 Frida 做运行时分析，以及在 Hopper 中修补二进制。练习使用 CoinZa：作者根据其所述在 App Store 正式应用中发现的漏洞类型，专门编写的一个故意不安全的 Objective-C 应用。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 183873a (2024-04-17). The course was written mainly in 2019; commits since mid-2020 are a few small wording and command fixes. Device instructions cover iOS 10 through 12, and many setup tools are from that period, so they may not work on current devices. The introduction excludes jailbreaking, iOS exploitation, tweak development, backend API testing and in-depth ARM assembly.

The prerequisites page lists no mandatory knowledge but recommends a Mac (Xcode has no Windows alternative), basic Objective-C, Swift, JavaScript, HTML, SSH/SCP and man-in-the-middle concepts, and an ARM disassembler such as Ghidra, IDA or Hopper's trial. A jailbroken iPhone/iPad/iPod on iOS 10 or later is needed only for the decryption module and the Cycript and Frida exercises.

No third-party app is needed for the exercises: the author ships CoinZa as an already-decrypted IPA, plus an EPUB of the course, in the companion repository RE-iOS-Apps-Extras-Github. The README says its vulnerabilities come from production apps but are reproduced in CoinZa instead of being published against those apps, and the closing page asks readers to report vulnerabilities responsibly.

There is no separate license file; the README carries an MIT-style permission notice (Copyright 2019 Ivan Rodriguez) and an at-your-own-risk disclaimer; the closing page asks people who reuse the material to credit the author. This collection read the course pages at the reviewed commit and did not install CoinZa or follow the device steps; the course mentions no AI or REA use.

name: Webamp: a browser reimplementation of Winamp 2
description_en: Reimplements Winamp 2's main, equalizer and playlist windows in HTML5 and JavaScript, with Web Audio playback, volume, balance and equalizer, and renders original classic .wsz skins, which its documentation says match Winamp 2.9 pixel for pixel; Milkdrop presets run through the Butterchurn WebGL port. It ships as the webamp npm module for embedding in web pages, and the same monorepo runs webamp.org and the skins.webamp.org skin museum. Its webamp-modern prototype targets Winamp 3/5 modern skins with an interpreter for MAKI skin scripts, whose undocumented bytecode format the author reverse engineered and documents in the repository.
description_zh: 用 HTML5 和 JavaScript 重新实现 Winamp 2 的主窗口、均衡器和播放列表窗口，借助 Web Audio 实现播放、音量、声道平衡和均衡器，并渲染原有的经典 .wsz 皮肤，其文档称渲染效果与 Winamp 2.9 逐像素一致；Milkdrop 预设通过 Butterchurn 的 WebGL 移植版运行。它以 webamp npm 模块的形式发布，可嵌入网页，同一 monorepo 还运行着 webamp.org 和 skins.webamp.org 皮肤博物馆。其中的 webamp-modern 原型面向 Winamp 3/5 的现代皮肤，内含 MAKI 皮肤脚本解释器；MAKI 字节码格式原本没有公开文档，作者对其进行了逆向分析，并在仓库中写成文档。
requirements: Release at review: webamp 2.3.1 on npm, published 2026-06-16; the reviewed master commit (2026-10-17) adds unreleased accessibility and API changes listed in the changelog. The README says it works in modern Edge, Firefox, Safari and Chrome. It reimplements Winamp's behavior and skin rendering rather than recovering Winamp's code, and webamp-modern remains a prototype with an open list of unimplemented MAKI and skin features.

No original Winamp installation is needed: Webamp bundles a default skin and sample track, and users can load their own Winamp 2 .wsz skins, audio files, Milkdrop presets and .eqf equalizer presets. Skins and audio fetched from another domain must be served with CORS permission, because Webamp reads their contents.

Development uses pnpm and Turborepo; .nvmrc names Node.js 22 and CI uses Node.js 20 to build every package, lint, type-check and run the Jest tests. These test Webamp's own parsing and rendering, not equivalence with Winamp. Compiling webamp-modern's MAKI test scripts calls the bundled Winamp 5.66 mc.exe, directly on Windows or through Wine elsewhere.

The code is MIT-licensed, and the README says the Winamp name, interface and sample audio file are Nullsoft's property. Bundled files that carry no license of their own: the Nullsoft MAKI compiler builds under packages/webamp-modern/resources/maki_compiler (five mc.exe versions from Winamp 3 alpha 8r to Winamp 5.66, nscrt.dll and the MAKI .mi library headers), the skins named after Winamp defaults (base-2.91, Winamp 3 build 499, Winamp Modern 5.66) and the third-party community skins used for demos and tests, the llama sample MP3 and the Winamp Modern Skins tutorial PDF. The bundled Perl MAKI decompiler is GPL-2.0. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use; nothing was built or run.

name: awesome-decompilation
description_en: A short, link-only reading list on decompiling machine code, last updated in 2023. Its 45 links cover foundational theses, compiler and program-analysis books, decompiler products and projects, pipeline topics from intermediate representations to type, control-flow and identifier recovery, early neural-decompilation papers and binary-to-source matching.
description_zh: 篇幅不长、只列链接的机器码反编译阅读清单，最近一次更新在 2023 年。45 个链接涵盖奠基性学位论文、编译器与程序分析书籍、反编译器产品和项目，从中间表示到类型、控制流和标识符恢复的反编译流程主题，早期神经网络反编译论文，以及二进制与源码匹配。
requirements: Not maintained as a current index: the reviewed master commit of 2023-03-05 is the newest in the repository and added the December 2022 preprint Beyond the C (arXiv 2212.08950). The AI-based section therefore stops at six neural-decompilation papers and projects, and later work, including LLM-based decompilation, is absent.

Entries are bare links under 13 headings, with no annotations, dates, status or license notes. They point to paper and thesis PDFs, vendor product pages, GitHub repositories and online-store book pages, and some PDFs are third-party mirrors; this review did not check whether every link still resolves.

The scope is native-code decompilation theory and tooling. Its six projects are Hex-Rays, Ghidra’s decompiler, JEB, RetDec, rev.ng-c and jsdec, and its eight intermediate representations include LLVM IR, VEX, BAP, REIL, ESIL, Binary Ninja’s LLIL and VTIL. It is a reading list, not an index of game decompilations or reconstruction projects.

The repository holds only README.md, with no license file or contribution guide, and GitHub detects no license, so the list states no reuse terms. Linked papers, books and tools keep their own rights, and some listed decompilers are commercial products. An independent reading list; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: tiny-dec
description_en: Zhuo Zhang's small educational decompiler for 32-bit RISC-V (RV32I) ELF files, written in Python to teach how decompilation works rather than to compete with production decompilers. Its 19 deliberately separate stages run from ELF loading, decoding and p-code lifting through SSA, stack, type, variable and range recovery to control-flow structuring and C output, and the CLI can stop at any stage to print that stage's intermediate result. The README also offers a Claude Code plugin whose AI tutor walks learners through the stages with quizzes and exercises.
description_zh: Zhuo Zhang 用 Python 编写的小型教学用反编译器，面向 32 位 RISC-V（RV32I）ELF 文件，目的是讲清反编译的工作原理，而非与生产级反编译器竞争。它把流程刻意拆成 19 个独立阶段：从 ELF 加载、指令解码和 p-code 提升，经过 SSA、栈、类型、变量和取值范围恢复，再到控制流结构化和 C 代码输出；命令行可在任一阶段停下，打印该阶段的中间结果。README 还提供一个 Claude Code 插件，其中的 AI 导师会结合小测和练习，带学习者逐个阶段学习。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 4f5f1e0 (2026-05-27), the repository's only commit; the package is version 0.1.0, and the repository's test and lint workflows passed on that commit. The README calls it a teaching tool, not a production decompiler: it handles RV32I only, and unresolved expressions stay in the output as raw<...> rather than being guessed. A live demo site at tiny-dec.zzhang.xyz shows the stages.

Input is an RV32I ELF file. The repository commits 13 C test programs and 39 RV32I builds of them (-O0 and -O2, PIE and non-PIE) under tests/fixtures, so no outside binaries are needed. Rebuilding them or compiling one's own C code needs clang, lld and LLVM with RISC-V support, installed locally or through the included Docker development image.

Requires Python 3.12+ and Poetry, and the loader leaves ELF parsing to pwntools; the README lists Ubuntu/Debian system packages, and a devcontainer is included. The AI tutor needs Claude Code and installs as a plugin from the repository's marketplace manifest; its skill files hold one lesson guide per pipeline stage.

MIT license (Copyright 2026 Zhuo Zhang). The 500-test count and the example outputs are the author's. This collection did not install or run the decompiler, try the tutor or judge output quality. The tutor is an AI teaching aid, not an REA integration, and the repository does not mention REA.

name: sead: a decompilation of Nintendo’s first-party C++ standard library
description_en: Decompiles sead, the C++ standard library that Nintendo statically links into its first-party games, covering containers, heaps, strings, math, file devices, threads, the game framework and graphics. Compile-time presets target the recent versions used by Breath of the Wild, Super Mario Odyssey, Splatoon 3, Tears of the Kingdom and Super Mario Bros. Wonder, and game decompilations such as Breath of the Wild pull it in as a submodule. Names come from debugging symbols and assertions in retail titles, and the README warns that many inlined and templated names are guesses.
description_zh: 反编译 sead，即 Nintendo 静态链接进其第一方游戏的 C++ 标准库，涵盖容器、堆、字符串、数学、文件设备、线程、游戏框架和图形等模块。编译期预设针对《旷野之息》《超级马力欧 奥德赛》《斯普拉遁 3》《王国之泪》和《超级马力欧兄弟 惊奇》所用的较新版本，《旷野之息》等游戏反编译项目以子模块方式引入它。命名来自零售游戏中的调试符号和断言，README 也提醒许多内联与模板函数的名称只是猜测。
requirements: The reviewed master commit (2026-10-11, no releases) derives from aboood40091/sead but targets newer sead versions. The README says several modules currently fail to build for Switch and points to a GitHub project page for progress; seadVersion.h adds a Super Mario Maker 2 preset and a custom feature set alongside the README’s list.

Building needs no game files. Checking accuracy needs the original sead, which ships only statically linked in games: the README advises legally owning a recent first-party title with debugging symbols, naming Super Mario Odyssey 1.0.0, Splatoon 2 up to 3.1.0 and the Nintendo Labo pilot build.

The README asks for a partially C++17-capable compiler such as Clang 3.9 or newer and CMake 3.10+. CMakeLists builds an object library only for the nin (nnSdk, Switch) platform and links NintendoSDK headers supplied by the host project, the old or new open-ead header repository depending on a migration option. The README also describes Wii U (cafe) sources and declares other platforms unsupported.

The README asks contributors to match non-inlined functions against the original assembly, tolerating only register-allocation or obviously harmless reordering differences marked NOT_MATCHING, and to undo inlining with help from pilot builds and assertions; MATCHING_HACK_NX_CLANG guards codegen hacks. The repository has no checker or progress data of its own, and CI only runs clang-format, so matching is checked in consumer projects. This review ran nothing.

No license file is present and GitHub detects none; the README says nobody outside Nintendo has sead’s source. res/ holds the decompiled primitive-renderer shader sources plus a 2 KB compiled Wii U shader binary that was updated alongside them. Nintendo’s games keep their own rights, and the reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: TeddyCloud: a self-hosted replacement for the Toniebox cloud
description_en: Reimplements the Boxine cloud services a Toniebox talks to as a self-hosted C server, so the box can fetch audio, settings and over-the-air content locally while the owner controls what reaches the manufacturer. It serves and caches tonie audio, converts other audio into the box’s TAF format, can pass requests through to the original cloud, and adds a web interface, MQTT and Home Assistant integration. Protobuf definitions in the repository describe the box’s freshness-check, RTNL log and TAF header messages.
description_zh: 以可自托管的 C 服务器重新实现 Toniebox 所连接的 Boxine 云服务，使盒子能在本地获取音频、设置和无线下发内容，同时由用户控制哪些数据发往厂商。它可提供并缓存 tonie 音频，把其他音频转换为盒子使用的 TAF 格式，可将请求透传到原云端，并提供网页界面、MQTT 及 Home Assistant 集成。仓库中的 protobuf 定义描述了盒子的 freshness-check、RTNL 日志和 TAF 头部报文。
requirements: Reviewed at the stable master head of 2026-08-25, the v0.7.0 merge; release tc_v0.7.0 was tagged the same day, and active development continues on the develop branch. The project’s setup guide covers Toniebox 1 boxes with CC3200, CC3235 or ESP32 chips, and the README lists Toniebox 2 support as planned.

Setup is invasive and specific to each box: the project guide has owners dump their own box’s client certificates, flash a replacement CA into the box and redirect its DNS, and the server can extract or inject certificates in an ESP32 firmware dump. The repository ships no box certificates, firmware or tonie audio (those directories are empty placeholders), and this record gives no extraction or flashing steps. The dev-sandbox’s pre-generated certificates are self-signed and meant only for local testing.

Builds with a hand-written Makefile, protoc-c and a C toolchain, plus submodules for CycloneTCP/SSL/Crypto, cJSON, Opus, Ogg, the teddycloud_web frontend and emsdk; Linux debug builds enable AddressSanitizer and UBSan, and Docker is the recommended path on macOS. Release tc_v0.7.0 attaches an amd64 zip from the Windows/Linux release workflow, and Debian, Ubuntu and Alpine Docker images are published for several platforms. Stream conversion uses ffmpeg.

Python API tests for the custom-tonie JSON endpoints and a WASM TAF-encoder test run through Makefile targets; the reviewed workflows build and publish without running them. A dev-sandbox serves mock tonies, box and TAF data. Behavior with real boxes and the Boxine cloud remains project-reported, and this source review ran nothing.

GPL-2.0 (LICENSE); the vendored Cyclone stack, Opus, Ogg, cJSON and FatFs keep their own terms. Tonie audio, box firmware and Boxine’s services keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: Reverse Engineering Reading List
description_en: A short reading list, compiled by One Thawt mostly in 2015–2016, of about 58 links to reverse-engineering tools, books, papers, talks and blog posts, kept in a README and a separate malware-analysis page. Sections run from disassemblers and debuggers, beginner talks and classic books through data-structure recovery papers, instruction-set references, iOS, Android and Windows material, unpacking, deobfuscation and protocol inference from network traces.
description_zh: 由 One Thawt 编写的简短阅读清单，主要成形于 2015–2016 年，在一个 README 和单独的恶意软件分析页面中收录约 58 个链接，涵盖逆向工程工具、书籍、论文、演讲和博客文章。各部分从反汇编器与调试器、入门讲座和经典书籍，到数据结构恢复论文、指令集参考资料、iOS、Android 与 Windows 相关资料、脱壳、反混淆，以及基于网络流量的协议推断。
requirements: Reviewed at commit a1ee767 (2023-05-02). 46 of 53 commits date from 2015–2016; the last added entries are x64dbg (2017), Binary Ninja (2018) and Ghidra (2019), and the 2023 commit merged a 2018 pull request that removed a dead link. The list therefore predates most current tools and research, including any machine-learning or LLM-assisted reverse engineering.

Most entries are a bare link, some followed by a quoted publisher or project description, and there are no notes on difficulty, platform or currency. Many point to 2010–2016 posts and PDFs on personal or project sites, and the README suggests archive.org for links that are down. In an automated check at review, six of the 59 unique URLs in the two files gave no response, a 404 or a sign-in page, and the TIE and HyperV entries link to unrelated documents (an iOS 6 security talk and an IR-synthesis slide deck).

Books link to Amazon store pages, and IDA Pro, Binary Ninja and Hopper are commercial products. The Windows section also links older write-ups on kernel-protection bypasses, which this record does not describe further.

GitHub detects no license and the repository has no license file, so the list states no reuse terms; linked works keep their own rights. The author offers copies of unavailable documents on request through a personal contact page. Nothing in the list mentions AI or REA.

name: Animal Forest: an in-progress matching N64 decompilation
description_en: Rebuilds the Japanese Nintendo 64 release of Animal Forest (Dōbutsu no Mori) from C code reverse-engineered from the ROM, combined with assets and assembly extracted from a user-supplied ROM. Default builds compare the uncompressed and recompressed ROMs with stored MD5 checksums. The README rules out use as a port base or for commercial purposes, and decomp.dev reported 18.52% of code matched at the reviewed commit.
description_zh: 将从 ROM 逆向得到的 C 代码与从使用者自备 ROM 中提取的素材和汇编结合，重建日版 Nintendo 64《动物之森》（どうぶつの森）。默认构建会用仓库保存的 MD5 校验未压缩与重新压缩的 ROM。README 明确该项目不作为移植基础，也不用于商业目的；decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 18.52% 的代码已匹配。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress decompilation whose codebase could change drastically and warns that some parts of the ROM may not yet be shiftable. The only configured version is jp, the Japanese N64 release, in both the Makefile and CI. The output is an N64 ROM; README states that the project is not a port and that serving as a port base or any commercial use is explicitly a non-goal. The GameCube Animal Crossing decompilation it links to is a separate project.

Supply your own Japanese Animal Forest ROM as the base ROM in baseroms/jp; .z64, .n64 and .v64 files are accepted. make setup decompresses it and checks the result against baseroms/jp/checksum.md5, then make extract uses splat to derive assembly and assets locally. The reviewed tree holds no ROM, graphics or binary asset files; game-derived content is limited to tables such as the DMA file table header and small address tables under src/objects.

README documents Linux, preferably Debian or Ubuntu, with make, Git, build-essential, clang, MIPS binutils and Python 3 with pip and venv; make venv installs pinned splat64 0.24.0 plus spimdisasm and mapfile-parser. The tools Makefile downloads static recompilations of IDO 5.3 and 7.1 from decompals/ido-static-recomp v1.2 and pigment64 0.6.3, and the build compiles libultra from the bundled ultralib subrepo. NON_MATCHING builds turn the checksum comparison off.

With COMPARE at its default, make rom and make compress check both ROMs against the stored MD5 values. Functions not yet decompiled remain extracted assembly included through GLOBAL_ASM, so a passing check does not mean complete decompilation. CI builds jp in a private container that supplies the base ROM and compiler archives, compares warning counts and uploads an objdiff-format report. decomp.dev's report for the pinned commit lists 465,796 of 2,515,744 code bytes (18.52%) and 2,998 of 14,415 functions matched, with no unit complete; this collection ran no build.

README licenses src and include, as far as possible, and other files that state no other license under CC0-1.0, excluding subrepos such as asm-differ, asm-processor, fado and ultralib. Nintendo's game, ROM contents and the downloaded compilers keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Remade
description_en: The source repository of remade.wiki, a community-curated directory of open-source reimplementations of closed-source software, mostly creative, productivity and engineering applications. Each listing is a YAML record naming the original software, languages, platforms, license and self-reported status, compatibility and limitations, and the directory also tracks requests for software nobody has reimplemented yet.
description_zh: remade.wiki 的源码仓库。remade.wiki 是由社区整理的目录，收录闭源软件的开源重新实现，以创意、办公和工程类应用为主。每个条目是一份 YAML 记录，注明被重现的原软件、编程语言、平台、许可证，以及自报的开发状态、兼容程度和局限；目录还收集尚无人重新实现的软件请求。
requirements: A young directory: the repository was created on 2026-10-09, and its history reached 308 commits by the reviewed commit of 2026-10-19. Its catalog files hold 123 project records, 13 supporting tools, 2 suites and 379 Project Requests for software with no listed reimplementation yet; remade.wiki is built from these files.

Listings target closed-source originals, mostly desktop and web applications, with Adobe, Autodesk and Microsoft products frequent among them. By category there are 53 creative, 37 productivity and 22 engineering records, plus 5 operating-systems, 3 developer-tools, 2 other and 1 games record. Status and compatibility are self-reported: 78 records are experimental, 26 alpha, 13 beta, 5 stable and 1 planned, and 107 claim partial compatibility.

POLICY.md requires independently authored code without leaked or unauthorized source, binaries or assets, excludes forks, ports, launchers and mods of the original, and leaves clean-room claims to each project’s authors; Remade states it does not audit provenance or legality. Only one record mentions a clean-room process, so whether a listing relied on clean-room work, reverse engineering or public documentation must be checked at its own source.

The repository’s MIT license covers the directory’s code and data; listed projects keep their own licenses, from MIT and Apache-2.0 to GPL and AGPL, with one recorded as Unlicensed. The project’s own 2026-10-17 documentary audit of 119 entries left unreachable repositories and license conflicts unresolved and disclaims software, legal or compatibility certification. An independent directory; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: PixMob IR reverse engineering: controlling event wristbands at home
description_en: Recovers enough of the infrared protocol used by PixMob event wristbands to light them at home, starting from Flipper Zero recordings made at concerts and games and replaying them to bracelets. Pulse-timing analysis found 38 kHz signals with bit intervals of roughly 700 µs, and targeted brute forcing from an ESP32 discovered hundreds of colour, fade, random and motion-mode commands, now sent through Arduino, Python and web tools. The README calls the result far from exhaustive and points to a later repository that decoded most of the full IR protocol through MCU dumping.
description_zh: 从在演唱会和球赛现场用 Flipper Zero 录下的信号出发，把录音重放给手环，恢复出足以在家中点亮 PixMob 活动手环的部分红外协议。脉冲时序分析发现信号载波为 38 kHz、比特间隔约 700 微秒；项目再用 ESP32 做有针对性的暴力枚举，找到数百条颜色、渐变、随机和体感模式命令，现可通过 Arduino、Python 和网页工具发送。README 称这些结果远未穷尽，并指向一个后来通过 MCU 转储基本解出完整红外协议的仓库。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-02-06 main head; there are no releases. The write-up covers IR bracelets, while the rf folder adds 915 MHz and 868 MHz OOK recordings and notes for RF wristbands, where a further encoding layer and a likely CRC remain unresolved. The project reports testing six IR bracelet versions made between 2014 and 2021, and a hardware table lists boards and MCUs where known.

Needs the user’s own PixMob bracelets with fresh batteries and an Arduino-compatible board or ESP32 with a 940 nm IR emitter, using the IRremote or IRremoteESP8266 library; a Flipper Zero can instead send codes from a separate repository. The Python tools need pyserial, PySimpleGUI and clipboard, and the web interface runs in Chrome and connects directly to the Arduino.

The evidence is recordings and observed bracelet reactions: the repository holds raw Flipper IR captures from several events, edited RF captures, the discovered effect definitions, a record of brute-force attempts and a dump of one bracelet’s 24C02 EEPROM. The README says brute forcing targeted only a few packet lengths, so the code list is far from exhaustive, and the programming and choreography signals used at events remain undiscovered.

Python unit tests cover the conversion functions and Flipper-file parsing; there is no CI. Effects are reported by the author and contributors from their own bracelets, and this source review ran no code or hardware.
MIT (LICENSE). PixMob’s hardware, firmware and trademarks are outside that license, and the X-ray images are credited to Samy Kamkar. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: Reverse Engineering resources (wtsxDev)
description_en: A single-README awesome list, started in January 2017 and maintained under the KaliTut name, of 139 reverse-engineering links in 16 sections: books, courses, practice targets, hex editors, binary-format tools, disassemblers, binary analysis, bytecode analysis, import reconstruction, dynamic analysis, debugging, Mac decryption, document analysis, scripting, Android and YARA. Entries are mostly a tool or resource name with its link, a few with a one-line usage note, and lean towards Windows and macOS tooling and malware analysis.
description_zh: 以单个 README 维护的 awesome 清单，2017 年 1 月创建，以 KaliTut 名义维护，共收录 139 个逆向工程链接，分为 16 个部分：书籍、课程、练习目标、十六进制编辑器、二进制格式工具、反汇编器、二进制分析、字节码分析、导入表重建、动态分析、调试、Mac 解密、文档分析、脚本、Android 和 YARA。条目大多只有工具或资源名称及链接，少数附一行用法说明，内容偏重 Windows 与 macOS 工具以及恶意软件分析。
requirements: Reviewed at commit b254985 (2019-03-07), still the default-branch head; all 26 commits date from 2017–2019, so the list predates most current tools and any LLM-assisted workflow. In an automated check at review, 24 of its 147 unique URLs gave no response, a 404 or a 503, among them every tuts4you download link, the Apple man-page links, Crackmes.de, malwr.com and the CodePlex z3 page.

Entries state no license, platform, maturity or maintenance status, so each tool must be checked at its own source; several, such as IDA Pro, 010 Editor and Binary Ninja, are commercial. Books mostly use amzn.to short links, and the header image and five closing links point to book lists on kalitut.com.

The Practice section places crackme and CTF sites next to public malware-sample repositories with only a warning to be careful with malware, and the Mac Decrypt section names tools without describing their use; this record treats the list only as a directory of analysis resources.

A package.json and .travis.yml set up remark-lint checks for list order, duplicate links and dead links on Node.js 8 under Travis CI. GitHub detects no license, the repository has no license file and the package.json license field is empty, so the list states no reuse terms; linked tools and books keep their own. An independent discovery list; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: Decomp Academy
description_en: A free, English, in-browser course in matching decompilation maintained by Jack Price-Burns: learners read a function's target assembly, write C, and the original console compiler grades the result byte for byte. Lessons build from reading registers and arithmetic through control flow, structs, floating point, the ABI, globals, optimizer behaviour and 64-bit integers, then finish with functions adapted from open-source decompilation projects. The curriculum now spans GameCube PowerPC, Game Boy Advance Thumb and Nintendo 64 MIPS courses, and the frontend source is on GitHub.
description_zh: 由 Jack Price-Burns 维护的免费英文在线课程，在浏览器中教授一致性反编译：学习者阅读函数的目标汇编，编写 C 代码，再由原版主机编译器逐字节评判结果。课程从读寄存器和算术运算讲起，依次覆盖控制流、结构体、浮点、ABI、全局变量、优化器行为和 64 位整数，最后以改编自开源反编译项目的函数收尾。课程目前包括 GameCube PowerPC、Game Boy Advance Thumb 和 Nintendo 64 MIPS 三门，前端源码公开在 GitHub 上。
requirements: Reviewed at frontend commit a21f9d0 (2026-09-23); the repository was first published in June 2026 and has had commits most months since. The README still describes a single GameCube course of 258 lessons, but the reviewed curriculum and the live site list 755 lessons in three courses: GameCube (263), Game Boy Advance (251) and Nintendo 64 (241), each in four tiers from warm-up to real functions.

Lessons run in the browser at decomp-academy.dev and the README says no signup is needed to start; an account stores progress. Grading compiles the learner's C with the original compilers and diffs it using objdiff: Metrowerks CodeWarrior GC/2.0 for GameCube and SGI IDO 5.3 for Nintendo 64 on the hosted backend, a separate AGPL-3.0 repository that the README says runs the CodeWarrior compilers under wibo, and agbcc built to WebAssembly in the browser for Game Boy Advance.

No game files are needed: the later lessons adapt functions from open-source decompilation projects the README credits (Star Fox Adventures, Pikmin 2, Metroid Prime, Mario Party 4), and targets are generated server-side from each lesson's reference C. This repository contains no compiler, and the backend README says it commits only wibo, not MWCC; for local development the README expects Node 18+ and a sibling Star Fox Adventures decompilation checkout that supplies MWCC and binutils, while .env.example says a fresh clone uses the hosted compile API by default.

The frontend is AGPL-3.0, which also covers modified versions run as a network service. This collection read the README, curriculum metadata, one real-function lesson and the live home page; it did not solve lessons or check grading. A CLAUDE.md lesson-authoring guide for Claude Code is committed, but the README does not say how lessons were written, and REA is not mentioned.

name: Phantom Hourglass: an early-stage matching Nintendo DS decompilation
description_en: Recreates C++ source for The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass by hand-decompiling its European and US Nintendo DS releases, using the dsd toolkit to delink code from a user-supplied ROM and rebuild the ROM. objdiff tracks matches function by function, and the default build compares the output ROM with a stored SHA-1. The work is at an early stage: decomp.dev reported 2.82% of code matched at the reviewed commit.
description_zh: 通过手工反编译，为《塞尔达传说 幻影沙漏》的欧版与美版 Nintendo DS 重建 C++ 源码：借助 dsd 工具集从使用者自备的 ROM 中拆分代码，再重新构建 ROM。objdiff 逐个函数跟踪匹配情况，默认构建会将输出 ROM 与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。项目仍处于早期阶段：decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 2.82% 的代码已匹配。
requirements: README marks the project as a work in progress that targets the European and American versions, with other versions possibly supported later; configure.py takes eur or usa. Decompilation covers the ARM9 program, its TCM modules and overlays, while docs/build_system.md says the ARM7 program is not decompiled. The output is a Nintendo DS ROM, not a PC port.

Supply your own decrypted base ROM for each version in extract/ as baserom_ph_eur.nds or baserom_ph_usa.nds, matching the SHA-1 values in extract/README.md; dsd then extracts code and assets from it locally. INSTALL.md calls a byte-matching ROM optional and requires the user’s own DS ARM7 BIOS file, matching one of two listed SHA-1 values, to produce one. README says the repository contains no assets or assembly; config/ does commit game-derived dsd delink, symbol and relocation tables for 65 modules per version.

INSTALL.md lists Windows (recommended) or Linux with Python 3.11+ and pip, GCC 9+, Ninja and pre-commit hooks; on Linux the Windows compiler runs through wibo by default, or Wine on request. configure.py downloads dsd v0.11.0, objdiff v3.4.0, sjiswrap v1.2.2 and wibo 0.6.16 from GitHub releases, and a Metrowerks mwccarm bundle (version 2.0/sp1p5 is used) from decomp.aetias.com.

The default ninja targets generate objdiff data, run dsd’s module and symbol checks and compare the built ROM with ph_eur.sha1 or ph_usa.sha1. CI builds both versions in a build container that supplies extracted files and the compiler, running the ARM9 link, objdiff report and checks but not the ROM hash. decomp.dev’s default usa report for the pinned commit lists 102,202 of 3,622,306 code bytes (2.82%) and 1,351 of 24,610 functions matched, with 28 of 190 units complete; this collection ran no build.

The repository carries CC0-1.0; that dedication does not cover Nintendo’s game, its extracted files, the BIOS or the downloaded Metrowerks compiler. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Kinoko: reimplementing Mario Kart Wii’s physics engine for exact ghost replay
description_en: Re-implements Mario Kart Wii’s physics engine in C++ as a command-line simulator, continuing stblr/Hanachan’s goal of perfectly accurate time-trial ghost replay. Each test case replays a recorded ghost through the engine and compares kart position, rotation, velocities, speed and checkpoint state frame by frame with a trace captured from the original game. It is a behavioural reimplementation of the physics only, not a matching decompilation, and has no graphical frontend.
description_zh: 以 C++ 将 Mario Kart Wii 的物理引擎重新实现为命令行模拟器，延续 stblr/Hanachan 的目标：完全准确地回放计时赛幽灵记录。每个测试用例让引擎重放一条幽灵记录，并逐帧将赛车的位置、旋转、速度向量、速率和检查点状态与从原版游戏采集的轨迹比较。它只在行为层面重新实现物理部分，并非一致性反编译，也没有图形前端。
requirements: README describes a C++ reimplementation of Mario Kart Wii’s physics engine aiming at perfectly accurate ghost replay. At the reviewed commit STATUS.md lists 55 time-trial ghost test cases, each marked synchronized for every frame; the latest GitHub release, 0.6 (2025-09-04), adds x86-64 Linux, macOS and Windows binaries of the simulator. Source comments name addresses in the original game, but nothing rebuilds its executable; README points to the separate riidefi/mkw matching decompilation for that.

Running needs the Race folder (the Common and course archives) from your own Mario Kart Wii disc, placed relative to the executable; the repository ships no game files, and README requires any contributed frontend not to distribute in-game assets. The committed samples are time-trial ghost files (.rkg) with per-frame .krkg reference traces that README says come from a custom vabold/mkw-sp build running the PAL release; such traces are verification data captured from the game, as is common for reconstruction projects.

README lists g++ 13.1 with C++23, ninja 1.3 and Python 3.6; configure.py generates the ninja build and compiles testCases.json into the binary suite file. CMakeLists.txt also exposes a libkinoko library target for embedding the engine in other C++23 projects. CI builds with GCC 14 on Ubuntu; the program is a command-line host with test and replay modes, and README says no GUI is planned.

kinoko test compares position, rotation, internal and external velocity, speed, acceleration, soft speed limit, race completion and checkpoint values with every .krkg frame by exact equality and reports the first desynchronized frame; kinoko replay checks whether a ghost finishes with the time in its .rkg header. CI runs the suite with runtime files fetched from a secret-configured URL and checks that STATUS.md is current. These are project-reported results; this collection built and ran nothing.

LICENSE applies MIT (copyright vabold, 2022–2026) to the project; Mario Kart Wii and its game data keep Nintendo’s rights, and the bundled doxygen-awesome-css theme has its own license file. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: OWASP Firmware Security Testing Methodology (FSTM)
description_en: A free English methodology, maintained by Aaron Guzman and published on GitBook, for security testing and reverse engineering embedded-device firmware. It is organized as nine stages: information gathering, obtaining firmware, analyzing the image, extracting the filesystem, static analysis of its contents, emulation, dynamic testing, runtime analysis and binary exploitation, with example commands for tools such as binwalk, unblob, FACT, EMBA, Firmwalker, QEMU and Ghidra. An October 2025 revision added C/C++ static-analysis tools, SBOM generation and a mapping to the OWASP IoT Security Verification Standard (ISVS).
description_zh: 由 Aaron Guzman 维护、发布在 GitBook 上的免费英文方法论，用于嵌入式设备固件的安全测试与逆向工程。全文分为九个阶段：信息收集、获取固件、分析固件镜像、提取文件系统、静态分析文件系统内容、仿真、动态测试、运行时分析和二进制漏洞利用，并给出 binwalk、unblob、FACT、EMBA、Firmwalker、QEMU 和 Ghidra 等工具的示例命令。2025 年 10 月的修订加入了 C/C++ 静态分析工具、SBOM 生成，以及与 OWASP IoT 安全验证标准（ISVS）的对应关系。
requirements: Reviewed at default-branch commit ec666e8 (2025-10-05). Most of the text dates from 2019–2020, with a 2022 EMBA/EMBArk update and an October 2025 revision that refreshed tool references, removed commercial ones and added the SAST, SBOM and ISVS sections; the published GitBook includes those additions. A feature branch adding ISVS requirement mappings by stage (June 2026) was not merged at review, and a shorter 2020 Chinese translation sits on the separate zhong-wen-fstm branch.

Its stated audience is security researchers, software developers, consultants, hobbyists and information-security professionals. It is a single long reference page of procedures and commands rather than a paced course, and it points to the OWASP IoT Security Testing Guide for hardware, wireless, network and user-interface tests outside firmware.

Following it needs the firmware image or the physical device under an authorized assessment; the methodology tells testers to choose acquisition methods by project objectives and rules of engagement and to follow local laws. Some stages assume hardware debug access and a chip programmer. Tools mostly run on Linux; the README links a preconfigured EmbedOS Ubuntu VM from 2020 and, for practice, deliberately vulnerable firmware such as OWASP IoTGoat, DVRF and DVID.

Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (License.md). This collection read the README at the reviewed commit and checked that the GitBook carries the 2025 sections; it did not run the commands or tools. The methodology describes no AI or REA use.

name: Awesome Android Reverse Engineering
description_en: An awesome list of Android reverse-engineering training, tools and resources started in 2023 by James Stevenson, with 92 one-line entries, 16 of them starred as great and up to date. It covers courses, videos and books; static analysis and deobfuscation, networking and Frida-based instrumentation, decompilers and malware analysis tools; documentation and case studies; CTFs and crackmes; obfuscation and anti-reversing; and a short firmware and kernel section.
description_zh: James Stevenson 于 2023 年创建的 awesome 清单，收录 Android 逆向工程的培训、工具和资源，共 92 个单行条目，其中 16 个以星标注为优质且较新的资源。内容涵盖课程、视频和书籍，静态分析与反混淆、网络分析与基于 Frida 的插桩、反编译器和恶意软件分析工具，文档与案例研究，CTF 与 crackme，混淆与反逆向，以及一个简短的固件与内核部分。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 0ade43d (2025-07-08). 51 of 58 commits date from 2023; a March 2025 rewrite reorganized the list and added the obfuscation and firmware sections, and the July 2025 commit removed the Cloud API section while its contents-menu entry remains.

Entries give a link and a one-line summary with no license, version or maintenance notes, and some summaries are loose; AFLSmart, for example, is described as a firmware-image fuzzer, while its own README presents an input-structure-aware greybox fuzzer. In an automated check at review, 8 of 90 unique URLs gave no response, a 404 or a 530: five linked GitHub repositories no longer exist, four of them (the ATDF, Paranoid, libhooker and Android kernel-exploits entries) added in the March 2025 rewrite, and the Houseparty case study, the Flare-On page and AndroidXref did not load.

Six entries are the maintainer's own tools and one his blog post. Burp Suite, IDA Pro, JEB and DexGuard are commercial, the Documentation section links the APKMirror and APKPure download sites, and tools for bypassing app controls, dumping memory and kernel exploitation appear as listed; this record treats the list only as a directory of analysis resources.

LICENSE is the MIT License (2023, James Stevenson), although the README points to a LICENSE.md that does not exist; placeholder changelog and to-do files from the repository template remain under .github. Linked tools, books and APKs keep their own terms. An independent discovery list; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!: a matching GameCube decompilation of the debug build
description_en: A work-in-progress 1:1 decompilation of Mario Kart: Double Dash!! that rebuilds the GameCube main.dol of the US debug build (MarioClub_us) from C and C++ with the original Metrowerks compilers, checking it against a stored SHA-1. The build splits the binary from a user-supplied disc image, and objdiff compares objects during development. decomp.dev reported 47.09% of code matched at the reviewed commit; a European retail target is configured but marked as not working yet.
description_zh: 《马力欧卡丁车：双重冲刺!!》的进行中 1:1 反编译：用原版 Metrowerks 编译器从 C 与 C++ 源码重建美版调试构建（MarioClub_us）的 GameCube main.dol，并与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。构建从使用者自备的光盘镜像中拆分二进制，开发时用 objdiff 比对目标文件。decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 47.09% 的代码已匹配；欧版零售目标虽已配置，但标注为尚不可用。
requirements: README calls this a WIP 1:1 decompilation and says only the debug version is supported: the default MarioClub_us (USA) target, whose main.dol SHA-1 config/MarioClub_us/build.sha1 records. configure.py also lists Release_eu, but its config.yml is marked as not working yet, and CI builds only MarioClub_us. The output is a GameCube DOL, not a PC executable or port.

Copy your own disc image of that build to orig/MarioClub_us; ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ and TGC images are accepted. README says the repository contains no game assets or assembly: decomp-toolkit splits the user’s DOL using the committed symbol and split tables, and during the build extracts a font, system.arc and build-time data from that DOL locally.

Builds need Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (with wine-crossover) or Linux (an automatically downloaded wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.6.2, objdiff v3.3.1, binutils 2.42-1, sjiswrap v1.2.1, wibo 0.7.0 and the 20250812 compiler bundle, using Metrowerks GC/2.6 for game, JSystem, MSL and TRK code and GC/1.2.5n for the Dolphin SDK libraries.

Objects marked Matching (518 in configure.py; 277 remain NonMatching and 13 Equivalent) are compiled from source, the rest are taken from the split DOL, and the build checks main.dol against build.sha1. CI builds MarioClub_us in a container that supplies the disc files and compilers, uploads a progress report and validates symbol order for changed C++ files. decomp.dev’s report for the pinned commit lists 1,517,644 of 3,222,748 code bytes (47.09%) and 8,695 of 15,357 functions matched, with 518 of 807 units complete; this collection ran no build.

The repository carries CC0-1.0; Nintendo’s game, disc contents and the downloaded compilers keep their own rights. README credits JSystem and SDK code reused from other decompilations, including Metroid Prime, Pikmin 2, Super Mario Galaxy, Super Mario Sunshine and Twilight Princess. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: 3S Decomp: a byte-compared PS2 decompilation of Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike
description_en: Decompiles the PlayStation 2 executable of Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike from Street Fighter Anniversary Collection into C that period Metrowerks and EE GCC compilers rebuild, then compares the rebuilt executable word by word with the user’s original. README reports the game code fully decompiled and the CRI middleware partly so. The separate 3SX native port describes itself as this project’s continuation.
description_zh: 将 Street Fighter Anniversary Collection 中《街头霸王 III：3rd Strike》的 PlayStation 2 可执行文件反编译为 C 源码，用当年的 Metrowerks 与 EE GCC 编译器重新构建，再将重建出的可执行文件与使用者自备的原文件逐字比较。README 报告游戏代码已全部反编译，CRI 中间件部分完成。另有独立的 3SX 原生移植，自称是本项目的延续。
requirements: README reports the game code fully decompiled and the CRI middleware partly decompiled, with most file-system and sound functions the game uses matching; cri-progress.md checks off 497 of the 503 CRI functions it lists. At the reviewed commit, two game functions (sea_write and mlt_obj_trans_rgb_ext) and 39 of 52 CRI C files still include assembly in the PS2 build, and PS2 SDK and GCC library code is out of scope. The output is the PS2 executable, not a PC port.

Building needs THIRD_U.BIN from the user’s own copy of the game; the split configuration records its SHA-1 as cf58495054c31ad852175c66e9ca04d5094f000e, and make split derives the assembly and linker script from it. The decompiling guide also relies on the executable’s DWARF debug data, dumped with decomp-toolkit, for signatures and local variables. A separate split_cps3 target for the CPS3 arcade version needs a user-supplied arcade ROM set and has only a code-segment configuration.

The build guide covers Linux (Debian packages with i386 support, MIPS binutils, and a Python venv with splat64 0.29.0 and spimdisasm 1.35.0) and macOS through the provided Dockerfile. make setup_tools downloads Metrowerks mwccps2 3.0b38 and EE GCC 2.96 from decomp.me’s compiler releases plus the wibo loader for Windows tools; m2c, asm-differ, mwccgap and saturn-splitter are git submodules.

A successful build ends with compare_bytes.py checking the rebuilt executable against the original from offset 0x80 to 0x478A00 and printing “Files match ✅”. That check tolerates 163 listed words in about 20 game and CRI functions, attributed to register and operand swaps, assert line numbers, string encoding, a misplaced nop and a call misalignment, so equivalence is near-byte-level by the project’s own check rather than a whole-file hash. The latest commit removed the GitHub Actions workflows, and this collection built nothing.

LICENSE is AGPL-3.0 for the project’s code. The original executable and game content keep their own rights; include/cri carries headers marked “CRI Middleware SDK” and “Copyright (c) … CRI-MW”, and the vendored zlib keeps its own license. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Halo: Combat Evolved: an incremental re-implementation patched into the original Xbox executable
description_en: A research project re-implementing the original Xbox Halo: Combat Evolved in C, one function at a time. Rewritten functions are compiled into a separate image and patched into the user’s original executable with redirects from the original implementations, so the hybrid game can be run and debugged in xemu or on an Xbox as work progresses. The project reports an early stage, and its sources document no byte-for-byte comparison with the original code.
description_zh: 一个以 C 语言逐个函数重新实现初代 Xbox 版 Halo: Combat Evolved 的研究项目。重写的函数编译为独立映像，再修补进使用者自备的原版可执行文件，并从原有实现重定向过去，使这一混合版本能在开发过程中于 xemu 或 Xbox 上运行和调试。项目自述仍处于早期阶段，其来源也未记录与原代码的逐字节比较。
requirements: README describes studying and creating a free, open-source re-implementation of the Xbox launch title; its current-state list reports that the patched game runs, the main loop and several more functions are re-implemented, and there is a long way to go. The linked progress page, whose data file was last modified in November 2022, reports 0.37% of the .text section’s game code across 40 functions. The last default-branch commit is dated 2023-07-07.

Supply the retail disc’s game files and the original executable version 01.10.12.2276, identified by MD5 in README and kb.json and placed as cachebeta.xbe in a halo-patched directory; tools/patch.py checks that hash. The repository includes no game executable or assets, and README says they must come from your own copy. The build writes a patched default.xbe beside them as the user’s local modified copy; the project distributes no game build.

Builds use CMake 3.16+, Python 3 with libclang, pefile and pyxbe, and either 32-bit MSVC on Windows or Clang and LLD targeting i386-pc-win32 on Linux and macOS; a Dockerfile provides an Ubuntu 22.04 build image. The result targets the original Xbox and runs in the xemu emulator or on console hardware, and the build generates a .gdbinit for debugging with GDB through xemu’s GDB server.

kb.json declares 323 original functions and 71 data items with addresses, grouped by original object file; tools/knowledge.py generates headers, thunks and an import library from it, and gen-struct-checks.py emits static size checks for types.h. CI builds only the re-implementation image (Debug and Release on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS) without original files, so it checks compilation, not behaviour. The sources document no byte-for-byte or automated gameplay comparison, and this collection ran nothing.

The repository has no license file and GitHub detects none, so reuse terms for the project’s code are not stated; src/xboxkrnl.exe.def carries a CC0-1.0 notice (2017, Stefan Schmidt). README presents the work as educational research, the progress page says it is not affiliated with Microsoft or Bungie, and the game keeps its rights holders’ terms. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door: an early matching GameCube decompilation
description_en: A work-in-progress matching decompilation of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door that targets the Japanese Rev 0 GameCube release (G8MJ01), rebuilding MarioSt.dol and 31 REL modules with the original Metrowerks compilers and checking each against a stored SHA-1. The build splits these binaries from a user-supplied disc image, and objdiff compares objects during development. decomp.dev reported 12.10% of code matched at the reviewed commit.
description_zh: 《纸片马力欧 RPG》（Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door）的进行中一致性反编译，目标为日版 Rev 0 GameCube 版本（G8MJ01）：用原版 Metrowerks 编译器重建 MarioSt.dol 和 31 个 REL 模块，并逐一与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。构建从使用者自备的光盘镜像中拆分这些二进制，开发时用 objdiff 比对目标文件。decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 12.10% 的代码已匹配。
requirements: README lists one supported version, G8MJ01 (Rev 0, JP); configure.py defines no other version and CI builds only G8MJ01. README still carries template leftovers: its badges point at another project, its clone command names NWPlayer123/G8MJ01-dtk and one line calls G8MJ01 the USA version. The output is a GameCube DOL and REL set, not a PC port.

Copy your own G8MJ01 disc image to orig/G8MJ01; ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ and TGC images are accepted. README says the repository contains no game assets or assembly: decomp-toolkit splits main.dol and the RELs using committed symbol and split tables, and extracts the memory-card icon and banner textures from the DOL into local headers. Decompiled sources such as src/pmario_sound.c also carry game data tables reconstructed as C.

Builds need Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (with wine-crossover) or Linux (an automatically downloaded wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.8.3, objdiff v3.7.1, binutils 2.42-2, sjiswrap v1.2.2, wibo 1.1.0 and the 20260305 compiler bundle, using Metrowerks GC/2.6 for game and REL code and GC/1.2.5n for the Dolphin SDK. tools/ttydasm is a Rust helper that decodes a named event script from the linked DOL or REL outputs in build/G8MJ01.

Objects marked Matching (100 of 547 in configure.py) are compiled from source and the rest come from the split originals; the default ninja target checks the DOL and all RELs against config/G8MJ01/build.sha1 before reporting progress. CI builds G8MJ01 in a container that supplies the disc files and compilers and uploads a progress report. decomp.dev’s report for the pinned commit lists 457,800 of 3,784,980 code bytes (12.10%) and 2,029 of 9,770 functions matched, with 100 of 1,239 units complete; this collection ran no build.

The repository carries the MIT License (copyright NWPlayer123), and libs/musyx has its own MIT license; neither covers Nintendo’s game, disc contents or the downloaded compilers. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Awesome Frida
description_en: An awesome list of libraries, scripts, tools, talks and articles built on or about Frida, the dynamic instrumentation toolkit, started by David Weinstein in May 2016. Its 82 entries fall into libraries (about half of them NowSecure Node.js modules), script collections and projects, talks and papers, tools powered by Frida such as r2frida, objection, friTap and Fridump, videos, blog posts and community links, most with a one-line summary.
description_zh: David Weinstein 于 2016 年 5 月创建的 awesome 清单，收录基于或围绕动态插桩工具包 Frida 的程序库、脚本、工具、演讲和文章。全部 82 个条目分为程序库（约一半是 NowSecure 的 Node.js 模块）、脚本合集与项目、演讲与论文、基于 Frida 的工具（如 r2frida、objection、friTap 和 Fridump）、视频、博客文章以及社区链接，大多附有一行简介。
requirements: Reviewed at commit e20da3b (2026-04-10). 43 of 68 commits date from 2016–2017, most talks, videos and posts are from 2015–2017, and after the April 2023 addition of RoboDroid the only change is the April 2026 addition of rekit. Entries do not say which Frida version they target; frida-load is marked deprecated and the Lobotomy entries are struck through.

In an automated check at review, 13 of 110 unique URLs gave no response or a 404, including the OSDC, ZeroNights and RMLL event pages and a three-part tutorial series, and three talk PDFs are linked as relative files that are not in the repository. Of the 57 GitHub repositories linked, 4 are archived, 2 no longer exist and 13 have not been pushed to since 2019. The README asks contributors to flag listings that are unmaintained or have had no commits for two to three years.
Several listed tools dump process memory, decrypt protected apps or log TLS keys, and two posts cover detecting Frida; this record treats the list only as a directory of instrumentation resources.

The LICENSE file is CC0 1.0. The contribution guide, adapted from the general awesome-list guidelines, refers to a code of conduct and a list-creation guide that are not in the repository. Linked projects keep their own licenses. An independent discovery list; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: 3SX: a native Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike port continuing the PS2 decompilation
description_en: Builds Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike as native C for Windows, macOS and Linux, continuing the 3s-decomp PS2 decompilation, with SDL3 for video, input and audio and GekkoNet for rollback netplay. README stresses that it is neither a recompilation nor emulation. The port needs the player’s own PS2 game files and works toward arcade-accurate balance, which an optional Statcheck build tests against CPS3 RAM states recorded from Fightcade replays.
description_zh: 延续 3s-decomp 的 PS2 反编译成果，将《街头霸王 III：3rd Strike》构建为可在 Windows、macOS 和 Linux 上运行的原生 C 程序，以 SDL3 处理画面、输入和声音，以 GekkoNet 实现回滚联机。README 强调它既不是重编译，也不是模拟。移植版需要玩家自备 PS2 游戏文件，并以接近街机版的平衡性为目标；可选的 Statcheck 构建会用 Fightcade 对战录像中记录的 CPS3 内存状态来检验这一点。
requirements: README calls 3SX a native port and a continuation of 3s-decomp, explicitly neither a recompilation nor emulation. At the reviewed commit the game code under src/sf33rd has no remaining INCLUDE_ASM stubs, and src/port supplies SDL3 platform, input and sound layers, including its own ADX decoder. This is a modified port: its goals include fixing balance regressions the PS2 version introduced, and the arcade-balance option is marked work in progress. The only release is a rolling pre-release rebuilt from main, and goals such as stable PC play and the arcade ROM as sole dependency remain on the 1.0 milestone.

Play requires a legally obtained PS2 copy of Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike or Street Fighter Anniversary Collection: a startup wizard reads the user’s disc image, or SF33RD.AFS from it is placed in the resources folder, and release builds compare that file with a SHA-256 in resources.c. The arcade-balance option also needs the user’s sfiii3nr1.zip CPS3 ROM set. The tree ships no game archives, but src/bin2obj carries large C data tables from the decompilation.

Prebuilt rolling releases cover Windows, macOS, and x86_64 and arm64 Linux. Source builds use CMake 3.24+ with Clang, after MSYS2 MinGW64 packages on Windows, the listed Ubuntu packages or Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS; build-deps.sh fetches and builds SDL3, SDL_net, GekkoNet, libcdio, minizip-ng and TF-PSA-Crypto. CMake and CI also carry a PSP branch built with Docker tooling.

Pull-request CI only builds the Windows, macOS, Linux and PSP targets. Arcade accuracy is checked with the optional Statcheck build: tools/fcade-replays, described as a reverse-engineering helper for Fightcade’s replay stream, downloads replays; a custom FBNeo fork records per-frame CPS3 RAM dumps; and Statcheck stops at the first mismatch in health, positions, stun, super-art meter, timer or round phase. The reviewed tree publishes no Statcheck results, and this collection built or ran nothing.

The repository carries an agent skill with a Codex interface file. It directs a coding agent to compare local functions with a CPS3 program through a read-only Ghidra MCP server, mark each function’s parity and add CPS3 behaviour behind the arcade-balance flag; the reviewed files do not say how much code was written this way, and no REA use is established. LICENSE is AGPL-3.0. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES lists GPLv3+ libcdio with zlib, BSD-2-Clause, MIT and Apache-2.0 components, the game and its assets keep their own rights, and README says the project does not condone piracy.

name: re4: a byte-identical decompilation of the Resident Evil 4 GameCube debug build
description_en: Reconstructs C and C++ source for the two-disc Resident Evil 4 GameCube debug prototype (G4BE08) and rebuilds main.dol and all 114 REL overlays with the compilers the README names, checking every output against a SHA-1 list. Function names are Capcom’s own from the debug build’s Bio4.sym files, and most struct and field names are aligned from the PS2 debug build’s debug information. The project’s research log says AI agents did the matching work; byte identity is project-reported.
description_zh: 为 Resident Evil 4 的双光盘 GameCube 调试原型版（G4BE08）重建 C 与 C++ 源码，并用 README 所列编译器重新构建 main.dol 及全部 114 个 REL 覆盖模块，逐一与 SHA-1 清单比对。函数名沿用调试版 Bio4.sym 符号文件中 Capcom 自己的命名，多数结构体与字段名则依据 PS2 调试版的调试信息对齐得出。项目的研究日志称一致性工作由 AI 智能体完成；字节一致为项目报告的结果。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-10-02 head, under four weeks after the first commit of 2026-09-07. README calls the decompilation complete: every unit compiles to the original bytes, src/ holds about 570,000 lines of C and C++ with no assembly files, and 526 `// COMPILER-DIFF:` spots coax the compiler’s register or instruction choices without emitting code. Nearly all remaining inline assembly is in routines the vendors also wrote in assembly. The output is the debug prototype’s DOL and RELs, not a retail build or PC port.

Supply your own images of both debug discs in orig/G4BE08/: disc 1 provides main.dol and most RELs, disc 2 the four island-stage RELs, and configure.py also reads the matching Bio4 symbol files from them. The game code’s compiler is built from SN Systems’ GPL source release of its ProDG 3.9.3 GCC port, which the user also supplies. The repository contains no game assets.

The documented host is Linux with Python 3 and ninja. tools/sn-gcc/build.sh builds SN’s GCC 2.95.3 (SN BUILD v1.79) natively once with the project’s Linux-host and memory-flag patches; CRI middleware builds with Metrowerks CodeWarrior 2.4.7 and the Nintendo SDK, taken from dolsdk2004, with GC/1.2.5n. The first configure run downloads pinned decomp-toolkit, objdiff, wibo and CodeWarrior compiler releases.

A successful build should end with ninja reporting 100% matched and linked, and dtk shasum against config/G4BE08/build.sha1 should print OK for all 115 binaries; tools/bytecmp.py compares single units and tools/asmcheck.py --all counts instructions emitted from asm templates, a total changes must not alter. The repository has no CI workflow or release, so these results are project-reported, and this collection built nothing.

LICENSE applies CC0 only to the project’s build scripts, tools, configuration and documentation. README and LICENSE state that the reconstructed game, SDK and middleware source in src/ and include/ remains the property of Capcom, Nintendo and CRI Middleware and is published for research and preservation only. docs/research/README.md describes its matching notes as written by the AI agents that did the matching work; no REA use is documented.

name: Super Smash Bros. Brawl: an early matching Wii decompilation
description_en: A work-in-progress matching decompilation of Super Smash Bros. Brawl that targets the USA Rev 2 Wii release (RSBE01_02), splitting main.dol and 126 REL modules from a user-supplied disc image and checking the rebuilt binaries against stored SHA-1 values. objdiff compares objects during development, and six other regional revisions are listed but commented out of the supported set. decomp.dev reported 1.27% of code matched at the reviewed commit.
description_zh: 《任天堂明星大乱斗X》（Super Smash Bros. Brawl）的进行中一致性反编译，目标为美版 Rev 2 Wii 版本（RSBE01_02）：从使用者自备的光盘镜像中拆分 main.dol 和 126 个 REL 模块，并按仓库保存的 SHA-1 校验重建出的二进制。开发时用 objdiff 比对目标文件；另外六个地区修订版虽已列出，但在支持列表中被注释掉。decomp.dev 报告所审提交有 1.27% 的代码已匹配。
requirements: README lists one supported version, RSBE01_02 (USA Rev 2), with the Japan, USA Rev 1, PAL and Korea revisions commented out; configure.py names all seven, but only RSBE01_02 has a configuration and CI builds only it. The output is a Wii main.dol and REL set, not a PC port.

Copy your own disc image to orig/RSBE01_02; ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ and TGC images are accepted. README says the repository contains no game assets or assembly: decomp-toolkit splits the DOL and RELs using committed per-module symbol and split tables, and extracts one embedded binary (HomeBtnIcon) from the DOL locally. Game headers come from the BrawlHeaders submodule (Sammi-Husky/BrawlHeaders), which README says to initialize before building.

Builds need Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (with wine-crossover) or Linux (an automatically downloaded wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.7.5, objdiff v3.4.4, binutils 2.42-1, sjiswrap v1.2.2, wibo 1.0.0 and the 20250812 compiler bundle, compiling and linking with Metrowerks GC/3.0a5.2.

Objects marked Matching (184 in configure.py; 20 remain NonMatching) are compiled from source and the rest come from the split originals; the default ninja target checks main.dol and the RELs against config/RSBE01_02/build.sha1 before reporting progress. CI builds RSBE01_02 in a container that supplies the disc files and compilers and uploads a progress report. decomp.dev’s report for the pinned commit lists 201,252 of 15,833,548 code bytes (1.27%) and 2,504 of 92,523 functions matched, with 516 of 4,415 units complete; this collection ran no build.

The repository carries CC0-1.0; Nintendo’s game, disc contents and the downloaded compilers fall outside that dedication, and the BrawlHeaders submodule declares no license on GitHub. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: re-plants-vs-zombies: decompiling and modernizing Plants vs. Zombies GOTY
description_en: Reconstructs C++ source for Plants vs. Zombies on PopCap’s open-source SexyAppFramework, starting from an earlier community decompilation of version 0.9.9 and adding functionality reversed from the Game of the Year edition, with functions annotated by GOTY addresses. The project also modernizes the engine with current C++ and is replacing the DirectDraw and Direct3D 7 renderers with GLFW. It builds a fan executable that runs from an original game folder, aiming at a modernized, extensible game rather than an identical binary.
description_zh: 以 PopCap 开源的 SexyAppFramework 为基础重建 Plants vs. Zombies 的 C++ 源码：起点是社区早先对 0.9.9 版的反编译，再补入从年度版（GOTY）逆向得到的功能，并以 GOTY 版地址标注函数。项目同时以现代 C++ 改造引擎，并正将 DirectDraw 与 Direct3D 7 渲染器替换为 GLFW。它构建出在原版游戏目录中运行的同人可执行文件，目标是现代化、可扩展的游戏，而不是完全一致的二进制。
requirements: README describes decompiling the latest functionality of the first PvZ title and expanding the game and its engine, building on a since-deleted 0.9.9 decompilation by Miya (rspforhp) that it credits ruslan831 with archiving. Its roadmap marks x64 support and achievements as partial, the GLFW renderer and cross-platform replacements as in progress, and Zombatar and a modding API as not done. There are no releases; the last commit is dated 2026-07-11.

Playing needs the original game files from a purchased copy; README links the Steam Game of the Year Edition but names no exact executable version. The built executable is run from that game folder, and the audio code loads bass.dll or fmod.dll at runtime instead of linking a committed copy. README says the repository includes no PopCap IP beyond the open-source engine; Resources.cpp/.h reconstruct the game’s generated resource-ID tables, data derived from the game as is usual for such projects.

Builds use CMake 3.16+ and C++23. README documents Visual Studio Community, whose CMakeSettings.json has x86 and x64 MSVC configurations, or CMake with Ninja; toolchain.cmake cross-compiles with x86_64-w64-mingw32 Clang and windres. The reviewed build produces a Windows executable, and the repository has no CI workflow.

The sources document no tests, CI or comparison with the original executable; contributors annotate reversed functions and class members with their GOTY addresses. Fidelity to the original game is not measured, and this collection built or ran nothing.

LICENSE dedicates the repository under CC0 1.0. The SexyAppFramework code derives from the engine PopCap made public, but PopCap’s license text is not included; the ogg code keeps Xiph.org’s BSD-style notice, and the FMOD 3 (Firelight, 1999–2002) and BASS 2.4 (Un4seen, 1999–2022) API headers keep their vendors’ copyrights. The original game and its files keep their rights holders’ terms. README says the project does not condone piracy; the reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Awesome Ghidra
description_en: An awesome list of Ghidra scripts, plugins, extensions, learning materials and related services, kept by the Allsafe GitHub organization since December 2019. Its 49 entries comprise 36 scripts and extensions, from malware-analysis and crypto-constant finders to Go, JNI, EVM and EFI helpers, Python and Jupyter bridges, P-code emulation and patch-diff correlators; 10 books, talks and courses; and three related projects such as r2ghidra-dec and Ghidraaas, each with a one-line summary.
description_zh: 由 GitHub 组织 Allsafe 自 2019 年 12 月起维护的 awesome 清单，收录 Ghidra 脚本、插件、扩展、学习资料和相关服务。全部 49 个条目包括 36 个脚本与扩展，从恶意软件分析和加密常量查找工具，到 Go、JNI、EVM 和 EFI 辅助工具、Python 与 Jupyter 桥接、P-code 模拟以及补丁对比关联器；10 份书籍、演讲和课程资料；以及 r2ghidra-dec、Ghidraaas 等 3 个相关项目，每项附一行简介。
requirements: Reviewed at commit 9265b2f (2026-06-18). 42 of 53 commits date from 2019–2021; after that gap the maintainers merged four contributor pull requests in June 2026, adding entries such as the printf-inliner plugin, 0xdea's scripts, IDAObjcTypes and GhidrAI. Entries name no Ghidra versions, GhidrAI is the only AI-assisted entry, and no MCP server is listed.

Entries give a link and a one-line summary with no license or maintenance information. Of the 42 GitHub repositories linked, 1 is archived and 17 have not been pushed to since 2021, so each project's Ghidra compatibility must be checked at its source; in an automated check at review only the OOAnalyzer plugin path returned a 404.

Five entries are the maintaining organization's own scripts and tools. The Materials section includes a Japanese-language practical guide, the NSA's GhidraClass course material in the Ghidra repository, conference talks and The Ghidra Book.

GitHub detects no license and the repository has no license file or contribution guide, so the list states no reuse terms; linked projects keep their own licenses. An independent discovery list; the reviewed source establishes no REA connection.

name: Sonic Advance 1 & 2: a matching GBA decompilation with widescreen ports
description_en: Reconstructs Sonic Advance and Sonic Advance 2 for the Game Boy Advance as C that rebuilds six hash-listed ROMs with SAT-R’s agbcc fork, and compiles the same code into widescreen SDL ports for Linux, macOS and Windows plus PSP and PS2 builds. README reports Sonic Advance 2 built entirely from C with about 60 functions still non-matching. Extracted graphics, music and data are committed, so the builds read no original ROM.
description_zh: 将 Game Boy Advance 版《索尼克 Advance》和《索尼克 Advance 2》重建为 C 源码，借助 SAT-R 的 agbcc 分支重新构建六个列有哈希值的 ROM，同一套代码还可编译为面向 Linux、macOS 和 Windows 的宽屏 SDL 移植版，以及 PSP 和 PS2 版本。README 报告《索尼克 Advance 2》已全部由 C 构建，仍有约 60 个函数不一致。提取出的图像、音乐和数据都提交在仓库中，因此构建时不读取原 ROM。
requirements: README marks the project unfinished and under active development. It lists six ROM targets with SHA-1 values: Sonic Advance (Europe) and Sonic Advance 2 (USA, Europe, Japan, Japanese Virtual Console and a 2002-10-25 USA beta). README reports that SA2 builds 100% from C with about 60 non-matching functions pulled in from asm/non_matching, which at the reviewed commit holds 64 SA2, 99 SA1, 17 shared and 8 engine files, and that over 600 SA2 functions are unnamed. The Tiny Chao Garden and Collect Rings multiboot sub-games are built for matching and only partly decompiled.

The documented builds read no original ROM. The tree commits over 12,000 PNG sprite frames and tiles, 474 MIDI songs, tilemaps and other raw data, including a 191 KB data file included piecewise into the Tiny Chao Garden multiboot ROM. Port CI jobs still download a base ROM from private storage, which the Makefile does not reference.

INSTALL.md targets Linux (with WSL for Windows users) and macOS: ARM GCC and binutils, libpng, SDL2 and MinGW-w64, plus mkisofs or cdrtools for PS2. Matching GBA builds need SAT-R’s agbcc fork built and installed into the tree. Ports build with make sdl (Linux/macOS), sdl_win32 (Windows), sdl_psp (PSPDEV) and ps2 (PS2DEV) at a 426×240 widescreen resolution; README marks the Win32 OpenGL target not functional, and no GitHub release is published.

On the GBA platform, make runs a SHA-1 check of the built ROM against its listed hash. CI checks formatting, then builds and hash-checks SA2 USA, SA1 Europe and the four other SA2 variants; it also builds SDL, Win32, PSP and PS2 port targets for both games on Ubuntu and macOS, and replays a committed any% speedrun input recording through a headless SDL build. Matching applies to the GBA ROMs, not to the widescreen ports, and this collection built nothing.

The repository has no license file and GitHub detects none. The extracted graphics, music and data, and the Nintendo SDK libraries rebuilt in libagbsyscall, m4a and agb_flash, keep their rights holders’ terms. README sets a strict no-LLM/no-AI policy for issues and pull requests; the reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Paleblood: a functional decompilation of Bloodborne with its own runtime
description_en: Rewrites code from Bloodborne’s PS4 executable (CUSA03173 with update 1.09) as readable C++, one function at a time, aiming at a native PC source port on a clean-room runtime of its own. It is a functional rather than matching decompilation: each replacement is hooked in, compared with the original machine code on recorded and generated inputs, and independently reviewed. Work is at an early stage: README reports 21 of 157,757 functions verified, and the game does not yet run on Paleblood’s own runtime.
description_zh: 将 Bloodborne PS4 可执行文件（CUSA03173，含 1.09 更新）的代码逐个函数改写为可读的 C++，目标是在项目以净室方式自行编写的运行时上实现原生 PC 源码移植。它追求功能等价而非字节一致：每个替换函数都以钩子接入，在录制与生成的输入上与原始机器码对照比较，再经独立审核。项目仍处早期：README 报告 157,757 个函数中已验证 21 个，游戏尚不能在 Paleblood 自己的运行时上运行。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-10-19 head, 12 days after the first commit. The generated status reports 31 functions replaced and 21 verified out of a 157,757-function Ghidra export; the project’s loader maps the executable, and its boot stops at the first unimplemented system call with 247 of 686 system imports implemented. Replacements cover parts of the frame loop and the event, kernel, input, AI, character, physics and render layers, and BB_TARGET_FPS reproduces three community frame-rate patches in code.

Requires Bloodborne CUSA03173 (EU) with the 1.09 update, dumped from the user’s own PS4; the executables converted from it must match target.sha256. README says the repository holds no game code, assets, binaries, decompiler output or extracted data, a check rejects game data in the pre-commit hook and CI, and the project does not provide or point to game files, pkgs, firmware, keys or decryption tools.

Development is documented on Linux with CMake 3.20+ and CTest, plus Ghidra 12.0.3 with the GhidraOrbis loader for analysis. Full game runs still use an external scaffold: third_party/bbport, the project’s fork of the GPL-2.0-or-later bloodborne_pc port, which runs the original executable natively with shadPS4-derived Vulkan rendering. CI does not fetch that submodule.

README says tools/verify.py runs the original code and a replacement side by side, comparing return values, registers, every byte written and every library call, and that deliberately wrong versions must fail; options that replace a community patch are checked against the original with that patch applied. CI builds with GCC and Clang and runs unit, harness and policy checks without game data, so verification against the game is contributor-run and project-reported; this collection ran nothing.

GPL-2.0-or-later per LICENSE; the bbport scaffold has its own GPL-2.0-or-later notice, which README says grants no right in the game or its code. README calls Paleblood a fan project unaffiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or FromSoftware and describes the runtime as clean-room. CONTRIBUTING.md allows disclosed, verified AI-assisted work, and recent commits carry Co-Authored-By trailers naming Claude Opus 5.5 and Codex; no REA use is documented.

name: Pikmin 2: a fully matched GameCube decompilation across five releases
description_en: A fan decompilation of Pikmin 2 that rebuilds main.dol for five GameCube releases (USA retail, two USA demos, PAL and Japan) with the original Metrowerks compilers, checking each against a stored SHA-1. The build reads main.dol from the user’s own copy of each release. decomp.dev reported all code matched and fully linked for every version at the reviewed commit, and a non-matching mode builds the US DOL entirely from C++ for modding.
description_zh: 由爱好者进行的《皮克敏2》反编译项目：用原版 Metrowerks 编译器为五个 GameCube 版本（美版零售版、两个美版体验版、PAL 版和日版）重建 main.dol，并逐一与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。构建读取使用者自有各版本中的 main.dol。decomp.dev 报告所审提交中各版本的代码均已全部匹配并完全链接；另有非一致性模式，可完全由 C++ 源码构建美版 DOL 以供模组制作。
requirements: README still calls this a work-in-progress decompilation and lists five supported versions: GPVE01 (USA retail, the default), GPVE01_D17 and GPVE01_D18 (USA demos 17 and 18), GPVP01 (PAL) and GPVJ01 (Japan). Each has its own configuration and SHA-1 file, and CI builds all five. Outputs are GameCube DOLs, not a PC executable or port.

Each version needs main.dol from the user’s own copy of that release at orig/<version>/sys/main.dol, and decomp-toolkit checks it against the hash in that version’s config.yml before splitting. The repository commits game-derived symbol and split tables for every version; config comments say the GPVE01 symbols were generated from a pikmin2UP.MAP linker map and the Japanese and PAL tables were recovered from those DOLs using the US symbols. No disc images or extracted game files are included.

Builds need Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (with wine-crossover) or Linux (an automatically downloaded wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.7.5, objdiff v3.4.1, binutils 2.42-1, sjiswrap v1.2.2, wibo 1.0.0-beta.5 and the 20250812 compiler bundle, using Metrowerks GC/2.6 for game, JSystem and runtime code and GC/1.2.5n for the Dolphin SDK libraries.

configure.py marks 1,154 objects Matching for every supported version and one more for Japan only; none is NonMatching. The default ninja target checks the linked DOL against config/<version>/build.sha1 before reporting progress, and CI builds all five versions in a container that supplies the original files and compilers. decomp.dev’s reports for the pinned commit list 100.00% of code matched and fully linked for each version (24,957 functions and 1,153 units for GPVE01); this collection ran no build.

With --non-matching, README says the final hash check is disabled and the US DOL builds completely from C++ source that is, to the team’s knowledge, functionally equivalent, so every file can be edited for modding. The repository carries CC0-1.0 in LICENSE.MD; Nintendo’s game, its files and the downloaded compilers fall outside that dedication. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Gran Turismo 4: an agent-assisted PS2 engine matching decompilation
description_en: Decompiles Gran Turismo 4’s PS2 engine executable (CORE.GT4, NTSC-U v1.01) into one C or C++ source per function for Sony’s ee-gcc 2.96, matching public libraries such as newlib and Expat from their own source.
