The README credits AI agents (Anthropic’s Claude) driving the project’s tools with most of the matching, each function accepted only on a compiler-and-judge comparison, and reports 95.4% of functions and 83.6% of code bytes matched for an October 2026 commit. A local full build links sources at their original addresses, fills the rest from disassembly and compares SHA-1 with the user’s executable.
description_zh: 将 Gran Turismo 4（《GT 赛车 4》）的 PS2 引擎可执行文件（CORE.GT4，NTSC-U v1.01）按每个函数一个 C 或 C++ 源文件反编译，面向 Sony 的 ee-gcc 2.96，并用 newlib、Expat 等公开库自身的源码匹配其函数。README 称大部分匹配工作由驱动项目工具的 AI 智能体（Anthropic 的 Claude）完成，每个函数须通过编译器与判定器的比对才算完成，并报告 2026 年 10 月某次提交时 95.4% 的函数和 83.6% 的代码字节已匹配。本地完整构建将源码链接到原始地址，其余部分用反汇编补齐，再与使用者的可执行文件比较 SHA-1。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress matching decompilation of the engine executable only: most game logic lives in Adhoc scripts, which the separate OpenAdhoc project re-creates, and the separate GT4 Native PC port is described as not playable. The progress-branch report for commit ba5d800 (2026-10-19), which decomp.dev also shows for the reviewed commit, gives 29,551 of 30,962 functions and 83.55% of code matched, 82.08% of code linked from source and 2.13% of data placed from source; 202 hand-written assembly functions are not counted.

Supply your own Gran Turismo 4 (USA) v1.01 disc image (SCUS-97328); orig/README.md lists SHA-1 values for SCUS_973.28, CORE.GT4 and the ELF converted from it. Nothing from the game is committed, so the SHA-1 build check and the progress reports run only where those files are present, not in CI.

Documented for Linux or WSL (Ubuntu) with Python 3.11+ and rabbitizer. tools/setup_linux.sh installs MIPS binutils and 32-bit libc, downloads decomp.me’s ee-gcc 2.96 build, clones decomp-permuter and installs splat in a virtual environment; project.toml names further decomp.me compilers, including ee-gcc 2.9 for about 270 Sony SDK functions.

A function counts as matched when tools/match.py (or the agents’ tools/swarm.py) prints MATCH, and tools/build.py links every function at its original address and compares SHA-1 of the loaded segments. CI runs unit tests, an assembly-in-C policy check and layout checks and compiles every source, but cannot link or compare without the game; matching figures are author-reported, and this collection built or ran nothing.

MIT for the project’s tools, documentation and source. THIRD_PARTY.md lists matched public libraries under their own terms (Expat, newlib, GNU libio and the GCC runtime under GPL with exceptions, SGI STL headers, MT19937), which build.py --without can leave out, and records proprietary SCE-RT/Medius, Logitech and Sony SDK code as identified but not copied. Gran Turismo 4 belongs to Sony Interactive Entertainment. Agent instructions are in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/; the reviewed sources establish no REA use.

name: Mario Kart Wii: an in-progress matching decompilation of the PAL release
description_en: A work-in-progress matching decompilation of Mario Kart Wii that targets the PAL release (RMCP01), rebuilding main.dol and the StaticR.rel module from C and C++ with Metrowerks compilers and checking both against stored SHA-1 values. The build splits these binaries from a user-supplied disc image, and objdiff compares objects during development. The README’s progress badges point to a decomp.dev page that did not resolve at review, and the default branch was last updated in September 2025.
description_zh: 《马力欧卡丁车 Wii》的进行中一致性反编译，目标为 PAL 版（RMCP01）：用 Metrowerks 编译器从 C 与 C++ 源码重建 main.dol 和 StaticR.rel 模块，并与仓库保存的 SHA-1 比对。构建从使用者自备的光盘镜像中拆分这些二进制，开发时用 objdiff 比对目标文件。README 的进度徽章指向的 decomp.dev 页面在审阅时无法访问，默认分支最后更新于 2025 年 9 月。
requirements: README lists one supported version, RMCP01 (PAL); configure.py defines no other and CI builds only RMCP01. The repository was renamed from riidefi/mkw, which README’s badges and clone command still use, and CONTRIBUTING.md and HACK.md still describe an earlier mkwutil and ppcdis build layout that the pinned tree no longer contains. The output is a Wii main.dol and StaticR.rel, not a PC port.

Copy your own RMCP01 disc image to orig/RMCP01; ISO (GCM), RVZ, WIA, WBFS, CISO, NFS, GCZ and TGC images are accepted, and config.yml records the expected SHA-1 of both binaries. README says the repository contains no game assets or assembly; decomp-toolkit splits main.dol and StaticR.rel locally using the committed, game-derived symbol and split tables.

Builds need Python and ninja on Windows (native tooling recommended), macOS (with wine-crossover) or Linux (an automatically downloaded wibo on x86, Wine elsewhere). configure.py pins decomp-toolkit v1.3.0, objdiff v2.4.0, binutils 2.42-1, sjiswrap v1.2.0, wibo 0.6.16 and the 20240706 compiler bundle, using Metrowerks Wii/0x4201_127 for the game, NW4R, EGG, RFL and MSL code and as the linker, and GC/3.0a5.2 for the Revolution SDK, TRK, DWC and GameSpy libraries.

Objects marked Matching (106 of the 213 listed in configure.py; 105 NonMatching, 2 Equivalent) are compiled from source and the rest of each binary comes from the split originals; the default ninja target checks main.dol and StaticR.rel against config/RMCP01/build.sha1 before reporting progress. CI builds RMCP01 in a private container holding the original files and uploads a progress report. decomp.dev had no report for the repository under either name at review, so no completion figure is cited; this collection ran no build.

The repository carries CC0-1.0; lib/gamespy keeps the GameSpy SDK’s own BSD-style license from IGN Entertainment, and Nintendo’s game, disc contents and the downloaded compilers keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Pinyon Shift: a ShiftGlue static recompilation of Forza Horizon for PC
description_en: Builds a native port of the Xbox 360 release of Forza Horizon by translating its PowerPC executable ahead of time into C++ with ShiftGlue, the author’s fork of ReXGlue, and compiling it on the player’s machine from their own disc. A renderer written for this game runs its GPU commands on Vulkan, and some translated library code, such as FMOD Ex DSP units, is replaced by independently written native code checked against the translated original. README presents it as a playable preview with rendering bugs and slowdowns.
description_zh: 使用作者对 ReXGlue 的分支 ShiftGlue，将 Xbox 360 版 Forza Horizon 的 PowerPC 可执行文件提前转换为 C++，并依玩家自有光盘在其电脑上编译，构建原生移植版。专为该游戏编写的渲染器在 Vulkan 上执行其 GPU 命令；部分转换后的库代码（如 FMOD Ex 的 DSP 单元）由独立编写、并与转换后原版对照检查的原生代码替代。README 称其为可游玩的预览版，仍有渲染错误和卡顿。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026-10-17 head, tagged v0.6.0; the repository was created on 2026-08-25. It holds the launcher, build tools, host code and configuration, and README says it contains no game, assets, generated translations or prebuilt executable; the v0.6.0 Windows launcher archive holds only the launcher and a source archive. This is static recompilation with native replacements, not recovered authored source.

Requires an ISO dumped from the user’s own USA retail disc (serial MS-2505, title ID 4D5309C9) or an unmodified folder extracted from it; setup checks its exact size and SHA-256 against config/supported-dumps.json and rejects unknown dumps. Owned DLC packages are verified before import, and the Rally and 1000 Club add-ons need the optional title update v4 build.

Players need Windows 10/11 x64, x86-64 Linux including SteamOS, or macOS 13+ on Apple silicon, with a Vulkan 1.3 GPU; NVIDIA is tested, while AMD and Intel are not yet qualified. The launcher installs pinned build tools and builds the game locally, which takes 20–60 minutes and about 30 GB the first time; the Windows source path needs Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools 17.1+. An Android 13+ arm64 build is a developer alpha cross-compiled on the PC.

CI checks the repository boundary, runs release-tooling and host tests, builds the launchers and cross-builds the Android runtime, all without the game. Scripted render-test routes, golden frame replays and README’s performance figures, such as a 119 fps median at 1x on an RTX 4080, come from the project’s local runs; this collection built or ran nothing.

BSD-3-Clause covers only independently authored material. docs/LEGAL.md says it grants no rights to Forza Horizon, Xbox software, ReXGlue or user-supplied content, and bars committing generated translations, hand translations of disassembly or decompiler output, and data copied from the executable. README states no affiliation with Microsoft, Xbox, Turn 10 Studios or Playground Games. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md agent instructions bar AI attribution in commits; the sources state no other AI or REA use.

name: Touhou 7: reconstructing Perfect Cherry Blossom 1.00b source
description_en: Reconstructs C++ source for the Windows executable of Touhou 7: Perfect Cherry Blossom 1.00b and its custom.exe configuration tool, built with the original Visual Studio .NET 2002 and DirectX 8 toolchain and compared function by function with the user’s originals through reccmp. The committed progress badges report th07.exe fully implemented at 99.78% accuracy and custom.exe fully matched. The README says the game should be fully playable, but a matching build trips the game’s integrity check, and the cross-platform ports live on separate branches.
description_zh: 为 Touhou 7：东方妖妖梦 1.00b 版的 Windows 可执行文件及其 custom.exe 设置工具重建 C++ 源码，使用原版 Visual Studio .NET 2002 与 DirectX 8 工具链构建，并通过 reccmp 与使用者自备的原程序逐函数比较。仓库内的进度徽章报告 th07.exe 已全部实现、准确率 99.78%，custom.exe 已完全匹配。README 称游戏应可完整游玩，但匹配构建会触发游戏自身的完整性检查；跨平台移植位于其他分支。
requirements: README calls this a work-in-progress matching decompilation of th07.exe 1.00b and custom.exe; the committed, mutable badges report 694 of 694 th07.exe functions implemented at 99.78% accuracy, and custom.exe at 100% for both. Behaviour is meant to match the original but may differ. The portable and reallyportable branches (desktop, mobile and web ports) are separate and not covered here. README credits the GensokyoClub th06 and th08 decompilations for shared types, names and code.

Supply your own th07.exe 1.00b (README gives its MD5, reccmp-project.yml its SHA-256), copied to resources/, for icon extraction and as reccmp’s comparison base; custom.exe is needed only for the configuration tool, and --no-icon builds without either. No game executable or game data files are committed; resources/csv holds the function, global, string and float tables reccmp uses.

This branch builds only for 32-bit Windows with the MSVC 2002 toolchain, run under Wine on Linux, and needs uv and ninja. scripts/download_deps.py fetches Visual Studio .NET 2002 and the DirectX 8 SDK from archive.org and EstexNT’s var_order compiler patch from a gist; scripts/build.py generates and runs the ninja build.

Contributors diff with reccmp, which reports per-function accuracy against the original as an HTML page or for one address. Because th07.exe is not yet byte-identical, README says a matching build fails the game’s integrity check and crashes after 3,999 Supervisor cycles; --no-matching disables that check. The repository has no CI; badge figures are project-generated, and this collection built or ran nothing.

CC0 1.0 for the repository; the game and the downloaded Microsoft toolchain and SDK keep their own terms. resources/svgicon.png, embedded in the progress badge, is the game’s cover artwork marked © 2003 Team Shanghai Alice, which the CC0 dedication does not cover. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: DKC1Recomp: static recompilation of Donkey Kong Country
description_en: Statically recompiles the North American v1.0 SNES release of Donkey Kong Country into native Windows, macOS and iOS applications with a pinned fork of snesrecomp, which translates 65816 code to C and links it against a modelled SNES hardware runtime. Function boundaries, entry flag states and jump-table targets are ingested from a byte-identical community disassembly instead of discovered heuristically, and the game code is generated locally from the user’s verified ROM. Optional widescreen, CRT filters, MSU-1 music and a Dixie Kong Country variant are host-side additions to what the README calls a playable bring-up.
description_zh: 借助固定版本的 snesrecomp 分支，将 SNES 版《大金刚国度》北美 v1.0 静态重编译为 Windows、macOS 与 iOS 原生程序；该框架把 65816 代码转译为 C，并链接到模拟 SNES 硬件的运行时。函数边界、入口标志状态与跳转表目标均取自一份逐字节一致的社区反汇编，而非靠启发式发现；游戏代码在本地由使用者经校验的 ROM 生成。可选的宽屏、CRT 滤镜、MSU-1 音乐和 Dixie Kong Country 变体都是宿主端附加功能，README 称这一移植处于可游玩的初步运行阶段。
requirements: Reviewed at the main commit tagged v0.0.14 (2026-09-15); releases v0.0.15 to v0.0.17 (through 2026-09-19) are tagged on commits that are not on main. README reports a playable bring-up with fully statically generated game code, a headless validation host and Windows, macOS and iOS hosts. Widescreen, on by default in the desktop host, fails closed to stock output or black margins where a scene is unproven; the generated widescreen coverage report lists 252 of 256 level entrances as never observed, and the Dixie variant is not validated over the full game.

Supply your own headerless Donkey Kong Country (USA) v1.0 ROM of 4 MiB, checked against the SHA-256 in the README; other images are rejected unless a single audited data-only edit is pinned by its hash. The optional Baby Kong mod also verifies the user’s own North American DKC3 ROM in memory. README states that no ROM bytes, extracted assets or generated game code are committed; the Dixie variant embeds the hack author’s public IPS patch, which the project records as a deliberate exception applied only to the verified clean ROM.

A source build initializes the snesrecomp submodule and runs scripts/generate_snesrecomp.py against the ROM, writing C into the git-ignored generated/ directory; recomp/*.cfg holds only names, addresses and structural metadata from the GPL-3 Yoshifanatic1 disassembly. Windows builds need Windows 10/11 x64, Visual Studio 2022 C++ tools, Python 3, Git, CMake, Ninja and an OpenGL 3.3 GPU; the arm64 macOS app targets macOS 26 with CMake, Ninja and SDL2, and the iOS sideload IPA needs iOS/iPadOS 16 or newer and re-signing for the recipient’s device.

Verification is deterministic tooling rather than a matching build: a headless host with input playback, replayable flight-recorder bundles, save-state continuity checks, route recipes and regression contracts, plus C and Python model tests, many of which need the private ROM. The reviewed tree has no CI workflow; the bring-up log reports nine private boot replays and inspection of the live window for the v0.0.10 Windows host. This collection built and ran nothing.

Project host and tooling code is MIT; the pinned snesrecomp fork is under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, the cfg metadata keeps its GPL-3 provenance, the Windows package adds SDL 2.30.9 (zlib) and miniz 3.0.2 (MIT), and Nintendo and Rare keep their game rights. AGENTS.md sets operating rules for Codex and other coding agents working in the repository; no REA use is established, and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: San Andreas Unity: a GTA San Andreas engine reimplementation in Unity
description_en: Reimplements the Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas engine in Unity (C#), loading the archives, RenderWare models and textures, collision, animations, audio, text and item definitions from the user’s own PC installation. README says it will not be a complete reimplementation; it focuses on gameplay features, multiplayer and a framework for extending and modding the game through C# plugins. Development has stalled: the newest commit on any branch dates from 2022-09-30.
description_zh: 在 Unity（C#）中重新实现《侠盗猎车手：圣安地列斯》的引擎，从使用者自有的 PC 版安装中读取归档、RenderWare 模型与纹理、碰撞、动画、音频、文本和物品定义。README 表示这不会是完整的重新实现，重点在于游戏玩法、多人模式，以及可通过 C# 插件扩展和改装游戏的框架。项目开发已停滞：所有分支中最新的提交日期为 2022-09-30。
requirements: Reviewed at the head of the default dev branch, committed 2022-09-30; no branch has a later commit, GitHub records the last push on 2023-06-16 and the latest release is v4.0 (2022-05-24), so the project appears inactive. README says it will not be a complete reimplementation and focuses on gameplay, multiplayer and a moddable framework; Docs/TODO.md still lists work such as asynchronous geometry loading and unloading distant parts of the world. The reviewed files do not describe how the original engine was analysed.

Play requires a PC installation of GTA San Andreas that the user owns: on first start the game asks for its path, and config.json points the loaders at data files such as gta.dat, the vehicle, ped and default .ide files, handling.cfg, water.dat, carcols.dat and weapon.dat. The Android build needs those PC files copied to the device, about 5 GB according to the wiki, with the audio folder optional. The repository ships no game data; the NavMeshes submodule holds a precomputed navigation mesh, which the wiki says is generated from the imported game world because the original game has none.

Development uses Unity 2020.3.26 or newer (the project file names 2020.3.26f1), a recursive clone of the MirrorLite, UnityStandardAssets, NavMeshes, NetworkDiscoveryUnity and UGameCoreUtilities submodules and the Startup scene. README reports testing on Linux, Windows, macOS and Android with both Mono and IL2CPP backends; v4.0 provides Windows and Linux archives and an Android APK. Multiplayer runs as a dedicated server, host or client, and game modes load as C# DLL plugins.

There is no CI workflow or automated test suite for the importers or gameplay, and no comparison with the original executable is published. Evidence consists of README claims that multiplayer fully works, the v4.0 release notes, screenshots and videos; Docs/Performance.md records vertex and draw-call counts for one Las Venturas view. This collection did not build or run the project.

LICENSE is MIT with a 2015 copyright line for James King; the bundled NVorbis and Newtonsoft.Json DLLs and the submodules are separate projects under their own terms, and Rockstar’s game files keep their own rights. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: MinecraftLCE: an early-stage Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition decompilation
description_en: Decompiles Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition v1.0.17, a Legacy Console Edition release, into C++ that is compared function by function with the original executable using a patched Clang 4.0.1 and the open-ead Switch decompilation tools. The README explains the choice of the Switch build for its matchable Clang toolchain and type information, with names ported from the symbol-bearing Wii U Edition. At the reviewed commit the function list marks about 11% of functions decompiled, most of them matching; the result cannot run the game.
description_zh: 将 Legacy Console Edition 系列中的 Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition v1.0.17 反编译为 C++，借助打过补丁的 Clang 4.0.1 和 open-ead 的 Switch 反编译工具，与原可执行文件逐函数比较。README 解释了选用 Switch 版的原因：其 Clang 工具链可以匹配且带有类型信息，函数名则从带符号的 Wii U Edition 移植而来。所审提交时函数列表标记约 11% 的函数已反编译，其中大多已匹配；产物无法运行游戏。
requirements: README describes a work-in-progress decompilation of Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition v1.0.17 that cannot be used to play the game. At the reviewed commit data/mcswitch_functions.csv lists 57,972 functions: 6,279 matching, 224 non-matching and 51,469 not yet decompiled, the 11.217% that a workflow writes into the GitHub description. Matched functions are checked individually; there is no whole-executable rebuild.

Supply the main NSO executable from your own Minecraft: Nintendo Switch Edition v1.0.17 update; the Wii U Edition’s Minecraft.Client.rpx (Patch 35, v560) is recommended only for porting symbols. README says these executables will never be provided in the repository and no game assets are included.

Documented for Linux or WSL (with macOS also intended): Python 3.6+, Ninja, CMake 3.13+, ccache, llvm-objdump, libncurses5, a Rust toolchain and the listed Python modules. tools/setup.py converts the executable, downloads Clang 4.0.1 from the LLVM releases and applies the committed libc++ patches; submodules supply open-ead’s nx-decomp-tools, nnheaders and musl and the stb image library, and lib/ vendors libpng and zlib.

tools/check compares compiled functions with the original and tools/common/progress.py summarises the function list. CI lints, compiles the project without the game and publishes progress counted from the committed function list, so matching status is project-reported; this collection built or ran nothing.

No license file is present and GitHub detects none; Minecraft belongs to Microsoft and Mojang, and vendored libraries keep their own licenses. README says Microsoft-licensed Java Edition mappings cannot be used and notes that projects whose research was not clean-room have been taken down. The reviewed sources establish no AI or REA use.

name: Final Fantasy VII: a matching PlayStation decompilation
description_en: Reconstructs C source for the US PlayStation release of Final Fantasy VII, aiming for code that compiles back to the original main executable and its game overlays. The build splits the user’s disc files with splat, compiles with period cc1-psx compilers and checks every rebuilt file against its SHA-1. A native build against the PsyZ PlayStation-library replacement is compiled in CI but is not documented as a playable port.
description_zh: 为 Final Fantasy VII 美版 PlayStation 发行版重建 C 源码，目标是让代码重新编译出原版主可执行文件及各游戏覆盖段（overlay）。构建流程用 splat 拆分使用者自备的光盘文件，以当年的 cc1-psx 编译器编译，并用 SHA-1 校验每个重建文件。基于 PsyZ（PlayStation 库替代实现）的原生构建会在 CI 中编译，但未作为可游玩的移植版加以说明。
requirements: The project describes itself as a matching decompilation of the PS1 game; config/us.yaml defines the single us version, covering SCUS_941.63 and battle, field, menu, world, minigame, magic and other overlays with 29 SHA-1 entries. Source tables such as the chocobo minigame’s arccosine table are data taken from the game, as is usual for such projects. README states no completion figure; CI uploads a progress report as a build artifact, and this collection recorded none.

Supply disc 1 of Final Fantasy VII (USA) as BIN/CUE under disks/; README lists the USA Interactive Sampler CD as optional, though the reviewed config builds only us. CONTRIBUTING says the repository includes no original game data and is not a playable or standalone version. CI fetches its disc images from a private dependency repository through a secret token.

README documents Debian/Ubuntu and Arch Linux with Go, Python 3 (a venv with splat64, spimdisasm and others), ninja, 7zip, bchunk and mipsel-linux-gnu binutils and GCC; CI notes that Ubuntu 24.04’s binutils 2.42 linker does not match the game. Make downloads the cc1-psx-26 and cc1-psx-272 compiler builds from the project’s init release and checks them against committed SHA-256 files; maspsx, m2c, asm-differ and PsyZ come in as submodules, and a Dockerfile is provided.

make build ends with a ninja rule running sha1sum -c over the expected hashes of every overlay. CI on the upstream repository checks formatting, runs that build, lints for overlapping symbols and compiles the PsyZ build. These checks compare file identity for the US release, not gameplay coverage, and this collection did not rerun them.

LICENSE is AGPL-3.0; the game discs, extracted data and downloaded compilers keep separate rights. README says the decompiled code is written by humans and rejects LLM-accelerated decompilation, while allowing LLMs for tooling, permuting hard functions or hunting runtime bugs; CONTRIBUTING forbids autonomously generated pull requests and commit messages. No REA use is documented and no runtime reproduction is claimed.

name: Mega Man X Recompiled: a snesrecomp static recompilation
description_en: Statically translates the 65816 CPU code of the SNES Mega Man X (USA Rev 1) to C with the snesrecomp framework; the PPU, audio, DMA and other hardware run in the framework’s runtime, and a LakeSnes-derived interpreter executes whatever the static pass cannot prove. The C is generated locally from the user’s ROM, with function names imported from community DiztinGUIsh annotations. Playable Zero, co-op and rollback netplay, X2/X3 boss weapons and adaptive widescreen are layered on top, using assets extracted locally from the user’s own sequel ROMs.
description_zh: 借助 snesrecomp 框架，将 SNES 版《洛克人 X》（美版 Rev 1）的 65816 CPU 代码静态转译为 C；PPU、音频、DMA 等硬件由框架运行时处理，静态分析无法证明的部分则交给源自 LakeSnes 的解释器执行。C 代码在本地由使用者的 ROM 生成，函数名取自社区的 DiztinGUIsh 注解。项目在此基础上加入可操作的 Zero、合作与回滚联机、X2／X3 的头目武器以及自适应宽屏，所用素材在本地从使用者自有的续作 ROM 中提取。
requirements: Reviewed at the main commit of release v2.2.9-alpha (2026-10-18), which offers a Windows ZIP and a Linux AppImage. The snesrecomp README lists the game as fully playable, and this README says the adaptive widescreen renderer was playtested through the ending on Windows. Execution is interpreter-first: compiled bodies replace only code the analysis proves, the rest stays interpreted, and Rockman X (Japan v1.1) is a separate variant that keeps its original view.

Supply your own Mega Man X (USA) Rev 1 ROM as .sfc or .smc, headered or not. Zero, co-op and the X3 weapons also need the user’s Mega Man X3 USA ROM, and the X2 weapons the Mega Man X2 USA ROM; their assets are extracted on the user’s machine. README states that ROMs, extracted assets and the generated src/gen C are neither committed nor in the downloads; the Saber Zero sprites and sounds from the Zashiko Mod are included with permission for non-commercial use.

Source builds clone the snesrecomp, recomp-ui and dizProjects submodules, stage the ROM and run tools/regen.sh, which emits per-bank C from recomp/bank*.cfg. CMake with Ninja and SDL3, or SDL2 as a fallback, is the maintained build: Windows 10+ through MSYS2 mingw64 with Python 3.9+ and rustup, Linux with gcc or clang, and macOS on Apple Silicon or Intel.

CI compiles ROM-free setup hosts and runs the ROM-free CTest regressions; ROM-backed state tests and a replay suite that stops at the first WRAM, co-op, camera or VRAM mismatch need the user’s ROMs. A dated coverage checkpoint reports two 12,000-frame routes matching the control build’s CPU and WRAM traces and final snapshots, without comparing audio, and the v2.2.9 release notes report Windows and Linux checks of all 28 Boss Rush pairs. This collection ran none of them.

The project and the pinned snesrecomp framework are under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; the interpreter is LakeSnes-derived (MIT), vendored dependencies keep their own licenses, and Capcom keeps its game rights. README presents the project as part of R.A.I.D. (Retro AI Development), a Discord community for AI-assisted retro reverse engineering, but names no model or workflow for this repository; no REA use is established.

name: OpenSC4: an early open-source reimplementation of SimCity 4
description_en: Reimplements SimCity 4 as a Godot project in GDScript that reads DBPF archives, region folders and city saves from the user’s own SimCity 4 installation. The code draws a region view with city thumbnails and interface elements built from the game’s UI definitions, opens a saved city’s terrain and water in 3D, and includes a DAT explorer for previewing archive subfiles. It is an early, inactive engine case without simulation gameplay, not a playable replacement.
description_zh: 以 Godot 项目和 GDScript 重新实现 SimCity 4，从使用者自有的 SimCity 4 安装目录读取 DBPF 归档、区域文件夹和城市存档。代码可绘制带城市缩略图的区域视图，并依据游戏的 UI 定义生成界面元素，可在 3D 中打开已存城市的地形与水面，还附带用于预览归档子文件的 DAT 浏览器。这是一个早期且已停滞的引擎案例，尚无模拟玩法，并非可替代原版的实现。
requirements: The reviewed main snapshot (2024-03-29) only added a README and a Discord invite; the last code change dates from 2023-02-17, and the repository has no releases or tags. README describes an open source “clone” meant to use modern hardware and run on other platforms. The code covers DBPF parsing, a region view for the hard-coded Timbuktu region, a city terrain view and the DAT explorer, with no zoning, budget or growth simulation; the reviewed files do not describe how SimCity 4 was analysed.

Needs the user’s own SimCity 4 installation: the boot screen asks for its folder and checks for SimCity 4.ini, Sound.dat, Intro.dat, SimCity_1.dat to SimCity_5.dat and EP1.dat, then reads .sc4 city saves, config.bmp and region music from that folder. .gitignore excludes SimCity 4 data, although the tree contains a “Graphics Rules.sgr.backup” text file whose header says SC4Launcher generated it.

Runs from source in the Godot editor: README’s setup is to install Godot, import the cloned project and run it, without naming a version. project.godot uses config_version 4 and the scripts call Godot 3 APIs such as yield and Directory; no export presets or packaged builds are provided.
The repository has no tests or CI workflows and publishes no comparison with SimCity 4’s behaviour or output; this collection did not run the project.

GitHub detects no license and the tree has no license file; nine GDScript files carry AGPL-3.0-or-later headers for “The OpenSC4 contributors” (2023), and utils/logger.gd is MIT-licensed code from KOBUGE Games’ godot-logger. SimCity 4 and its data keep their owners’ rights. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: synchrony
description_en: JavaScript cleaner and deobfuscator aimed mainly at output from javascript-obfuscator (obfuscator.io). It parses a script with acorn and runs a fixed pipeline of AST transformers that fold expressions, clean member accesses, remove dead branches, split sequence expressions, undo switch-based control-flow flattening and decode string arrays, re-implementing their base64 and RC4 decoders in TypeScript rather than executing the input. It ships on npm as deobfuscator with a synchrony CLI and a library API, and optional renaming replaces identifiers with generated word names rather than recovering the originals.
description_zh: 主要面向 javascript-obfuscator（obfuscator.io）输出的 JavaScript 清理与反混淆工具。它用 acorn 解析脚本，再运行一组固定的 AST 转换器：折叠表达式、整理成员访问、删除死分支、拆分逗号表达式、还原基于 switch 的控制流平坦化，并解码字符串数组；其中 base64 和 RC4 解码器以 TypeScript 重新实现，而不是执行输入代码。它以 deobfuscator 之名发布在 npm 上，提供 synchrony 命令行工具和库 API；可选的重命名会把标识符换成生成的单词名，并不能恢复原名。
requirements: Latest release at review: 2.4.6, published to GitHub and to npm as deobfuscator on 2026-07-07, the same day as the reviewed master commit; the previous release, 2.4.5, dates from 2023-11-09. The README also points to a hosted web version at deobfuscate.relative.im, whose deployment was not reviewed.

Install with npm, yarn or pnpm, or from the Git repository; package.json declares no Node.js version. The CLI reads one file, writes <name>.cleaned.<ext> unless --output is given, and offers --rename, --loose parsing, --ecma-version and --sourceType. A --config file is loaded with Node's require, so it runs as code, and a custom transformer list replaces the default pipeline; two jsconfuser transformers are available only that way and are not documented in the README.

The README warns that output from old javascript-obfuscator versions will likely not deobfuscate correctly and that there is no user configuration for the automatic string decoder. The repository has no test suite, and its latest commit removed the GitHub CI configuration.
GPL-3.0-only according to package.json and LICENSE.md. No scripts were deobfuscated in this review, and the reviewed sources establish no REA connection.

name: R.E.L.I.V.E.: an Oddworld Abe’s Oddysee and Abe’s Exoddus engine reimplementation
description_en: Reimplements the engine of Oddworld: Abe’s Oddysee and Abe’s Exoddus as an open-source replacement executable that runs from the user’s own game folder. The team decompiled the original executables and replaced their functions incrementally, using injected DLLs that hook reimplemented code into the patched retail executable, then rewrote the result into a standalone cross-platform engine. The project site says both games are playable in their entirety, with bug fixes and windowed, high-resolution and controller play.
description_zh: 以开源的替代可执行文件重新实现 Oddworld: Abe’s Oddysee 与 Abe’s Exoddus 的引擎，在使用者自己的游戏目录中运行。团队先反编译原版可执行文件并逐步替换其中的函数，借助注入的 DLL 将重新实现的代码挂接到打过补丁的零售版程序中，之后再把成果改写为独立的跨平台引擎。项目网站称两款游戏均可完整通关，并修复了缺陷，支持窗口模式、高分辨率和手柄游玩。
requirements: Reviewed at the master commit of 2026-09-01 that merged the SDL3 port; the latest release is github-v1.0.9, labelled “relive stable v1.0.9” (2025-03-21), while CMake still declares project version 0.1. The project site’s FAQ says both games can be played through, over a hundred original bugs are fixed and there should be no noticeable gameplay difference from the retail version; PSX-quality music, deeper modding and an in-game level editor are listed as future work. The FAQ describes the method as decompiling the retail executable and then spending years rewriting the output into readable code.

Play requires the user’s own Abe’s Oddysee or Abe’s Exoddus installation; the FAQ names the Steam, GOG and early disc versions. The executable runs from the game folder that holds the .lvl files, and the Linux launcher scripts look for the default Steam folder or ask for that directory. The repository contains no game data files, though source files embed data tables used by the reimplemented code, such as fonts and video-decompression tables; the FAQ says the team will not provide game files.

Builds use CMake 3.10+, C++17 and SDL3 after a recursive clone of the Detours, googletest, magic_enum, jsonxx, stb, lodepng and nlohmann/json submodules; README documents Visual Studio 2022 on Windows and Ubuntu packages on Linux, and cpack produces a Debian package. MSVC builds also produce the AliveDllAE and AliveDllAO hooking DLLs, linked with Detours on 32-bit Windows. GitHub Actions builds Windows 32-bit, Windows 64-bit and Linux packages; its macOS job is commented out, although the FAQ says the games run on macOS.

The GitHub Actions workflow builds and packages without running tests. The tree has googletest unit and integration tests for the relive_api level-data tool, and the integration test reads .lvl files from hard-coded GOG install paths; older AppVeyor and Azure Pipelines configurations still invoke ctest. The FAQ reports automated replays that record a full play-through with a stable build and flag desyncs in development builds (the recorder saves input, RNG, ticks and sync points), but no replay results are published, and this collection ran nothing.

The repository has no license file and GitHub detects none; README only says contributions will be licensed under a GPL-compatible license, most likely MIT, in the future, so reuse terms are currently unstated. 3rdParty/DxOld carries three DirectX 7-era Direct3D headers, one with a Microsoft all-rights-reserved notice, and the submodules keep their own licenses. The FAQ disclaims affiliation with Oddworld Inhabitants, whose games keep their own rights; the reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: RetDec
description_en: Avast's retargetable machine-code decompiler built on LLVM. It takes ELF, PE, Mach-O, COFF, AR, Intel HEX or raw code for 32-bit x86, ARM, MIPS, PIC32 and PowerPC or 64-bit x86-64 and ARM64, recovers functions, types and C++ class hierarchies, and emits C or a Python-like language with call and control-flow graphs.
description_zh: Avast 推出的基于 LLVM 的可重定向机器码反编译器。可处理 ELF、PE、Mach-O、COFF、AR、Intel HEX 或原始机器码，覆盖 32 位 x86、ARM、MIPS、PIC32、PowerPC 以及 64 位 x86-64 和 ARM64，能恢复函数、类型和 C++ 类层次结构，输出 C 或类 Python 语言代码，并生成调用图和控制流图。
requirements: README warns that RetDec is in limited maintenance mode: pull requests are reviewed with priority, issues get delayed reactions and are not actively solved unless they concern basic maintenance, and only very limited development continues. The latest release is v5.0 (2022-12-08); the reviewed master commit of 2026-05-26 is 81 commits ahead of it and still declares version 5.0.

Release packages cover Linux, macOS and Windows; README lists Windows 7+, Linux, macOS and experimental FreeBSD, with about 5–6 GB per installation. Source builds need a C++17 compiler (GCC 7+, Visual Studio 2017 15.7+ or full Xcode on macOS 10.15+), OpenSSL 1.1.1+, Python 3.4+ and, outside Windows, autotools; CMakeLists.txt requires CMake 3.13, not README's 3.6. The build downloads pinned Capstone, Keystone, YARA and yaramod, an Avast LLVM fork and a 2019 support package.

Input is the user's own executable, object file, archive or raw machine code. Since v5.0 the decompiler is also a set of CMake libraries for other projects, and separate retdec-idaplugin and retdec-r2plugin repositories embed it in IDA and radare2.

GitHub Actions builds Release and Debug builds on Ubuntu 22.04, Windows (MSYS2) and macOS, then runs the separate retdec-regression-tests suite. README calls nightly builds unguaranteed, with possible regressions, and Docker support community-maintained.
MIT (Avast Software). The modified PeLib keeps its zlib/libpng license, and LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY lists the other components, including Keystone used under its FOSS exception to GPLv2.

name: Age of Empires Free Software Remake: a re-implementation on the original data
description_en: Re-implements Microsoft’s Age of Empires and its Rise of Rome expansion as a cross-platform C++17 engine on SDL2 and OpenGL that loads the original game’s DRS archives and language.dll resources. README says it mimics the Windows API and the Genie engine for compatibility and reconstructs some code from the disassembly; the repository adds format notes and Python tools for inspecting the original data files. Only very basic gameplay through a multiplayer session exists so far, so it is an early engine case rather than a playable replacement.
description_zh: 以基于 SDL2 和 OpenGL 的跨平台 C++17 引擎重新实现 Microsoft 的《帝国时代》及其资料片《罗马复兴》，载入原版游戏的 DRS 归档和 language.dll 资源。README 称项目为兼容起见模仿 Windows API 和 Genie 引擎，部分代码依据反汇编重建；仓库另附格式笔记和用于检查原版数据文件的 Python 工具。目前只能通过多人会话进行非常基础的游戏，因此这是一个早期引擎案例，而非可替代原版游玩的实现。
requirements: The reviewed master snapshot (2026-09-20) sets CMake version 0.1, and the repository has no releases or tags; the user guide says no binary builds are provided. README reports only very basic gameplay and only multiplayer mode: single-player means hosting a session and adding computer players, which only gather resources until attacked. doc/reverse_engineering documents the DRS archive contents, the Windows API functions the original imports, the scenario format, civilizations and unit statistics.

Needs a legitimate copy of Age of Empires or Rise of Rome, on the CD-ROM or installed: the engine loads Border.drs, graphics.drs, Interfac.drs, sounds.drs and Terrain.drs from the data folder plus language.dll, and expects the game fonts COPRGTB.TTF and COPRGTL.TTF that the original installer adds. The repository contains no game data, and community replacement assets are not supported yet.

README lists Windows 10+, macOS Sequoia 15.7.7, Fedora 44 and Ubuntu 22+ as tested, while INSTALL still warns that Linux builds look for hard-coded legacy TTF font paths. Builds use CMake 3.11+ with C99 and C++17 against SDL2, SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer and OpenGL, plus the imgui, tracy, wepoll and miniz submodules; Windows builds use Visual Studio with vcpkg or MinGW.

GitHub Actions builds the game with Clang on Ubuntu and Fedora and runs the Google Test suite in headless mode; its tests cover networking, the protocol, the server, SDL and a UI menu rather than equivalence with the original executable. No comparison with the original game is published; this collection built or ran nothing.

LICENSE applies Apache-2.0; the submodules and the bundled headers in game/src/external keep their own licenses. README states that all copyrighted material and trademarks belong to their respective owners and calls the work an educational non-profit project. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: God of War PS2 static recompilation: a native Windows port via PS2Recomp
description_en: Statically recompiles the MIPS R5900 code of the NTSC-U PlayStation 2 God of War executable (SCUS-97399) to C++ with PS2Recomp and builds it as a native Windows program. Since October 2026 the port builds on Waffle565’s runtime, which replaces the PS2 hardware with native code: VU1 microprograms and, optionally, the game’s IRX modules are compiled ahead of time, and an OpenGL renderer stands in for the GS. The repository holds only the game-specific function map, recompiler configuration, overrides and runtime patches; the README reports gameplay on the opening ship level, with sustained 60 fps and a full playthrough still pending.
description_zh: 使用 PS2Recomp 将 PlayStation 2 版《战神》美版（SCUS-97399）可执行文件中的 MIPS R5900 代码静态重编译为 C++，并构建为 Windows 原生程序。自 2026 年 10 月起，移植以 Waffle565 的运行时为基础，用原生代码取代 PS2 硬件：VU1 微程序以及可选的游戏 IRX 模块会预先编译，OpenGL 渲染器则代替 GS。仓库只包含本作专用的函数映射、重编译器配置、覆盖实现与运行时补丁；README 报告已能在开场的船上关卡中游玩，而稳定 60 fps 与完整通关仍待完成。
requirements: Reviewed at main (2026-10-18); the project has published no release. README marks the port experimental and reports boot, menus, a new game and the ship fight with HUD, native VU1 and IOP, and exact game speed. Sustained 60 fps, saves and movies with sound (so far verified only in Waffle565’s port), a full playthrough and PAL languages remain open, and an intermittent hang of the window thread is under investigation. The .recomp.json metadata still describes an earlier, not-yet-playable state, and most technical documents are in Spanish.

Requires the user’s own NTSC-U God of War disc (SCUS-97399): the build reads its SCUS_973.99 executable, and play reads the IRX modules and PAK data from the user’s disc files kept at their original sectors. README states that the repository contains no game files, IRX modules or generated C++, and .gitignore excludes disc images, the executable, IRX and PAK files and the generated directories.

Builds only on Windows 10/11 x64 with Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools (C++ workload, including CMake and Ninja), Git and Python 3, with about 20 GB free and 16 GB of RAM recommended. scripts/2_compilar.cmd clones PS2Recomp at commit c5a9d02, applies the patches in order, generates about 6,400 C++ files from the user’s executable and builds ps2EntryRunner.exe; the first build takes 20–40 minutes.

CI validates the function map and recompiler configuration, applies every patch to PS2Recomp and runs its ps2x_tests runtime suite against a known-failures list, and runs game-independent GS, VU1, pad and camera tests, plus a Windows job that links an isolated PCSX2 GS module without a GPU. Gameplay and performance figures come from the author’s runs on one Ryzen 7 5800XT and RX 5700 XT machine, recorded in docs/ESTADO.md; this collection built and ran nothing.

The repository is GPL-3.0, matching PS2Recomp; the applied runtime comes from Waffle565’s God-Of-War-Native-Port, whose repository root has no license file, and brings PCSX2-derived code (GPL-3.0+). Sony Interactive Entertainment and Santa Monica Studio keep their game rights. AGENTS.md says several agents work on main at once, CLAUDE.md points Claude to those conventions and the status log credits fixes to Claude; no REA use is established.

name: REDasm
description_en: Cross-platform interactive disassembler whose version 4 is a plain-C rewrite: a C17 engine library, the Qt6 GUI kept in this repository, and loader, processor and analyzer plugins loaded as shared libraries. The listing supports renaming, comments and typed data, with a synchronized control-flow graph, cross-references, string detection, a hex view, patching and saved projects. Besides PE and ELF, loaders cover retro and console formats such as DOS MZ, Win16 NE, OS/2 LE/LX, PlayStation 1, original Xbox and ZX Spectrum, with x86/x86-64, MIPS32, ARM/Thumb, ARM64, Z80 and 6502 processors.
description_zh: 跨平台交互式反汇编器，第 4 版以纯 C 重写：由 C17 引擎库、保留在本仓库中的 Qt6 图形界面，以及以共享库形式加载的加载器、处理器和分析器插件组成。反汇编列表支持重命名、注释和类型化数据，并提供同步的控制流图、交叉引用、字符串检测、十六进制视图、补丁和项目保存。除 PE 和 ELF 外，加载器还支持 DOS MZ、Win16 NE、OS/2 LE/LX、PlayStation 1、初代 Xbox 和 ZX Spectrum 等复古及主机格式，处理器涵盖 x86/x86-64、MIPS32、ARM/Thumb、ARM64、Z80 和 6502。
requirements: Latest release at review: v4.0.0-beta3, published 2026-09-02, with a Linux x86_64 AppImage and a portable Windows x86_64 ZIP plus GPG-signed checksums; the reviewed master commit is 43 commits ahead of that tag. Nightly builds from master, which the README warns may be unstable, also include macOS DMGs. Version 4 is a complete rewrite still in beta; the README says version 3 was retired, and its last release, 3.0 beta 5, dates from 2021.

The README rates Windows 10+ with Visual Studio 2022 and Linux with GCC 12+ (Ubuntu 24.04/Debian 13 reference) as actively tested platforms with official binaries; FreeBSD and macOS only pass CI builds and tests, and Haiku only compiles. Source builds go through the separate workspace repository, which fetches the core, GUI, plugin and knowledge-base repositories and needs CMake 3.20, C17/C++17 compilers and Qt 6.8 LTS.

Executables and console program files are supplied by the user. The README's maturity tables rate PE, ELF and x86/x86-64 support production ready and Visual Basic 5/6 event recovery highly stable, but the DOS MZ, PS1 BIOS, Xbox, ZX Spectrum and NES (NROM only) loaders and the Z80 and 6502 processors only functional, and MSVC RTTI and exception-handling recovery work in progress. There is no decompiler yet, and extensions are written in C; a Python plugin API is on the roadmap.
GPL-3.0 for the GUI, the core and every bundled plugin; the separate knowledge-base repository of TOML signatures and type definitions is CC0-1.0. Nothing was built and no binaries were analyzed.

name: protobuf-inspector
description_en: Parses Protocol Buffers blobs (proto2 or proto3) without their .proto definition and prints a colored view of the fields in wire order, trying each length-delimited chunk as a nested message, then a packed array, a string and finally a hexdump. Analysts record what they work out in a protobuf_config.py file, with field types and names, message and enum types and custom native types, until the parser no longer has to guess. Field names, zig-zag encoding, signedness and integer-versus-float choices cannot be read from the wire, and the README says guesses can be wrong, especially for small chunks.
description_zh: 无需对应的 .proto 定义即可解析 Protocol Buffers 数据块（proto2 或 proto3），按线路编码顺序以彩色输出字段；对每个长度限定的数据块，依次尝试解析为嵌套消息、打包数组、字符串，最后退回十六进制转储。分析者把推断出的内容写入 protobuf_config.py，包括字段类型与名称、消息和枚举类型以及自定义原生类型，直到解析器不再需要猜测。字段名、zig-zag 编码、有无符号以及整数还是浮点数，都无法从线路数据中读出；README 也说明猜测可能出错，小数据块尤甚。
requirements: Development is dormant: the only release, 0.2 on PyPI and tagged v0.2.0, and the reviewed master commit both date from 2020-11-24, with no later commits. This records activity only, not a verdict on correctness or on compatibility with current Python versions.

Install with pip (setup.py declares Python >=3.3) and pipe one raw protobuf blob to protobuf_inspector on standard input, optionally naming the root message type. The README documents no capture, gRPC or HTTP handling, so blobs must first be extracted from traffic or files the analyst is entitled to inspect.

The CLI searches the working directory and each parent up to the filesystem mount point for protobuf_config.py and runs it with runpy, so a config file executes as Python code. A dump type writes matching chunks to dump.N files in the working directory, and parse errors stop inside the affected field and make the command exit non-zero.

ISC license. The README says the Python API was not designed as a library and may change. The repository has no tests or CI configuration; nothing was parsed in this review, and the reviewed sources establish no REA connection.

name: Lighthouse
description_en: Code-coverage explorer plugin for IDA Pro and Binary Ninja that loads execution traces of native programs and paints the executed code across the disassembler's views, without needing symbols or source. Its coverage overview lists per-function coverage, and a composing shell combines loaded coverage sets with logical operators to diff runs, filter functions and jump to addresses, while coverage cross-references show which of many batch-loaded sets executed a block. It reads DynamoRIO drcov logs, module+offset, absolute-address and Tenet traces, writes basic HTML coverage reports, and ships a prototype Intel Pin tool and a Frida script that produce drcov-compatible logs.
description_zh: 面向 IDA Pro 和 Binary Ninja 的代码覆盖率浏览插件，载入原生程序的执行轨迹，并在反汇编器的各个视图中为已执行代码着色，无需符号或源码。覆盖率总览按函数列出覆盖情况；组合命令行可用逻辑运算符组合已载入的覆盖率集合，用于比较多次运行的差异、筛选函数或跳转到指定地址；覆盖率交叉引用则显示批量载入的众多集合中哪些执行过某个基本块。它可读取 DynamoRIO drcov 日志、模块+偏移、绝对地址和 Tenet 轨迹，能生成简单的 HTML 覆盖率报告，并附带可输出 drcov 兼容日志的原型 Intel Pin 工具和 Frida 脚本。
requirements: Release at review: v0.9.3, published 2024-02-05 as a servicing release that adds full drcov v3 support and Binary Ninja/PySide6 fixes; the reviewed master commit is that tag. The develop branch is nine commits ahead with IDA 9.x, 9.2 and 9.3 compatibility fixes from 2025-2026 and a 0.9.4 development version, none of them released.

Requires IDA Pro 7 or newer (the IDA layer stops on IDA 6) or Binary Ninja, where the README says plugin-manager installation supports v3.5 and newer; for IDA the README copies the plugins folder into the user plugin directory. The README describes a cross-platform Windows, macOS and Linux Python 2/3 plugin with no third-party dependencies. In Binary Ninja, coverage is painted in linear, graph and IL views but not decompiler output.

Coverage is collected separately against the user's own target: the coverage README shows DynamoRIO drcov, the bundled CodeCoverage pintool (a prototype; the release attaches Windows builds for Pin 3.30, and macOS and Linux users build it against their own Intel Pin download) and the experimental frida-drcov.py, which its README recommends mainly for mobile applications. Absolute-address traces must match the database's address space; unmapped addresses are discarded, and other modules' hits in module+offset traces are not loaded.
MIT for Lighthouse and for the contributed pintool. Opening the coverage overview checks the GitHub releases API for a newer version. No coverage was collected or loaded.

name: RaceWave46: an AI-assisted Wave Race 64 recompilation for Windows
description_en: Recompiles the USA Rev 1 Nintendo 64 release of Wave Race 64 into a native Windows application with N64Recomp and RSPRecomp, on modified copies of the N64ModernRuntime, RecompFrontend and RT64 stacks. Game and microcode C is generated locally from the user’s ROM, after an included widescreen patch is applied to a temporary copy, and checked against recorded checksums. The port adds higher resolutions, frame interpolation, ultrawide views, rasterized and ray-traced reflections and shadows, split-screen or separate-window two-player play and RetroAchievements; the maintainer calls it an AI-assisted recompilation.
description_zh: 使用 N64Recomp 与 RSPRecomp，在经修改的 N64ModernRuntime、RecompFrontend 和 RT64 之上，将 Nintendo 64 版《Wave Race 64》美版 Rev 1 重编译为 Windows 原生程序。游戏与微码的 C 代码在本地由使用者的 ROM 生成：先将随附的宽屏补丁应用到临时副本，再按记录的校验和核对生成结果。移植加入了更高分辨率、帧插值、超宽视野、光栅化与光线追踪的反射和阴影、分屏或分窗口的双人游戏以及 RetroAchievements；维护者称其为 AI 辅助的重编译。
requirements: Reviewed at the repository’s single public commit, tagged v1.0.0 (release published 2026-09-16) with a Windows x64 build and a source ZIP. README targets 64-bit Windows 10/11 with Direct3D 12 and Vulkan back ends; the added reflections, shadows and separate player windows need Direct3D 12, and ray tracing needs DXR 1.1 / Shader Model 6.5. Controller Pak save and load are not implemented, multiplayer is local only, RetroAchievements lacks hardcore mode and leaderboards, and performance requirements are still being evaluated.

Building and playing need the user’s own unmodified Wave Race 64 (USA) Rev 1 ROM, in big-endian .z64 form for the build; players import it in the frontend. Generation verifies the ROM, patches a temporary copy with the included widescreen IPS patch, whose authorship the reviewed files do not state, and installs the verified output into git-ignored directories. README states that no ROM, saves, texture packs or account data are included.

Builds use Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools with the Windows 10/11 SDK and C++ CMake tools (MSVC x64, CMake 3.20+, Ninja), Python 3.11+, and N64Recomp and RSPRecomp built from the bundled, modified source. The first configuration downloads Microsoft DXC 1.8.2502 and 1.9.2607 compilers pinned by SHA-256, and BUILDING.md warns against substituting unmodified upstream dependencies.

The tree holds 84 CMake regression suites run individually through BUILD-TEST.ps1, some needing the user’s ROM, but no CI workflow; generation checks every generated file against the hashes in config/generated-code.json. README reports repeated hands-on testing of races, menus, course introductions and the championship ending. This collection built and ran nothing.

The project’s original contributions are GPL-3.0-only; N64ModernRuntime is GPLv3, other vendored components keep their own notices, and Nintendo keeps its game assets and trademarks. README states that AI tools were used for code implementation, debugging, research and documentation, while project direction, review and gameplay testing stay with the maintainer; no REA use is established.

name: OpenDrop: an open reimplementation of Apple AirDrop
description_en: Python command-line reimplementation of Apple's AirDrop protocol from SEEMOO Lab's reverse-engineering research. It finds receivers via _airdrop._tcp DNS-SD, sends binary-plist /Discover and /Ask requests over HTTPS and uploads gzip-compressed CPIO archives to exchange files with iOS and macOS. It is not affiliated with Apple.
description_zh: 基于 SEEMOO 实验室逆向研究、用 Python 编写的 Apple AirDrop 协议命令行重新实现。它通过 _airdrop._tcp DNS-SD 发现接收方，经 HTTPS 发送二进制 plist 格式的 /Discover 和 /Ask 请求，并上传 gzip 压缩的 CPIO 归档，与 iOS 和 macOS 设备互传文件。它与 Apple 无关联。
requirements: README calls OpenDrop experimental output of the Open Wireless Link reverse-engineering effort that lacks some AirDrop features and may break with future AirDrop versions, and says Apple neither affiliates with nor endorses it. The latest release is 0.13.0 (PyPI, 2021-04-29); the reviewed master commit of 2026-08-17 adds only a citation file and link edits since.

AirDrop runs only over Apple Wireless Direct Link, so OpenDrop is supported on macOS or on Linux with an open AWDL implementation such as SEEMOO's OWL; the default interface is awdl0. It needs Python 3.6+ (classifiers list 3.6–3.9), a current libarchive (Homebrew's on macOS), the openssl command and the packages in setup.py, including zeroconf and libarchive-c.

By default it creates its own self-signed key and certificate. Receivers in the default contacts-only mode need AirDrop keys, a certificate and an Apple ID validation record from the user's own Mac, which README says come from a separate SEEMOO extractor; the repository ships only Apple's public root CA certificate.

README lists known gaps: no Bluetooth Low Energy trigger, so Apple receivers may stay undiscovered; no peer authentication (neither TLS certificate chains nor validation records are checked) and automatic acceptance of every incoming file; and one file per transfer, with links sent but not received. CI runs black, flake8 and pytest on Python 3.6–3.9; its two tests only start the browser and server on loopback.
GPL-3.0. README points to the authors' USENIX Security 2019 AWDL paper and 2021 PrivateDrop paper for protocol details; AirDrop and AWDL remain Apple's protocols.

name: CHIPSEC
description_en: Platform security assessment framework, with Intel Corporation copyright notices, for analyzing PC hardware configuration, BIOS/UEFI system firmware and platform components from Windows, Linux or the UEFI shell. chipsec_main runs check modules that report whether expected protections are in place, such as BIOS and SPI flash write protection and locks, SMM and SMRR protection, memory-map locks and Secure Boot variables, as PASSED, FAILED, WARNING or informational results with JSON, XML and Markdown output. chipsec_util gives command-line and Python access to low-level interfaces and firmware data, including dumping the SPI flash to an image, decoding flash images into firmware volumes, files and NVRAM variables, and listing UEFI variables and tables.
description_zh: 平台安全评估框架（源码带有 Intel Corporation 版权声明），可在 Windows、Linux 或 UEFI Shell 中分析 PC 硬件配置、BIOS/UEFI 系统固件及平台组件。chipsec_main 运行检查模块，报告预期的保护措施是否到位，例如 BIOS 与 SPI 闪存的写保护和锁定、SMM 与 SMRR 保护、内存映射锁定及安全启动变量，结果分为 PASSED、FAILED、WARNING 和信息类，并可输出 JSON、XML 和 Markdown。chipsec_util 通过命令行和 Python 访问底层接口和固件数据，包括将 SPI 闪存转储为镜像、把闪存镜像解析为固件卷、文件和 NVRAM 变量，以及列出 UEFI 变量和表。
requirements: Release at review: 2.0.9, published 2026-09-24 with a source zip; the reviewed chipsec2 commit is five configuration and bug-fix commits ahead. The installation guide says the PyPI package is outdated. The README sends older Intel platforms (clients before 12th-generation Core, servers before 3rd-generation Xeon Scalable) to the chipsec1 branch, and almost all bundled platform configurations are Intel ones.

Runs as Administrator/root and loads a kernel driver that is distributed as source and built locally. Linux needs Python 3.8+, kernel headers, gcc and nasm; Windows 8 to 11 and Server 2012 to 2025 need Visual Studio with the WDK, and loading the self-built driver requires disabling driver signature enforcement or enabling test signing. The UEFI shell route boots a USB drive with the repository's prebuilt UEFI Python 3.6.8 package and requires Secure Boot to be off; a mkosi recipe builds a live Linux image. The --no-driver option works only for some commands and modules.

chipsec/WARNING.txt says to use it only on test systems, never production machines: the driver gives user mode access to physical memory and other hardware resources, and incorrect hardware access can hang or crash the OS. Some utility commands write or erase SPI flash or change UEFI variables and can leave a system unbootable; the separate tools modules, which include fuzzers, are outside this entry. A WARNING result requires manual analysis, and the results guide is marked as a draft.

Flash images and platform data come from the machine under test or the user's own dumps; the repository bundles no vendor firmware images. CI builds the Linux driver across distributions and runs unit tests on recorded platform data plus a QEMU UEFI-shell test. GPL-2.0. Nothing was run on hardware.

name: APK Studio
description_en: Qt6 desktop front end that drives Apktool, JADX, uber-apk-signer and ADB from an IDE-style workspace for Android packages. It decodes an APK into smali and resources, optionally adds JADX Java output, then rebuilds, signs (with optional keystore generation and zipalign) and installs the result on a selected device; manufacturer framework files and extra Apktool arguments can be supplied. Decoded projects open in a file tree with syntax-highlighted smali, Java, XML and YAML editing, an image viewer, a hex editor and search across files.
description_zh: 基于 Qt6 的桌面前端，在 IDE 式工作区中调用 Apktool、JADX、uber-apk-signer 和 ADB 处理 Android 安装包。它将 APK 解码为 smali 和资源文件，可选附加 JADX 生成的 Java 代码，随后重新打包、签名（可生成密钥库并执行 zipalign）并安装到所选设备；还可指定厂商框架文件和额外的 Apktool 参数。解码后的项目以文件树形式打开，提供 smali、Java、XML 和 YAML 的语法高亮编辑、图片查看器、十六进制编辑器和跨文件搜索。
requirements: Release at review: v6.3.0, published 2026-01-05 from the reviewed master commit, with a Linux x86_64 AppImage, a Windows x64 ZIP and a macOS DMG. The 6.x series began with v6.0.0 on 2025-12-03, following 5.2.4 from 2020, and no commits have landed since 2026-01-05. Source builds need CMake 3.16+, Qt 6.10.1+ (Core, Gui, Network, Widgets), a C++17 compiler, Git and the QHexView submodule.

The decoding, decompilation, signing and installation are done by the external tools. On first launch APK Studio can download Microsoft OpenJDK 11.0.29, the latest Apktool, JADX and uber-apk-signer GitHub releases and Google's latest platform-tools, or use installations configured in Settings; only the JDK version is pinned, and on macOS the automatic JDK is the Apple-silicon package. Its console shows the commands actually run, and the README asks users to separate Apktool problems from APK Studio issues.

APKs and any manufacturer framework files are supplied by the user; installation needs a device reachable through ADB. Decoded smali and JADX Java output are reconstructions to be checked, not original source. The README reports CI builds on Windows, Linux and macOS, and its disclaimer says the tool is not intended for piracy or other non-legal uses.
LGPL-3.0. Nothing was installed and no APKs were decoded.

name: Valetudo: local replacement for robot-vacuum vendor clouds
description_en: Replaces the vendor cloud of supported robot vacuums with a local service that runs on the rooted robot beside the vendor firmware and emulates the cloud endpoints that firmware expects, including a miio dummycloud and a counterpart for Midea's MSmart protocol. Its FAQ says each new vendor backend meant reverse engineering data formats, authentication and communication without vendor documentation; Valetudo converts the proprietary map formats into one ValetudoMap format and keeps Kaitai Struct descriptions of Dreame, Roborock and Viomi map files and a Midea protobuf schema as references. It adds a web interface, a REST API with Swagger UI and MQTT/Home Assistant integration, while feature parity with the vendor apps is an explicit non-goal.
description_zh: 用运行在已 root 机器人上、与厂商固件并存的本地服务取代受支持扫地机器人的厂商云，并模拟固件所期待的云端接口，包括 miio 模拟云（dummycloud）以及对应 Midea MSmart 协议的实现。其 FAQ 说明，每支持一个新厂商，都需要在没有厂商文档的情况下逆向分析数据格式、认证和通信；Valetudo 将各家专有地图格式转换为统一的 ValetudoMap 格式，并保留 Dreame、Roborock、Viomi 地图文件的 Kaitai Struct 描述和一份 Midea protobuf 模式作为参考。它提供网页界面、带 Swagger UI 的 REST API 以及 MQTT／Home Assistant 集成，但明确不以与厂商应用功能对等为目标。
requirements: Reviewed at the 2026.10.0 release commit of 2026-10-18. The README says Valetudo is not a custom firmware but a 'brain parasite' for the vendor firmware, whose own functions it relies on. The backend has Dreame, Roborock, Viomi, 3irobotix and Midea implementations, and the supported-robots page lists 50 model entries under 10 brand headings and calls the list exhaustive.

Requires a supported robot that its owner has already rooted. The docs describe rooting as model-specific and permanent ('Reverting to stock is impossible'), and say the vendor app stops working because cloud connectivity is cut; this record covers no rooting procedure. The repository and its releases ship no vendor firmware: release assets are Valetudo's own armv7, armv7-lowmem and aarch64 binaries with UPX-compressed variants, an OpenAPI schema and a release manifest, while the repository also commits pkg Node.js base binaries for packaging and small captured map files as test fixtures.

Valetudo runs on the robot's Linux system as a static Node.js 22 binary built with pkg; development needs Node.js >=20 according to the root package.json. The docs require Linux and computer skills, and sometimes hardware work, for installation, and offer peer support only.

CI on Node.js 22 runs type checks, lint, the frontend and backend builds and the backend node:test suite, including Dreame, Roborock and 3irobotix map-parser tests on captured maps and miio and MSmart packet tests. The supported-robots page says each listed robot was tested by the author personally unless noted. These are project-reported checks; this review ran nothing and compared no behaviour with vendor clouds.

Apache-2.0, although the README describes its governance as 'Freeware with source available'. The Kaitai structs declare CC-BY-SA-4.0, and a bundled robot model and tracker song are credited under CC-BY-NC-SA. Vendor firmware, apps and clouds keep their own terms. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: sourcemapper
description_en: Go command-line tool that recreates a web front end's original JavaScript source tree from a source map generated by webpack or a similar bundler, writing each embedded source file under the path the map records. It takes a .map file by URL or local path, walks a directory of .map files, or fetches a JavaScript file and follows its sourceMappingURL comment or SourceMap response header, including inline data: maps.
description_zh: Go 编写的命令行工具，可根据 webpack 等打包工具生成的源映射（source map）重建网站前端原有的 JavaScript 源码目录树，并把映射中内嵌的每个源文件写到其记录的路径下。它可通过 URL 或本地路径读取 .map 文件，递归处理整个目录中的 .map 文件，也可抓取 JavaScript 文件并跟随其中的 sourceMappingURL 注释或 SourceMap 响应头，内联的 data: 映射同样支持。
requirements: The project publishes no releases or tags. The README installs it with go install, a clone-and-build, or the BlackArch package; go.mod declares Go 1.16 and lists no third-party modules. The reviewed master commit, dated 2026-07-24, also adds the -dir batch mode and refuses to read a local path named by a remote sourceMappingURL.

Only one of -url, -jsurl or -dir is accepted per run, and -output is required. Remote fetches can carry extra request headers, go through a proxy or skip TLS verification. The README warns that a JavaScript file parsed with -jsurl can make sourcemapper send a GET request to any URL it names as its source map.

The input is a source map the user may inspect. The tool reads only the map's version, sources and sourcesContent fields, so maps without embedded sourcesContent are rejected and minified bundles without a map are out of scope; the mappings are not used, and output is the bundler's captured source text, not code verified against the deployed bundle.

BSD-3-Clause. Recovered front-end code remains subject to the site owner's rights. The README links a 2018 Pulse Security article describing its use for front-end source review in a penetration test. Nothing was built or run against any site.

name: Jazz² Resurrection: a native C++ reimplementation of Jazz Jackrabbit 2
description_en: Reimplements Jazz Jackrabbit 2 (1998) as a native C++ game on an extensively modified nCine engine, converting the user’s original game files into its own cache on first start. It runs on desktop, mobile, web and many homebrew console targets, with multiplayer, an enhanced Reforged mode and partial JJ2+ and MLLE support. A two-sided trajectory probe checks its non-Reforged movement against the original game, and the project reports 376 of 406 scenarios within 25 px/s.
description_zh: 以原生 C++ 在深度修改的 nCine 引擎上重新实现《爵士兔 2》（Jazz Jackrabbit 2，1998），首次启动时把使用者的原版游戏文件转换为自己的缓存。它可在桌面、移动设备、网页和众多自制软件主机平台上运行，支持多人游戏、增强的 Reforged 模式，并部分支持 JJ2+ 与 MLLE。项目用一个双向轨迹探针把非 Reforged 模式的移动与原版游戏对照，报告 406 个场景中有 376 个误差在 25 px/s 以内。
requirements: Reviewed at the master commit of 2026-10-17, just after release 3.9.0 of the same day, which reworked physics; release packages are published in the older deathkiller/jazz2 repository. README lists the Shareware Demo, Holiday Hare ’98, The Secret Files and Christmas Chronicles as supported, with partial JJ2+ and MLLE features, and marks the Nintendo 64, Dreamcast, Wii, GameCube and PlayStation 3 ports as not yet tested on real hardware. README calls the game fully rewritten in C++ and does not describe decompiling the original executable; the non-Reforged movement constants come from measurements of the original game.

Every build needs the contents of the user’s original Jazz Jackrabbit 2 directory, a retail version or the Shareware Demo, placed in a Source folder and converted into a cache on first start. On Nintendo 64, Dreamcast, PlayStation 2, GameCube and 3DS the content must first be converted with the project’s AssetPacker, and README says the resulting images can’t be distributed. The repository’s Content directory holds the game’s own fonts, extra animations, metadata and translations; the Windows 3.9.0 package contains it with an empty Source placeholder, and README says the Docker server image never contains original files.

README documents Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, Nintendo Switch, Web (Emscripten), a libretro core, Xbox (UWP), AmigaOS 3.x, AmigaOS 4.1 and MorphOS, Nintendo 64, Dreamcast, Wii, GameCube, 3DS, PSP, PS2, PS3 and Vita, plus a Docker dedicated server; desktop builds need an OpenGL 3.3 or OpenGL ES 3.0 GPU. Builds use CMake 3.15+, which downloads the prebuilt dependency set by default unless system libraries are used. Console builds use their own homebrew SDKs and toolchain files, and several console targets need custom firmware.

The Linux and Windows workflows build and package without running a test suite. An optional physics probe (WITH_PHYSICS_PROBE) drives the same scripted scenarios in this engine and in the original game with JJ2+ and logs every tick; the committed traces and comparison scripts let changes be checked without the original. For the 144 FPS engine capture, Results/README.md reports a median speed-distribution error of 0.1 px/s, 376 of 406 scenarios within 25 px/s and 70 of 397 scenarios whose animation-segment counts differ by over 25%. These are project-reported figures; this collection ran nothing.

LICENSE is GPL-3.0; Docs/ThirdParty.dox lists the third-party components, including parts of nCine (MIT), with their own licenses. Jazz Jackrabbit 2 and its data keep their owners’ rights. The reviewed sources establish no REA or AI use.

name: BinAbsInspector
description_en: Static vulnerability scanner from Tencent Keen Lab that runs as a Ghidra extension or headless script and applies abstract interpretation to Ghidra's P-code rather than to assembly, covering x86, x64, ARMv7 and AArch64 binaries. Its flow- and context-sensitive interprocedural analysis, with configurable value-set size and call-string depth, optional Z3 constraint solving and models of external functions, feeds checkers for 13 CWE classes, including command injection, buffer overflows and out-of-bounds access, format strings, integer overflow, double free, use-after-free and NULL dereference. Warnings list the instruction address and its call context, in the Ghidra console or as JSON.
description_zh: 腾讯科恩实验室开发的二进制静态漏洞扫描工具，以 Ghidra 扩展或无界面脚本方式运行，在 Ghidra 的 P-code 而非汇编上进行抽象解释，支持 x86、x64、ARMv7 和 AArch64 二进制。它执行流敏感、上下文敏感的过程间分析，可配置值集合大小和调用串深度，可选用 Z3 约束求解，并对外部函数建模，在此基础上运行 13 类 CWE 检查，涵盖命令注入、缓冲区溢出与越界访问、格式化字符串、整数溢出、重复释放、释放后使用和空指针解引用等。告警会列出指令地址及其调用上下文，显示在 Ghidra 控制台中或以 JSON 输出。
requirements: The only release, v0.1 from 2022-04-20, is an extension ZIP built for Ghidra 10.1.2. The reviewed main commit is 20 commits ahead; its Dockerfile and CI workflows use Ghidra 10.4 with JDK 17, and the last commit dates from 2024-05-14, so compatibility with current Ghidra releases is not documented. Source builds use Gradle 7.x (tested with 7.4) against a local Ghidra installation.

Z3 is required (tested version 4.8.15): the README suggests replacing the Java bindings bundled in lib/ with a matching package and installing the native library separately, not from Linux distribution packages. Runs use Ghidra's headless analyzer, the Script Manager after default auto-analysis in the GUI, or the provided Dockerfile, which builds Z3 from source and defaults to an Ubuntu mirror in China that the UBUNTU_MIRROR argument overrides.

Binaries are supplied by the user. Warnings are leads for manual review, not confirmed vulnerabilities; Keen Lab's release article reports its own Juliet test-suite comparison with cwe_checker on x86, x64 and ARMv7 for four CWE classes, scored by true and false positives and negatives.
GPL-3.0. Nothing was built and no binaries were analyzed.

name: libimobiledevice
description_en: C library and command-line tools that speak iOS devices' native service protocols without Apple's proprietary libraries or a jailbreak. Over usbmuxd or Wi-Fi sync it implements lockdownd pairing and services such as AFC file access, backup, app installation, crash reports, syslog, debugserver and WebKit inspection, plus Cython bindings.
description_zh: 用 C 编写的库及命令行工具，无需 Apple 的专有库或越狱即可使用 iOS 设备的原生服务协议通信。它经 usbmuxd 或 Wi-Fi 同步连接，实现 lockdownd 配对，以及 AFC 文件访问、备份、应用安装、崩溃报告、系统日志、debugserver 和 WebKit 检查等服务，并提供 Cython 绑定。
requirements: Latest release: 1.4.0 (2025-10-10), which NEWS calls a development release; it added MbedTLS support, Apple TV wireless pairing and iOS 17+ personalized developer disk image mounting, among other changes. The reviewed master commit of 2026-06-10 is nine commits ahead, mostly AFC and afcclient fixes.

Source builds use autotools and pkg-config with libplist 2.3.0+, libusbmuxd 2.0.2+, libimobiledevice-glue 1.3.0+ and libtatsu 1.0.3+ from the same organization (README says libtatsu must be built from source), plus OpenSSL by default, GnuTLS or MbedTLS; Doxygen and Cython are optional. The README dependency list includes the usbmuxd daemon and says the library is tested on Linux, macOS, Windows and Android.

Work starts from an iOS device the user controls and pairs with the host (idevicepair); the repository contains no Apple software. Screenshots and location simulation need a mounted Apple developer disk image, which is not included. README says library documentation is not yet available and points to the bundled utilities' source; each utility has a manual page.

GitHub Actions builds and installs the library on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows (MSYS2 MINGW64 and MINGW32) against the latest builds of its sibling libraries, on pushes, pull requests and a monthly schedule. The repository has no test suite, and no workflow exercises a device.

LGPL-2.1 for the library and utilities. The bundled ed25519 (zlib-style license) and Stanford SRP-based libsrp6a-sha512 (BSD-style) keep their own licenses. README states that the project is independent and not authorized, sponsored or approved by Apple.

name: ngrev
description_en: Electron desktop application that statically analyzes an Angular project's TypeScript sources and draws interactive graphs of its NgModules, components, directives, pipes and providers and how they depend on each other, without running the application. A project is loaded through its tsconfig file; views move from the module tree to individual modules, templates and providers, with fuzzy symbol search and PNG export of the current graph.
description_zh: 一款 Electron 桌面应用，对 Angular 项目的 TypeScript 源码做静态分析，以交互式图形展示其中的 NgModule、组件、指令、管道和服务提供者及其依赖关系，无需运行该应用。通过项目的 tsconfig 文件载入后，可从模块树逐层查看单个模块、模板和提供者，支持符号模糊搜索，并可将当前图形导出为 PNG。
requirements: Dormant: the latest release is v0.0.35 of 2021-01-18, with an unsigned macOS .dmg, a Linux AppImage and a Windows .exe. The reviewed master commit dates from 2021-07-26 and package.json already names an unreleased 0.0.36. The README calls it a community side project that the Angular team does not maintain.

Input is an Angular project's own source tree with its dependencies installed; for Angular CLI apps the README selects src/tsconfig.app.json. Applications must be compatible with the Ivy compiler, and versions older than Angular 11 are untested. The analyzer pins @angular/compiler-cli 11.0.3, ngast 0.6.2 and TypeScript 4.0.5, and support for later Angular releases is not documented. Deployed or minified bundles are not analyzed.

Source builds use Node.js and yarn (CI uses Node 12), Angular CLI 11 and Electron 11.1.0 packaged by electron-builder. The CI workflow runs a Spectron end-to-end test on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows that opens the app and parses a small Angular 11 fixture project; it does not check graph accuracy on real applications.

The README states MIT; LICENSE.md is the MIT text carried over from the angular-electron template, with its author's 2020 copyright line. Graphs show what ngast resolves from the sources, not runtime behaviour. Nothing was installed or run.

name: APKiD
description_en: PEiD-style identifier for Android packages from RedNaga. It scans APK and DEX files, nested ZIP entries and the native ELF libraries, PE DLLs and resources inside them with YARA rules, using the yara-python-dex DEX module, and reports the compilers, packers, protectors, obfuscators and anti-VM or anti-disassembly tricks it recognizes, per file or as JSON. Optional tracker rules attributed to the Exodus API flag embedded tracking SDKs; APKiD only identifies, and does not unpack or deobfuscate anything.
description_zh: RedNaga 推出的 Android 安装包识别工具，类似 PEiD。它借助 yara-python-dex 的 DEX 模块，用 YARA 规则扫描 APK、DEX 文件、嵌套的 ZIP 条目及其中的原生 ELF 库、PE 格式 DLL 和资源，报告识别出的编译器、加壳工具、保护工具、混淆工具以及反虚拟机或反反汇编手法，可按文件输出或输出 JSON。可选的追踪器规则注明来自 Exodus API，用于标出内嵌的追踪 SDK；APKiD 只做识别，不会脱壳或反混淆。
requirements: Latest release at review: 3.1.0, tagged and uploaded to PyPI on 2026-04-09; the reviewed master commit of 2026-10-07 adds later rules. pip install apkid pulls in yara-python-dex>=1.0.1. setup.py declares no python_requires and its classifiers name Python 3.6 and 3.7, while Travis CI uses 3.9 and the Dockerfile uses Python 3.11; on Windows the README pins Yara 3.11.0 and a separately built yara-python-dex wheel.

Provide APK, DEX or directory inputs you are entitled to examine. By default the CLI picks entries by file magic, searches nested ZIPs two levels deep, scans entries up to 100 MB and stops each YARA scan after 30 seconds; tracker rules are compiled separately and apply only with --scan-trackers. The README's usage block still shows v2.1.2 and omits --scan-trackers and --include-types.

Detection is signature-based, so unrecognized or modified packers and protectors go unreported; the README asks for unknown samples by file hash to write new rules. Tests compile and lint the rules and scan generated ZIP files; the repository has no sample corpus, and nothing was scanned in this review.

Dual-licensed: GPL-3.0, or a perpetual commercial license that allows distributing APKiD binaries and rules in commercial products but no source redistribution, which is why GitHub reports NOASSERTION. The reviewed sources establish no REA connection.

name: jsluice
description_en: Bishop Fox's Go library and command-line tool that parses JavaScript with tree-sitter to recover the endpoints a script calls, judging values by how the code uses them rather than by regular expressions alone. URL extraction follows location assignments, window.open, fetch, XMLHttpRequest and jQuery request calls, keeps the HTTP method, headers and query or body parameters, and stands in a placeholder for values only known at run time. Other modes flag credential-shaped values, print syntax trees, run tree-sitter queries and reformat minified code.
description_zh: Bishop Fox 推出的 Go 库与命令行工具，借助 tree-sitter 解析 JavaScript，还原脚本所调用的接口地址；它依据代码如何使用某个值来判断，而不仅仅依靠正则表达式。URL 提取会跟踪 location 赋值、window.open、fetch、XMLHttpRequest 和 jQuery 请求调用，保留 HTTP 方法、请求头以及查询或请求体参数，并以占位符代替只有运行时才能确定的值。其他模式可标记形似凭据的值、打印语法树、运行 tree-sitter 查询以及格式化压缩代码。
requirements: The project publishes no releases or tags: the README installs the CLI with go install and the package with go get. go.mod declares Go 1.18 and pins go-tree-sitter, goquery, jsbeautifier-go and a WARC reader. The reviewed main commit dates from 2024-01-10; the repository has Go unit tests and JavaScript fixtures but no CI workflow.

Inputs are JavaScript files, HTML pages whose inline scripts it extracts, WARC archives, raw source on stdin, or http(s) URLs fetched with optional cookies and headers; output is JSONL. The analysis is static: concatenated runtime values appear as EXPR or a chosen placeholder, and the README calls the approach not foolproof, so extracted endpoints are leads to check against the application.

secrets mode ships active matchers only for AWS, GCP and GitHub key formats and Firebase configuration objects, plus user-supplied JSON pattern files; the README shows that unanchored custom patterns match unintended values. Matches are pattern hits, not confirmed credentials, and this entry records no values found with the tool.
MIT, copyright 2023 Bishop Fox. Nothing was built or run.

name: LBA2 Remake: a Little Big Adventure 1 and 2 reimplementation in TypeScript and Three.js
